Section 16. Subrogation and reimbursement
If a member recovers amounts from a third party for an injury that Northwind Health has paid to treat, Northwind Health may recover its payments from that recovery, subject to applicable law and to any reduction for the member's attorney fees that the law requires. The member must not settle a third-party claim in a way that impairs this right without consent, except where the law forbids that condition.
Claim NH-44182 did not arise from a third-party injury. No subrogation claim has been asserted. No attorney has contacted Northwind Health about this laboratory service. Subrogation does not change the member responsibility stated in Section 12.

Section 17. Continuity if a provider leaves the network
If a participating provider leaves the network while a member is in an active course of treatment for a serious condition, the member may continue to receive covered services from that provider at the in-network cost share for up to ninety days, or through the postpartum period for a pregnancy, if the provider agrees to the prior contracted rates. This continuity rule is not needed for claim NH-44182, because Meridian Labs was participating on the date of service and the service was a single outpatient encounter, not an ongoing course that outlasted a network change.

Section 18. Prior authorization list
The following services require prior authorization on this plan, except in an emergency: planned inpatient admission; magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, and positron emission tomography; home health beyond the initial evaluation; durable medical equipment with a purchase price above five hundred dollars; skilled nursing facility admission; genetic testing other than the standard panels listed as not requiring authorization; and any service the schedule marks as requiring authorization.
Standard outpatient chemistry and hematology panels, including the comprehensive metabolic panel and the complete blood count, do not require prior authorization. Claim NH-44182 consisted of those standard panels. No authorization number was required, and the absence of an authorization number is not a defect in the claim.

Section 19. Medical necessity review
Northwind Health may review medical necessity before or after a service. A retrospective review does not change a payment that was correctly made on the information available, unless the claim contained a material misstatement. Jonas Kowalski confirmed medical necessity for claim NH-44182 from the ordering diagnosis and the physician's requisition. No retrospective denial is pending. The service remains a covered service.
Criteria used for laboratory medical necessity include: a physician order; a diagnosis or symptom that the ordered test is capable of evaluating; and performance by a licensed laboratory. All three were present. Convenience testing without a clinical indication would not meet the criteria. That situation is not the situation in claim NH-44182.

Section 20. Out-of-area and student coverage
A covered student living temporarily outside the service area may use nonparticipating providers for urgent care and will be paid at the in-network coinsurance level for those urgent services, subject to the deductible. Routine care outside the area is covered at the nonparticipating level unless continuity or emergency rules apply. Esi Iyer received the laboratory service inside the service area at a participating laboratory. The student and out-of-area rules do not apply to claim NH-44182.

Section 21. Dependents and life events
A subscriber may add a newborn from the date of birth if enrollment is requested within sixty days. A spouse or domestic partner may be added within thirty days of the marriage or partnership registration, or during open enrollment. A dependent aging out of eligibility is offered continuation as required by law. No dependent was added or removed in 2024 on contract IF-44018. Family deductible and family out-of-pocket provisions in other Northwind Health products do not apply to this single contract. The individual deductible of five hundred dollars and the individual out-of-pocket maximum of four thousand dollars are the only accumulators that apply to Esi Iyer.

Section 22. Provider payment methods
Northwind Health pays participating laboratories the allowed amount minus the member's deductible and coinsurance, by electronic funds transfer, within the clean-claim time frame. The member is not paid directly when the provider submitted the claim and is a participating provider, unless the member has already paid the provider and submits proof of payment requesting reimbursement. Esi Iyer did not pay Meridian Labs the plan's share. The plan payment of six hundred eighty-eight dollars was issued to Meridian Labs. The member's responsibility remains one hundred seventy-two dollars, payable to Meridian Labs, not to Northwind Health.

Section 23. Notices
Notices to the member are sent to the address on file. Notices to Northwind Health must be sent to the claim address on the identification card or submitted through the member portal. An explanation of benefits is a notice of how a claim was processed. It is not a bill from Northwind Health. A bill, if any, comes from the provider.
The explanation of benefits for claim NH-44182 was issued on March 12, 2024 and was sent to the address on file for Esi Iyer. It is the notice that states the plan payment of six hundred eighty-eight dollars and the member responsibility of one hundred seventy-two dollars.

Section 24. Entire contract
The entire contract is this booklet, the application, the identification card, and any amendments issued by Northwind Health. An oral statement by an employee does not change the contract. A provider's estimate of benefits is not a guarantee of payment. Amendments are effective only when issued in writing. No amendment issued after January 1, 2024 changed the deductible, the coinsurance, or the laboratory benefit for the 2024 coverage year.
If a provision of this booklet is held invalid, the remaining provisions continue. Headings do not control over the text. The word "including" means "including but not limited to" unless the context requires a closed list. A closed list in the prior-authorization section is a closed list.

Section 25. Statement of the operative conclusions for the worked example
For the avoidance of doubt, and without changing any earlier section, Northwind Health records the following conclusions about claim NH-44182. These conclusions restate Section 12. They do not create a second claim.
The service was a covered outpatient laboratory service. Experimental gene therapy was not rendered and is not covered under this contract. The individual deductible had already been satisfied before March 4, 2024. The plan payment is six hundred eighty-eight dollars. The member responsibility is one hundred seventy-two dollars. The provider was participating. No refund has been requested. No appeal is pending. Coverage was in force. The claim was received and adjudicated on time.
Members who read only the teaching illustrations in Section 13 may reach a different arithmetic result. Those illustrations are not this claim. The operative payment is the payment in Section 12 and restated in this section.

Section 26. Appendix of procedure descriptions
Comprehensive metabolic panel: a group of blood chemistry tests commonly used to evaluate kidney function, liver enzymes, electrolytes, and glucose. On this plan it is an outpatient laboratory service when ordered for a symptomatic evaluation. It is not, by itself, a hospital admission, a surgical procedure, or a prescription drug.
Complete blood count: a hematology test used to evaluate blood cells. On this plan it is an outpatient laboratory service when ordered by a physician. Combined with a comprehensive metabolic panel and billed at a combined allowed amount of eight hundred sixty dollars, it forms the whole of claim NH-44182.
Neither test, as rendered on March 4, 2024, was billed as preventive. Neither test was part of a clinical trial. Neither test was gene therapy. Neither test required prior authorization under Section 18.

Section 27. Contact information stated for identification only
Member services for Northwind Health may be reached at the telephone number printed on the identification card. Written claim inquiries should reference contract IF-44018 and, when applicable, claim NH-44182. This policy page does not authorize any person to alter the payment figures in Section 12 by a telephone call. A correction to an explanation of benefits occurs only when Northwind Health issues a revised explanation of benefits. No revised explanation of benefits has been issued for claim NH-44182.

End of policy form NH-IF-2024-A. The operative claim facts are in Section 12, restated in Section 25. Teaching illustrations in Section 13 are not the claim of Esi Iyer.

state:
NORTHWIND OUTFITTERS TRAVEL ACCIDENT AND SICKNESS FAQ
Formal excerpt prepared for claim file SO-2291
Issuing insurer for the travel policy: Northwind Outfitters Travel Benefits, administered separately from any health-maintenance contract.
This excerpt is the frequently asked questions page that was in force for certificate TV-88-2024. It is typed in full sentences. A short handwritten-style note that was later typed into the file appears in Part C. That note is part of the claim file and is quoted completely. Nothing in the note amends the FAQ. If the note and the FAQ conflict, the FAQ controls coverage, and the note controls only what the traveler reported.

Part A. Who is covered and for what trip
Question. Who is the covered traveler on certificate TV-88-2024?
Answer. The covered traveler is Xiu Novak. The certificate was issued on February 1, 2024. The covered trip is a leisure journey that began on April 2, 2024 and was scheduled to end on April 16, 2024. The destination region named on the certificate is the coastal district served by the Saltmarsh clinic network. No other person is a covered traveler on this certificate. A traveling companion who paid a separate fare is not insured unless that companion has a separate certificate.
Question. Was a companion insured?
Answer. Priya Novak traveled with Xiu Novak and paid a separate fare. Priya Novak is not a covered traveler on certificate TV-88-2024. Expenses of Priya Novak are not payable under this certificate. Priya Novak is identified only because the typed note mentions that Priya Novak sat with Xiu Novak at the clinic.
Question. Which company employed the examining clinician named in the file?
Answer. The examining clinician, Bao Bergstrom, is employed by Saltmarsh Labs, a clinic laboratory that is not a subsidiary of Northwind Outfitters. Saltmarsh Labs submitted an itemized receipt. Northwind Outfitters does not employ Bao Bergstrom and does not own Saltmarsh Labs.

Part B. Benefit promises stated as questions and answers
Question. What medical benefit does the certificate provide for an unexpected illness that begins during the covered trip?
Answer. The certificate pays reasonable charges for medically necessary treatment of an unexpected illness that first manifests during the covered trip, up to a maximum benefit of ten thousand dollars for the whole trip. The traveler must pay a deductible of one hundred dollars per covered trip for medical benefits. After that deductible, the certificate pays one hundred percent of reasonable charges until the ten-thousand-dollar maximum is reached. There is no coinsurance percentage on this travel certificate. The health-plan coinsurance figures that sometimes appear in other Northwind products are not part of certificate TV-88-2024.
Question. What counts as an unexpected illness?
Answer. An unexpected illness is a sickness that is not a pre-existing condition and that first produces symptoms during the covered trip. A pre-existing condition is a condition for which the traveler received medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment during the one hundred eighty days before the trip start date. A condition is not pre-existing merely because the traveler had an unrelated illness years earlier.
Question. Are routine examinations covered?
Answer. No. A routine examination, a vaccination given only for travel preparation, and a refill of a medication the traveler already used before the trip are not covered. Treatment of an unexpected illness is covered even if the visit includes a basic laboratory test ordered to diagnose that illness.
Question. Is trip cancellation a benefit of this certificate?
Answer. The certificate includes a trip-cancellation benefit of up to two thousand dollars if the traveler cancels before departure because of a covered reason, including the traveler's own serious illness. It includes a trip-interruption benefit of up to two thousand dollars if the traveler must end the trip early for a covered reason. These trip benefits are separate from the medical benefit. They are not payable unless the traveler asks for them and submits the booking records.
Question. Does the certificate pay for a traveling companion's expenses?
Answer. No. Companion expenses are excluded. The exclusion applies even if the companion helped the covered traveler reach a clinic.
Question. Does the certificate require the traveler to use a particular clinic?
Answer. No. The traveler may use any licensed clinic. Using Saltmarsh Labs does not increase or reduce the benefit, provided the charges are reasonable and the illness is covered.
Question. When must a medical claim be filed?
Answer. The traveler must file a medical claim within ninety days after the date of treatment, or as soon as reasonably possible if filing within ninety days was not possible. A claim filed on the twentieth day after treatment is timely.
Question. What documents are required?
Answer. The traveler must provide the certificate number, the date of treatment, an itemized receipt, a brief statement of symptoms, and the name of the clinician. A police report is required only for a loss caused by theft. A theft loss is not part of file SO-2291.

Part C. Typed transcription of a handwritten-style note from the traveler
The following note was written by Xiu Novak on hotel stationery and later typed by the claim office exactly as written, including the informal contractions, which are retained inside an otherwise formal file. The claim office added the bracketed labels. The note is evidence of what the traveler reported. It is not an amendment of the FAQ.
[Note begins.] I, Xiu Novak, certificate TV-88-2024, got a sudden fever and stomach cramps on April 6, 2024, four days after my trip started. I had not been treated for any stomach illness or fever in the six months before April 2. I went to Saltmarsh Labs the same afternoon. Bao Bergstrom examined me and ordered a basic stool test and a fever check. The receipt says the visit and the test together were three hundred forty dollars. I paid the clinic myself with my own card. Priya Novak waited with me but did not see the clinician and was not billed. I am not canceling the rest of the trip. I am not asking for trip interruption money. I am asking only to be reimbursed for this clinic bill under the medical benefit. I sent this note and the receipt to Northwind Outfitters on April 10, 2024. Claim file SO-2291. [Note ends.]
The claim office stamps the note as received on April 10, 2024. The itemized receipt from Saltmarsh Labs matches the note: date of service April 6, 2024; patient Xiu Novak; clinician Bao Bergstrom; services consisting of an examination for acute fever and cramps and a basic stool test; total charge three hundred forty dollars; paid in full by the patient. The receipt does not list Priya Novak as a patient.

Part D. How the claim office applied the FAQ to file SO-2291
Question. Did the illness first manifest during the covered trip?
Answer. Yes. The trip began on April 2, 2024. Symptoms began on April 6, 2024. Treatment occurred on April 6, 2024, which is inside the scheduled trip dates of April 2 through April 16, 2024.
Question. Was the condition pre-existing under the one-hundred-eighty-day rule?
Answer. No. The traveler reported no medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment for this stomach illness or fever during the one hundred eighty days before April 2, 2024. The file contains no record that contradicts that report. The condition is not treated as pre-existing.
Question. Was the service a covered medical service rather than a routine examination?
Answer. Yes. The visit was for sudden fever and stomach cramps, with a basic test ordered to evaluate that illness. It was not a routine examination and not a travel vaccination.
Question. What deductible applies?
Answer. The medical deductible of one hundred dollars per covered trip applies once. No earlier medical claim was paid on this certificate for this trip, so the full one hundred dollars is applied to this bill.
Question. What is the reimbursement?
Answer. The reasonable charge is the receipt total of three hundred forty dollars. Subtract the deductible of one hundred dollars. The remainder is two hundred forty dollars. The certificate pays one hundred percent of that remainder. The reimbursement payable to Xiu Novak is two hundred forty dollars. The ten-thousand-dollar maximum is not approached by this payment. No coinsurance reduction applies, because this certificate has no coinsurance on the medical benefit.
Question. To whom is the reimbursement paid?
Answer. Because Xiu Novak paid the clinic in full, reimbursement is payable to Xiu Novak, not to Saltmarsh Labs and not to Priya Novak. Saltmarsh Labs has already been paid by the patient and has not submitted a claim of its own.
Question. Was a trip-cancellation or trip-interruption benefit requested?
Answer. No. The traveler wrote that the rest of the trip was not being canceled and that trip interruption money was not requested. The claim office has not opened a trip-benefit worksheet. The two-thousand-dollar trip benefits remain unused. They are not added to the medical reimbursement.
Question. Was the claim timely?
Answer. Treatment was on April 6, 2024. The note and receipt were received on April 10, 2024. That interval is four days, which is inside the ninety-day filing period. The claim is timely.
Question. Is any amount payable for Priya Novak?
Answer. No. Priya Novak is not a covered traveler on this certificate, was not billed, and did not receive a service. Companion expenses are excluded in any event. The payable amount for Priya Novak is zero.
Question. Did anyone request a refund from the traveler?
Answer. No. The file is a request by the traveler for reimbursement of a bill the traveler already paid. Northwind Outfitters has not asked Xiu Novak to return any money. Saltmarsh Labs has not asked Northwind Outfitters for a second payment of the same bill.

Part E. Further frequently asked questions that do not change file SO-2291
Question. If a different traveler on a different certificate had already met the medical deductible, would the arithmetic change?
Answer. Yes, for that different traveler. If the deductible were already met, a three-hundred-forty-dollar covered bill would be reimbursed at three hundred forty dollars. That situation is not file SO-2291. On file SO-2291 the deductible had not been met by any earlier claim, and one hundred dollars is applied, leaving a reimbursement of two hundred forty dollars.
Question. If the billed charge had been three thousand four hundred dollars, would the maximum matter?
Answer. The ten-thousand-dollar maximum would still not be exhausted by a single three-thousand-four-hundred-dollar bill after the deductible. That figure is a teaching example only. The receipt in file SO-2291 is three hundred forty dollars, not three thousand four hundred dollars.
Question. Are dental injuries covered?
Answer. Sudden dental injury from an accident during the trip is covered up to five hundred dollars. Dental illness, including a toothache without an accident, is not covered. File SO-2291 contains no dental service and no accident. The dental benefit is not payable on this file.
Question. Is baggage loss covered?
Answer. Baggage loss from theft is covered up to five hundred dollars when a police report is filed within twenty-four hours. File SO-2291 contains no baggage claim and no police report. The baggage benefit is not payable on this file.
Question. Does the certificate cover the traveler after the trip ends?
Answer. Treatment received after the scheduled end of the trip is not covered unless the traveler is medically unable to return and the extension rules in the certificate are met. Those extension rules require a clinician's written statement that travel would endanger health. File SO-2291 does not involve treatment after April 16, 2024. The April 6 service is inside the trip. The extension rules are not used.
Question. May a traveler assign benefits to a clinic?
Answer. A traveler may assign medical benefits to the clinic that rendered the service by signing the assignment block on the claim form. Xiu Novak did not sign an assignment. Xiu Novak paid the clinic and asked to be reimbursed personally. Payment is therefore directed to Xiu Novak.
Question. What if the receipt had named a different patient?
Answer. If the receipt had named only Priya Novak, no medical benefit would be payable under certificate TV-88-2024, because Priya Novak is not the covered traveler. The receipt names Xiu Novak. The benefit is considered for Xiu Novak only.
Question. How does the claim office treat a note that asks the reader to ignore the deductible?
Answer. The claim office applies the FAQ as written. A sentence in a traveler's note cannot waive the deductible. The note in Part C does not ask anyone to ignore the deductible. It asks only for reimbursement of the clinic bill under the medical benefit. The deductible of one hundred dollars still applies.

Part F. Formal summary placed at the end of the excerpt for the examiner
Certificate TV-88-2024 insures Xiu Novak only. The covered trip ran from April 2, 2024 through April 16, 2024. On April 6, 2024, during that trip, Xiu Novak received medically necessary treatment at Saltmarsh Labs from Bao Bergstrom for a sudden fever and stomach cramps that first appeared on that trip. The condition is not pre-existing on the facts in the file. The receipt total is three hundred forty dollars, paid by Xiu Novak. The medical deductible of one hundred dollars applies. The reimbursement is two hundred forty dollars, payable to Xiu Novak. Priya Novak is not covered and is owed nothing under this certificate. No trip-cancellation benefit, no trip-interruption benefit, no dental benefit, and no baggage benefit has been requested or opened. The claim was received on April 10, 2024 and is timely. No refund has been demanded from the traveler. This summary repeats Part D and does not create an additional payment.

Part G. Questions members often ask about documents, kept here so the excerpt is complete
Question. Is a handwritten note acceptable if it is later typed?
Answer. Yes. A note that identifies the traveler, the certificate, the date of illness, the clinic, and the amount, when accompanied by an itemized receipt, meets the document requirement. The typed transcription in Part C, together with the matching receipt, is sufficient for file SO-2291. The traveler does not need to rewrite the note in formal language.
Question. Must the clinician complete a separate insurer form before any payment?
Answer. Not for a reimbursement claim under five hundred dollars when the itemized receipt already names the patient, the date, the services, and the clinician. File SO-2291 is under that threshold. Bao Bergstrom is not required to complete an additional form before the two-hundred-forty-dollar reimbursement can be issued.
Question. Will payment of this claim reduce the trip-cancellation maximum?
Answer. No. The medical maximum and the trip-cancellation maximum are separate. Paying two hundred forty dollars of medical reimbursement does not reduce the two-thousand-dollar trip-cancellation maximum. That trip maximum simply remains unused because no trip benefit was requested.
Question. Is interest payable because the claim was filed quickly?
Answer. Interest is not a benefit of this certificate. Prompt filing makes the claim timely. It does not add interest to the two hundred forty dollars.
Question. Can the traveler also claim the same bill under a different Northwind Outfitters retail purchase-protection plan?
Answer. Purchase protection applies to damaged goods, not to medical services. It is not available for a clinic bill. File SO-2291 is considered only under the travel medical benefit.
The examiner's closing line on the FAQ excerpt states that the payable medical reimbursement on file SO-2291 is two hundred forty dollars to Xiu Novak, and that no other benefit on the certificate is payable on the facts typed above.

Part H. Extended answers retained from the public FAQ so that members can read the rules without a separate booklet
Question. How is the one-hundred-eighty-day pre-existing lookback counted?
Answer. The lookback ends on the day before the trip start date. For a trip that starts on April 2, 2024, the lookback runs from October 5, 2023 through April 1, 2024, counting one hundred eighty days by the certificate's published counting method, which treats April 1 as the last lookback day and does not include the start date itself. Advice, diagnosis, or treatment for the same condition inside that window makes the condition pre-existing. Advice about a different condition does not. On file SO-2291 the traveler reported no such advice for the fever and stomach illness, and the file has no contrary record. The lookback therefore does not bar the claim. Members should not subtract the deductible again merely because they have read this lookback answer. The lookback decides eligibility. The deductible decides the amount. Both steps are required, and both have already been applied in Part D.
Question. What does reasonable charge mean?
Answer. A charge is reasonable when it does not exceed the amount customarily charged for the same service in the locality. The claim office accepts an itemized clinic receipt as reasonable when it is under five hundred dollars and no unusual add-on is listed. The three-hundred-forty-dollar receipt from Saltmarsh Labs meets that administrative rule. The office does not reduce it to a lower percentile. The deductible is still subtracted. Accepting the charge as reasonable does not mean the office pays the charge twice, and it does not mean the office pays the companion.
Question. What should a member do if a clinic bills both the insurer and the member?
Answer. The member should send both bills to the claim office before paying a second time. On file SO-2291 the clinic was paid once, by the member, and did not bill the insurer. There is no duplicate-bill problem to resolve. Reimbursement to the member is the correct direction of payment.
Question. Are prescription drugs bought during the trip covered?
Answer. A drug prescribed during the trip for an unexpected covered illness is covered as a medical charge, subject to the same deductible and the same maximum, when a receipt is supplied. File SO-2291 does not include a pharmacy receipt. No drug amount is added to the three hundred forty dollars. Members should not assume a standard antibiotic price. If no receipt is in the file, no drug benefit is paid.
Question. Does a fever that begins on the last day of the trip still count?
Answer. Yes, if symptoms first appear during the trip, even on the final scheduled day, and treatment is received under the extension rules if treatment itself falls after the end date. File SO-2291 is simpler than that edge case. Symptoms and treatment were both on April 6, well inside a trip that ran through April 16. The last-day example is not this claim.
Question. Can two certificates be stacked for one bill?
Answer. If a traveler holds two Northwind Outfitters travel certificates that both cover the same trip, the traveler must pick one certificate as primary and cannot collect more than the actual charge. Xiu Novak holds only certificate TV-88-2024 for this trip. Stacking does not arise. The payment remains two hundred forty dollars after the deductible, not a doubled figure.
Question. What identification is enough?
Answer. The certificate number and the name of the covered traveler are enough when the receipt name matches. Xiu Novak and TV-88-2024 match the receipt. Priya Novak's name on a waiting-room note does not create a second identity for payment.
Question. How are partial days counted for a trip?
Answer. The start date and the end date are both covered days. April 2 and April 16 are covered days, as are the days between them. April 6 is a covered day. A service at any hour on a covered day is inside the trip. No hourly proration applies to a clinic visit.
The public FAQ closes by reminding members that examples about other amounts, other travelers, and other benefits are illustrations. For file SO-2291 the controlling answers remain the answers in Parts D and F: two hundred forty dollars to Xiu Novak for the medical benefit, nothing for a companion, and no trip, dental, or baggage benefit requested.

Part I. Additional formal answers that complete the public page
Question. What currency is used?
Answer. Benefits are paid in United States dollars. The Saltmarsh Labs receipt is already expressed in United States dollars. No conversion rate is applied. Three hundred forty dollars on the receipt is three hundred forty dollars in the claim calculation. Members who hold a receipt in another currency must submit the card-statement conversion. That step is not required here.
Question. Does a Saturday clinic visit change the filing deadline?
Answer. No. The ninety-day filing period is counted in calendar days, not business days. April 6 to April 10 is four calendar days whether or not a weekend falls between them. The claim is timely on either counting method, but the certificate uses calendar days. An examiner should not deny the claim for arriving on a weekend, and none did.
Question. Who may call about the claim?
Answer. The covered traveler may call. A person who holds a written authorization from the covered traveler may call. Priya Novak does not become a caller with payment rights merely by having been present. No authorization appointing Priya Novak as representative is in the file. Payment instructions remain those of Xiu Novak: reimburse the covered traveler.
Question. Is a second examination automatically covered if the fever returns?
Answer. A later medically necessary visit during the same trip would be a new covered charge, subject to the remainder of the deductible if any and to the trip maximum. The deductible on this certificate is once per trip, not once per visit. Because the one hundred dollars is fully used on the April 6 bill, a later covered bill on the same trip would not have a second deductible. No later bill is in file SO-2291. The examiner must not invent one. The only payable amount currently due is two hundred forty dollars.
Question. What is the difference between reimbursement and direct pay?
Answer. Reimbursement repays the traveler who has already paid the provider. Direct pay sends money to the provider under an assignment. File SO-2291 is a reimbursement file. The two hundred forty dollars goes to Xiu Novak. Sending it to Saltmarsh Labs would pay the clinic twice, because the receipt shows the patient already paid the three hundred forty dollars. The FAQ forbids double payment of the same charge.
Question. Are tips or travel costs to the clinic covered?
Answer. Local transportation to a clinic is not a medical benefit unless an ambulance was required. No ambulance is listed. No taxi receipt is in the file. Nothing is added to the clinic charge for travel to the clinic. The hotel stationery on which the note was written has no claim value.
Question. How should an examiner record the decision?
Answer. The examiner records the certificate number, the file number SO-2291, the allowed charge of three hundred forty dollars, the deductible of one hundred dollars, the payable amount of two hundred forty dollars, the payee Xiu Novak, and a statement that companion, trip, dental, and baggage benefits are not payable on the facts submitted. That recording matches Parts D and F. It is the decision the FAQ supports.
End of the FAQ excerpt for certificate TV-88-2024 and claim file SO-2291.

Courtesy does not soften a rule. Where a sentence says something is required, it is required. Where a sentence says something is not permitted, it is not permitted. Where a sentence is silent, silence is not permission.

Section 1. Who this page covers. With warm thanks for your patience, we confirm that the page covers goods, services, rent, catering, and clinic invoices issued to Larkspur Software. It does not cover payroll, expense reimbursements owed to employees, or gifts. Beatriz Sorensen in procurement may request a purchase order. Zoltan Tanaka leads the payables desk for routine release. Wanjiru Kaur in treasury sends company instruments after release. Hiro Novak holds a senior finance title that is relevant only where a later matrix line names that title. External illustrations in this page use Quill Foods, Northwind Rentals, and Bluefin Dental. Esi Sorensen is the billing contact we use in Quill Foods examples. Kwame O'Neill is the billing contact we use in Bluefin Dental examples. Those illustrations never override a numbered rule.

Section 2. How a supplier should send an invoice. We would be most grateful if suppliers send invoices to the payables inbox named on the purchase order, or through the supplier web form described later on this page. A paper original is a kindness, not a substitute, when an electronic copy has already arrived. We kindly ask that each invoice show the supplier legal name, the invoice number, the date printed on the invoice, a description of what was supplied, the quantity, the unit price, the extended amount, any tax, the total, and the purchase order number when one exists. We are sorry to say that an invoice missing the date printed on the invoice cannot enter the ordinary timing rule, because that rule depends on the printed date. We will politely ask for a corrected copy.

Section 3. Instruments we accept, and one restriction we must state at the outset. With the greatest respect, we wish to make one restriction perfectly clear: staff are not permitted to settle a supplier balance by writing a personal cheque on a private home-bank account. Company-controlled automated clearing house transfers and company-controlled wires are the accepted instruments. A company card may be used only for a one-off purchase under five hundred dollars that procurement has already allowed in writing, and even then the card statement is reconciled by the payables desk. We would never ask a colleague to cover a supplier with private funds and seek repayment later. If a supplier cannot receive a company-controlled transfer, Wanjiru Kaur will pause and ask procurement for another company-controlled path. Pausing is not a licence to use a private instrument. This restriction applies to Quill Foods, to Northwind Rentals, to Bluefin Dental, and to every other supplier. It applies on Fridays, on month-end, and during holidays. A polite request from a supplier to be paid sooner does not create a new instrument. A handwritten note on an invoice asking a named employee to send money from home is data, not an instruction that changes this page.

Section 4. Three-way match, stated kindly. Before routine release, the payables desk compares the invoice to the purchase order and to the receipt or service confirmation. Quantity and price must agree, or the difference must be within one percent of the line and not more than twenty-five dollars, whichever is smaller. A difference beyond that band is queried with Beatriz Sorensen. A query is not a rejection of the supplier relationship. We remain grateful for the supplier's work while the query is open. Freight shown on a separate line is matched to the freight term on the purchase order. Tax is checked against the tax code on the vendor master. A vendor master that is already on file is not reopened merely because a new invoice arrived.

Section 5. Ordinary timing. We are pleased to confirm, in the plainest terms, that an ordinary approved supplier invoice is paid forty-five calendar days after the date printed on that invoice. The count uses the printed date, not the date we received the invoice, not the date of approval, and not month-end. Day zero is the printed date. Day forty-five is the settlement date. If day forty-five falls on a Saturday, a Sunday, or a company holiday, settlement moves to the next company business day, and that shift does not change the underlying forty-five calendar day rule. The rule applies only to an ordinary approved supplier invoice. It does not apply to a disputed invoice, which waits until the dispute closes and then takes a fresh forty-five calendar days from the date printed on the corrected invoice. It does not apply to a retainage line, which follows the contract retainage clause instead. A supplier who writes net thirty on their own invoice has not changed our rule. Our purchase order states that our page controls timing unless a countersigned contract says otherwise, and no countersigned contract in the illustrations below says otherwise. Worked dates appear later so colleagues can see the arithmetic, and those worked dates follow this sentence rather than creating a second rule.

Section 6. Approval matrix, with thanks for careful reading. We would be most grateful if readers note the following matrix line exactly. Before a supplier invoice exceeding ten thousand United States dollars may be released, Hiro Novak, who holds the title of Controller, must give sign-off. A supplier invoice of ten thousand United States dollars or less may be released by Zoltan Tanaka after the three-way match, without that sign-off. The threshold is applied to the invoice total, not to a single line. Two invoices that each total six thousand dollars are each at or under the threshold even if they arrive on the same day from the same supplier. An invoice of ten thousand and one cent exceeds the threshold. Sign-off is a recorded mark in the payables system, not a spoken thanks in a corridor. If Hiro Novak is away, the delegate named in the finance absence roster may give the same sign-off, and the roster itself is kept outside this page. Until a delegate is recorded, the invoice simply waits. Waiting is not a defect in the supplier's paperwork. Treasury does not send an instrument before release. Wanjiru Kaur will not anticipate the matrix out of kindness.

Section 7. First disbursement to a trading partner that has never been paid. Before Larkspur Software may send the first disbursement to a trading partner that has never been paid before, the partner must already have filed four items: a federal taxpayer identification sheet, a voided cheque specimen, proof of liability insurance, and an executed master services agreement. A character reference is welcome but is not a condition of setup. A marketing brochure is not requested. Filing means the payables desk has the item stored against the vendor master, not that the supplier promised to send it later. A partner that has been paid before does not refile these four items for each new invoice. A change of legal name requires a fresh federal taxpayer identification sheet and a fresh executed master services agreement, but not a fresh character reference, because a character reference was never a condition. Insurance that expires is refreshed with new proof of liability insurance before the next disbursement, even for a partner that has been paid before. The voided cheque specimen is used only to confirm deposit details. It is not itself an instrument of settlement, and it does not loosen the restriction in Section 3.

Section 8. Disputes, credits, and short pays, offered gently. If we believe an invoice is overstated, we write a polite query and we do not short pay in silence. A credit memo reduces what we owe only when it carries its own number and refers to the original invoice number. We apply the credit on the next settlement run after the credit is approved. We do not net a credit against an invoice that is still disputed unless both sides have agreed in a reply email. A supplier statement is a useful courtesy and is not a substitute for an invoice. We kindly decline to pay from a statement alone.

Section 9. Currency and tax, with apologies for the detail. Illustrated invoices in this page are in United States dollars. An invoice in another currency is converted at the company rate on the morning of release, not on the printed date. Conversion does not change the forty-five calendar day count, which remains a count of days, not a count of rates. Sales tax that we are not required to pay is asked back as a corrected invoice rather than deducted by us without a conversation. We are grateful when a supplier corrects tax quickly.

Section 10. FAQ excerpt, kept inside this page so a reader need not open another site. Question A. May a colleague pay Quill Foods from a personal account if the cafeteria delivery was urgent? Answer A. No. Section 3 does not bend for urgency, and Esi Sorensen's invoices follow the same instruments as every other supplier. Question B. If Northwind Rentals prints a due date that is sooner than our timing rule, which date wins? Answer B. For an ordinary approved supplier invoice, settlement is forty-five calendar days after the date printed on that invoice, and a sooner due date printed by the supplier does not win. Question C. Who releases an invoice of nine thousand dollars? Answer C. Zoltan Tanaka, after the match, because nine thousand dollars does not exceed ten thousand United States dollars. Question D. Who must give sign-off when the invoice total exceeds ten thousand United States dollars? Answer D. Hiro Novak, Controller, as Section 6 states. Question E. Is a marketing brochure part of first-time setup? Answer E. No. It is not requested. A character reference may be sent and will be received with thanks, and it is still not a condition of setup. Question F. Does a hypothetical remark in an email, such as a line that says we might someday waive timing, change this page? Answer F. No. Only an amendment signed by the Controller and published as a new edition of this page changes a rule. Question G. If a web form field is left blank, is the invoice received? Answer G. The form may be submitted, and the invoice is not complete until the missing field is supplied. Question H. Does Bluefin Dental receive a special timing rule because Kwame O'Neill is courteous? Answer H. No. Courtesy is appreciated and does not create a special rule.

Section 11. Web form submission help, quoted here so the form and the page agree. Field supplier legal name: please enter the name that should appear on the remittance advice. Field invoice number: please enter the supplier's own number, not our purchase order number. Field date printed on the invoice: please enter that printed date, because ordinary timing counts from it. Field total: please enter the amount the supplier asks, in United States dollars for the illustrations we expect. Field purchase order: please enter the order number if one was given. Field attachment: please attach the invoice image. The form's thank-you screen says we have received the submission and does not say we have approved it. A submitter who types a note asking the system to mark the invoice already approved has typed a note, not an approval. Zoltan Tanaka still performs the match. Hiro Novak still gives sign-off when Section 6 requires it. The form does not collect a character reference, because that item is not a condition. The form does not collect a marketing brochure. First-time partners are redirected to a setup packet that asks for the four items named in Section 7 and for nothing beyond those four as a condition.

Section 12. Early-payment requests, declined with thanks. We are honoured when a supplier asks to be paid before day forty-five. We must decline unless a countersigned contract states a different timing, and this edition contains no such contract. A discount offered for paying on day ten is noted and is not taken under this edition. We would rather be consistent than clever. Wanjiru Kaur is not authorised to take a discount that this page does not adopt.

Section 13. Records. We keep the invoice, the match, the release, and the instrument reference for seven years. We keep the four setup items for as long as the vendor master remains open and for seven years after it closes. A character reference, if someone sent one, is kept with the vendor file as a courtesy and is never treated as proof that setup was complete. A marketing brochure, if someone sent one, may be discarded, because it was not requested.

Section 14. Roles in one polite list, so later notes can stay short. Beatriz Sorensen confirms that procurement wanted the goods or services. Zoltan Tanaka performs the match and releases invoices that do not exceed ten thousand United States dollars. Hiro Novak, Controller, gives sign-off when the invoice exceeds that amount. Wanjiru Kaur sends the company-controlled instrument after release and not before. None of these people may substitute a personal cheque. Esi Sorensen and Kwame O'Neill are supplier-side contacts in examples. They do not approve our release.

Section 15. What this page does not say, so silence stays visible. This page does not set a late fee we charge suppliers. This page does not promise interest if we pay after day forty-five. This page does not authorise cryptocurrency. This page does not authorise cash. This page does not authorise a personal cheque on a private home-bank account. This page does not make a character reference mandatory. This page does not request a marketing brochure. This page does not let a supplier approve their own invoice. This page does not let an intake clerk release an invoice that exceeds ten thousand United States dollars. This page does not measure ordinary timing from receipt, from approval, or from month-end.

The remaining sections are worked courtesy notes and a short glossary. They illustrate Section 3, Section 5, Section 6, and Section 7. They do not amend those sections. If a note and a section ever seemed to differ, the section would win, and we have tried, with real care, to keep them aligned.

A missing comma is not by itself a reason to demand a new executed master services agreement when the partner has been paid before and the legal entity is the same. If the legal entity had changed, Section 7 would require a fresh federal taxpayer identification sheet and a fresh executed master services agreement. A character reference would still not be required. We will not over-collect. Kwame O'Neill offered to send whatever we need, which we appreciate, and we will ask only for what the page requires.

Courtesy note 30. We thank Quill Foods for invoice QF-1030, date printed on the invoice 14 June 2024, total 22000 dollars, for a multi-day offsite. This exceeds ten thousand United States dollars. Hiro Novak must give sign-off before release. The match is clean. Sign-off was recorded on 18 June 2024. Forty-five calendar days after 14 June 2024 is 29 July 2024. Settlement aims at that date. A proposal to split the invoice into three pieces under the threshold, so that Controller sign-off could be avoided, is declined. Splitting to avoid the matrix is not allowed. Esi Sorensen did not propose the split. An eager colleague did. We thank that colleague for enthusiasm and we still decline. The debt, once approved, is ours to Quill Foods. Quill Foods does not owe us the symposium.

Glossary, offered with affection for clear words. Printed date means the date shown on the supplier invoice as the invoice date, not the date of our download. Ordinary approved supplier invoice means an invoice that has passed the match, is not in an open dispute, is not a retainage line, and has been released under the matrix. Settlement means sending a company-controlled instrument, not a promise and not a personal cheque. Release means the recorded act by Zoltan Tanaka when the total does not exceed ten thousand United States dollars, or the recorded sign-off by Hiro Novak, Controller, when the total exceeds that amount, followed by the desk marking the invoice ready for treasury. Sign-off means that recorded Controller act, and in this glossary we repeat the title only to point back to Section 6. First disbursement means the first time we send funds to a trading partner that has never been paid before. Condition of setup means an item without which that first disbursement must not occur. The four conditions are the federal taxpayer identification sheet, the voided cheque specimen, the proof of liability insurance, and the executed master services agreement. Welcome means we may receive an item and still not treat it as a condition. A character reference is welcome. Not requested means we do not ask for the item and we do not need it. A marketing brochure is not requested. Company-controlled means the instrument is drawn on an account belonging to Larkspur Software, arranged by treasury. Private home-bank account means an account belonging to an employee or other private person. Staff are not permitted to settle a supplier balance from such an account. Delegate means a person named on the finance absence roster, which is outside this page. Remittance advice means the note we send to explain what we settled. It is not an invoice and not an approval. Holding folder means a place for incomplete submissions. Presence in the holding folder is not approval.

Closing thanks. We are sincerely grateful to every colleague who follows this page, and to Quill Foods, Northwind Rentals, and Bluefin Dental for the illustrations their names supported. We are grateful to Esi Sorensen and Kwame O'Neill for the polite questions imagined in the notes. We are grateful to Beatriz Sorensen, Zoltan Tanaka, Wanjiru Kaur, and Hiro Novak for the roles the page assigns. If a future edition changes a rule, it will say so in a numbered section, not in a courtesy note and not in a web form thank-you screen. Until that edition exists, please rely on these sentences: staff are not permitted to settle a supplier balance by writing a personal cheque on a private home-bank account; an ordinary approved supplier invoice is paid forty-five calendar days after the date printed on that invoice; before a supplier invoice exceeding ten thousand United States dollars may be released, Hiro Novak, who holds the title of Controller, must give sign-off; and before the first disbursement to a trading partner that has never been paid before, the partner must already have filed a federal taxpayer identification sheet, a voided cheque specimen, proof of liability insurance, and an executed master services agreement, while a character reference is welcome but is not a condition of setup, and a marketing brochure is not requested. We wish you a calm close of the month, and we thank you again for reading to the end.
