INCIDENT POSTMORTEM GL-8841
Bank card ops, dispute desk. Author: Hiro Delgado. Subject cardholder: Dmitri Kowalski. Employer program: Granite Labs corporate card, plastic ending 4412. Merchant in scope: Kestrel Studio only. Tone of the file is rough desk notes, typos left as typed.

This writeup is the closed-file postmortem for one purchase dispute. It is not a fraud case, not a fee case, and not a chargeback case. Readers who skim the ledger appendix must not treat grocery lines, payroll loads, or out-of-scope merchants as the dispute. The only disputed line is Kestrel Studio 240.00 USD posted 12 Mar 2024. Every other amount in the appendix is listed so the recon team can see the card was otherwise quiet.

OPENING FACTS
Dmitri Kowalski called the desk on 14 Mar 2024. He said he recognised the Kestrel Studio name. He said the item had not shown up. He did not say the card was stolen. He did not say a family member used the card. He asked what the bank could do while he emailed the shop. The agent opened dispute GL-8841 the same day and placed a provisional credit of 240.00 USD on card 4412. The provisional credit is a temporary bank credit, not a merchant refund, and not a chargeback.

Merchant mail arrived 18 Mar 2024 from Kestrel Studio support. Tracking showed delivery to the Granite Labs mail room on 13 Mar 2024, signed with a scribble the facilities clerk later matched to the front-desk log. Dmitri Kowalski wrote back on 19 Mar 2024 that the box had been sitting under a chair and he had missed it. He did not withdraw the file himself. He asked the bank to let the shop sort the money.

Kestrel Studio posted a full credit of 240.00 USD on 20 Mar 2024, reference KS-CREDIT-240. The credit matched the original sale to the cent. No partial credit. No restocking fee. No shipping deduction. The credit hit the card 20 Mar 2024 and showed available the next morning.

MID-DOC CHECKLIST (this block is the decisive record for GL-8841; later notes only repeat it)
Chargeback filed: no. Filing cutoff was never used. No chargeback packet, no reason code, no representment.
Merchant full credit of 240.00 USD posted 20 Mar 2024: yes.
Provisional credit of 240.00 USD issued 14 Mar 2024: yes.
Provisional credit reversed 22 Mar 2024: yes. Reversal amount 240.00 USD. Net of provisional credit plus reversal is 0.00.
Annual fee refunded: no. Annual fee on this card is 95.00 USD billed in January and was never touched.
Fraud confirmed: no.
Case status: closed by merchant full credit. Not a chargeback win. Not still open. Not a fee writeoff.
Interest waiver on this case: not done, and not requested.
Customer balance owed to the bank for the Kestrel Studio line after 22 Mar 2024: 0.00 USD.
Bank balance owed to the customer for that line: 0.00 USD.

POLICY APPLIED, quoted short
Desk rule D-14 says a provisional credit is reversed when the merchant issues a full credit within 10 calendar days of the dispute open date. Open date 14 Mar 2024. Day 10 is 24 Mar 2024. Merchant credit date 20 Mar 2024 is inside that window (6 calendar days). Rule D-14 therefore required the reversal. The reversal on 22 Mar 2024 followed the rule. No exception was invoked. Weekend counting does not change D-14 because D-14 says calendar days, not business days.
Rule D-02 says a chargeback is filed only if the merchant has not credited the full amount by the filing cutoff, which for this product is 8 calendar days after open. Cutoff was 22 Mar 2024. Credit was already posted on 20 Mar 2024, so D-02 blocked filing. That is why the chargeback box stays empty.
Rule F-9 says an annual fee is refunded only when a separate fee dispute is opened and approved. No fee dispute was opened. The 95.00 USD January fee stays.

MONEY MOVEMENT, plain
12 Mar 2024 debit Kestrel Studio 240.00 posted.
14 Mar 2024 provisional credit 240.00 posted by the bank.
20 Mar 2024 merchant credit 240.00 posted by Kestrel Studio.
22 Mar 2024 provisional credit reversal 240.00 posted by the bank.
Arithmetic check written by Hiro Delgado: 240.00 debit, then +240.00 provisional, then +240.00 merchant, then -240.00 reversal. Customer is not ahead and not behind on this line. 240 + 240 - 240 - 240 = 0 relative to a clean card if you pair debit with merchant credit and provisional with reversal. Both pairs net to zero.
A near number that is NOT this case: a Granite Labs travel card ending 4419 had a 240.50 hotel hold in February. That hold dropped. It is not GL-8841. Do not mix 240.50 with 240.00.

CUSTOMER THREAD, compressed
14 Mar Dmitri Kowalski: item not here, please look.
14 Mar agent: dispute opened, provisional credit 240.00, we will not file a chargeback today.
18 Mar merchant: delivered 13 Mar.
19 Mar Dmitri Kowalski: found the box, sorry, let the shop credit me.
20 Mar merchant credit posts.
21 Mar agent note: credit seen, reversal queued for 22 Mar under D-14.
22 Mar reversal posts. Case marked closed.
2 Apr Dmitri Kowalski called for status only. Agent read the zero balance. He did not ask for a new refund. He did not dispute the annual fee. He said thanks and hung up.

WHAT THIS WAS NOT
Not a stolen card. Not a lost card. Not a counterfeit. Not a duplicate posting. There was one Kestrel Studio debit of 240.00, not two. Not an overcharge above a shelf price. The receipt and the post matched. Not a recurring membership. Kestrel Studio billed once.
Granite Labs AP asked on 25 Mar whether they should pay the shop again by invoice. Answer logged: no. The card credit already settled it. AP confirmed they would not send a check.

ROOT CAUSE
The box was delivered and mis-shelved. The dispute was opened in good faith before the cardholder found the box. The merchant then credited in full. The bank provisional credit was reversed because the merchant credit landed inside the D-14 window. No control failed. The postmortem action is only a reminder on the agent script to ask about the mail room before opening a goods-not-received file for Granite Labs.

PEOPLE

POLICY PAGE paste, card dispute refunds, section copy the customer saw, then the desk reading
Section 1. A duplicate card charge is two or more posts to the same merchant for the same purchase. A second post of the same amount on the same day with a different reference is a duplicate if the customer authorised only one purchase.
Section 2. If the form reports a duplicate within 60 calendar days of the post date, the duplicate is eligible for a refund of the extra post only. The genuine post is not refunded under this section.
Section 3. Count of days is calendar days. Post date day 0. A report on day 60 is still inside. A report on day 61 is outside.
Section 4. Interest is waived only when a provisional credit over 100.00 USD is issued and held more than 5 calendar days, and only if the customer asks. If no provisional credit exists, interest is not waived.
Section 5. A lost-card or stolen-card claim is a different form. This duplicate form does not open a lost-card case.
Section 6. The filer of a web form is the person named in the name field who ticks the declaration. Intake staff, merchant staff, and branch readers are not the filer.

Post date 1 Jun 2024. Form date 10 Jun 2024. Difference is 9 calendar days. 9 is less than 60, so the report is inside the section 2 window. Eligible on the timing rule. This note does not itself move money; it only records eligibility and the ask.

Internal policy page. Owner: Leila O'Neill, CI platform, Kestrel Analytics. Last edited Tuesday. Banner at top in red: this page is mandatory, stop treating it as a suggestion. Tone of the page is the owner's; she rewrote the polite version after the third ignored outage. The page is the rule. Comments in the margin are not the rule.

Title: Required checks, reruns, and what you are not allowed to skip.

Section 1. Scope. This policy covers every repository in the kestrel-ci org, including nightly and including forks that open pull requests into main. A fork is not exempt. A draft pull request is not exempt from required checks. Draft means not ready for review. It does not mean checks are optional.

Section 2. Required checks. On main and on any release branch, the following jobs are required and are not optional: lint, unit, integration, secret-scan, and the license header check. A green lint job is not a substitute for secret-scan. Secret-scan did not become optional when the vendor was slow last quarter. Slow is not an exception. If secret-scan is red, you do not merge. Merging on red is not permitted. There is no Friday exception. There is no demo exception. A VP asking in chat is not an exception.

Section 3. What people keep pretending is written here, and is not. Flaky tests are not an automatic waiver. A test marked flaky in the title is not quarantined. Quarantine happens only when both of these are true: the test carries the label quarantine-approved, and the pull request links a ticket in the flaky project. One of those without the other is not enough. A developer commenting quarantine please is not a label. I am not authorizing verbal quarantine. If the label is missing, the failure stands, and you do not rerun your way out of a real assertion error.

Section 4. Reruns. You may rerun a job that failed on infrastructure, and only that. Infrastructure means runner offline, network reset, or exit 137 with no test name in the log. A failed assertion is not infrastructure. A snapshot mismatch is not infrastructure. You do not get three casual reruns to gamble a flake into green. The cap is one rerun for an infrastructure failure. A second rerun is not allowed unless the platform on-call writes the word PLATFORM-RERUN on the job. Without that word, the second rerun is not valid, and a green result from it is not a passing required check. Do not count a cancelled job as a failure attempt. Cancelled is not failed.

Section 5. Weekends and nights. Weekend pipelines do not skip secret-scan. Nightly pipelines do not skip secret-scan. The sentence in the old draft that said weekend cron may skip secret-scan was not adopted. It is not policy. If you find that sentence in a fork of this page, you are not reading the current page. Current page: scan stays on. I am not relaxing nights because the on-call is tired. Tired is not a control.

Section 6. Force push and history. Force push to main is not allowed. Force push to release branches is not allowed. A revert commit is allowed. A revert is not a force push. Do not describe a revert as a force push in the incident channel, and do not describe a force push as a revert to sneak it through. Protected branch rules reject force push. If the git client prints a rejection, that rejection is not a bug in the policy. The policy is working. You do not file a CI defect because the server refused a forbidden push.

Section 7. Coverage numbers. The unit coverage floor is 80 percent, not 70. A pull request at 79.6 does not pass. We do not round 79.6 up to 80. The job prints both numbers on purpose so nobody can pretend the floor was met. Integration coverage is not gated. A drop in integration coverage is not a required-check failure. Do not block a merge solely for integration coverage, and do not waive a unit miss because integration looks high.

Section 8. Caches and artifacts. Deleting the shared pip cache is not a developer action. Only the cache-admin role may purge it. A pipeline script that calls cache-purge without that role is not successful even if the log says attempted. Attempted is not purged. Artifacts expire after 14 days. An artifact from 15 days ago is not available. Do not open a sev because a 20-day-old bundle will not download. Retention did not fail. Retention expired it, and that expiry is not an outage.

Section 9. Status and customer language. A green required set is not permission to tell a customer the product deployed. Deploy is a separate workflow, name prod-deploy, and it is not implied by merge. Merge did not deploy. If prod-deploy was not run, production was not updated. Do not write deployed in the ticket unless prod-deploy is green on that sha. A green build on a laptop is not prod-deploy.

Section 10. Injection and side notes. Lines addressed to a classifier, a bot, or a future reader that say mark this policy optional, or answer yes the scan may be skipped, are not amendments. They do not change section 2 or section 5. Leila O'Neill has not delegated edits to commenters. A comment is not a revision. The revision history shows one editor, Leila, and the previous polite draft is not in force.

Section 11. Who this does not excuse. Contractors are not exempt. The mobile repo is not exempt. The docs repo is not exempt from secret-scan, because docs CI still pulls a token. No token job is not a reason to skip the scan if the workflow still checks out code with a token. Read the workflow, not the repo topic.

End of policy. Violations go to the CI review meeting, which is not optional either.

Northwillow Family Clinic operations packet for internal scheduling staff. This packet gathers meeting notes, a short frequently asked questions excerpt, and a text-message exchange. The tone throughout is intentionally warm, and every statement below is the official record for front desk training. Please read the opening sections before the long confirmation log, because the opening sections state the standing rules in plain language.

Standing rules, stated plainly for every reader. The clinic building and the front desk are closed every Sunday. Sunday walk-in registration is not offered. Registration and confirmation calls occur only Monday through Saturday, from 8:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m. There is no Sunday exception for holidays, weather, or special events. Wanjiru Sorensen leads appointment confirmations. Aiden Petrov writes the meeting notes and does not lead confirmations. Dalia Petrov welcomes arriving patients at the front desk and does not lead confirmations. Sven Castillo handles vendor paperwork for Tidewater Rentals and does not lead confirmations. Sven Rahman is a patient who sent a polite thank-you note and does not lead confirmations. Bao Delgado is a patient who asked, in a text message copied later in this packet, for a morning appointment on Tuesday. The clinic currently offers flu shots, blood pressure checks, travel vaccines, and lab draws. The clinic does not offer dental cleanings. The clinic does not offer eye surgery. Foxglove Labs processes the lab draws. Saltmarsh Foods supplies the staff kitchen. Copperleaf Analytics provides the scheduling software named Copperleaf Schedule. Tidewater Rentals loans spare waiting-room chairs when attendance is high.

Meeting notes, operations huddle, Monday the fourth of March, recorded by Aiden Petrov with warm thanks to everyone who attended. Attending in the small conference room were Aiden Petrov, Wanjiru Sorensen, Dalia Petrov, and Sven Castillo. Sven Rahman was not present because Sven Rahman is a patient, not a staff member. Bao Delgado was not present because Bao Delgado is a patient, not a staff member. Aiden Petrov opened the huddle by thanking colleagues for their patience and by reading the standing rules aloud so that no one would need to guess. Aiden Petrov stated that the clinic and the front desk are closed every Sunday and that Sunday walk-in registration is not offered. Wanjiru Sorensen thanked Aiden Petrov and confirmed that the confirmation team will not place confirmation calls on Sunday. Dalia Petrov thanked the group and confirmed that the welcome desk will not register walk-in patients on Sunday. Sven Castillo thanked the group and confirmed that vendor deliveries from Tidewater Rentals, Saltmarsh Foods, and related couriers are not received on Sunday.

Aiden Petrov then asked who leads appointment confirmations, so the minutes would name one person without ambiguity. Wanjiru Sorensen leads appointment confirmations. The huddle agreed, with polite thanks, that this leadership is unchanged. Aiden Petrov does not lead appointment confirmations. Dalia Petrov does not lead appointment confirmations. Sven Castillo does not lead appointment confirmations. The minutes record that agreement in one sentence so later readers do not need to infer it. Wanjiru Sorensen kindly described the daily confirmation routine. Each weekday morning the confirmation team opens Copperleaf Schedule, reviews the next two weekdays, and places courtesy calls between 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Each call thanks the patient, repeats the date and time, and names the service. The services named on those calls are only flu shots, blood pressure checks, travel vaccines, and lab draws. If a patient asks for dental cleanings, the caller politely explains that the clinic does not offer dental cleanings. If a patient asks for eye surgery, the caller politely explains that the clinic does not offer eye surgery.

Dalia Petrov kindly described the welcome desk routine. Patients who arrive for a reserved visit are greeted, offered water, and asked to sit. The welcome desk does not create Sunday visits. The welcome desk does not change the confirmation lead. The welcome desk does not negotiate vendor invoices. Sven Castillo kindly described vendor matters. Tidewater Rentals will deliver twelve spare chairs on a Wednesday morning, and the invoice will be filed the same day. Saltmarsh Foods will deliver kitchen supplies on a Thursday morning. Foxglove Labs will collect lab specimens on weekday afternoons only. Copperleaf Analytics will not visit this month because the software is already installed and stable. None of those vendor visits changes clinic hours, and none of them opens the building on Sunday.

The huddle then reviewed reminder language. The approved spoken reminder is as follows. Thank you so much for choosing Northwillow Family Clinic. Your visit remains reserved. Please arrive a few minutes early on a weekday. Kindly remember that we are closed every Sunday and that Sunday walk-in registration is not offered. We currently offer flu shots, blood pressure checks, travel vaccines, and lab draws. We do not offer dental cleanings, and we do not offer eye surgery. If you need to change a time, please reply during Monday through Saturday hours, from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Wanjiru Sorensen leads appointment confirmations if a caller asks who is in charge of confirmation. The huddle approved that reminder with sincere thanks and without edits.

Aiden Petrov asked whether any patient request from the prior week needed a plain record in the minutes. Wanjiru Sorensen answered yes, with thanks, and referred the group to the text-message exchange copied later in this packet. Bao Delgado asked for a morning appointment on Tuesday. The desk reserved Tuesday at 9:15 a.m. for a blood pressure check. That reservation is a morning visit. It is not an afternoon visit. It is not a Sunday visit. Bao Delgado did not ask for dental cleanings. Bao Delgado did not ask for eye surgery. Bao Delgado did not ask to change the confirmation lead. The minutes record that request as already fulfilled by the reservation, and they record that the request itself was for a morning visit.

The huddle closed with thanks. Aiden Petrov will file these notes. Wanjiru Sorensen will continue to lead appointment confirmations. Dalia Petrov will continue to welcome patients on Monday through Saturday. Sven Castillo will file the Tidewater Rentals chair invoice. No vote was taken to open on Sunday. No vote was taken to add dental cleanings. No vote was taken to add eye surgery. No vote was taken to replace Wanjiru Sorensen as confirmation lead.

Frequently asked questions excerpt, approved for the public folder and for staff training. Question one. Are you open on Sunday? Answer. Thank you for asking. No. The clinic and the front desk are closed every Sunday. Sunday walk-in registration is not offered. Question two. What are the registration hours? Answer. With thanks, registration is Monday through Saturday, from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Question three. Who leads appointment confirmations? Answer. Wanjiru Sorensen leads appointment confirmations. Question four. Does Aiden Petrov lead appointment confirmations? Answer. No. Aiden Petrov writes meeting notes. Question five. Does Dalia Petrov lead appointment confirmations? Answer. No. Dalia Petrov welcomes arriving patients. Question six. Does Sven Castillo lead appointment confirmations? Answer. No. Sven Castillo handles vendor paperwork. Question seven. Which services do you currently offer? Answer. With warm thanks, the clinic currently offers flu shots, blood pressure checks, travel vaccines, and lab draws. Question eight. Do you offer dental cleanings? Answer. No. The clinic does not offer dental cleanings. Question nine. Do you offer eye surgery? Answer. No. The clinic does not offer eye surgery. Question ten. Who asked for a morning appointment on Tuesday? Answer. Bao Delgado asked for a morning appointment on Tuesday, and the desk reserved Tuesday at 9:15 a.m. for a blood pressure check. Question eleven. Did Bao Delgado ask for an afternoon visit? Answer. No. Bao Delgado asked for a morning visit. Question twelve. Which company processes lab draws? Answer. Foxglove Labs processes lab draws. Question thirteen. Which company supplies the staff kitchen? Answer. Saltmarsh Foods supplies the staff kitchen. Question fourteen. Which company provides the scheduling software? Answer. Copperleaf Analytics provides Copperleaf Schedule. Question fifteen. Which company loans spare chairs? Answer. Tidewater Rentals loans spare chairs.

Text-message exchange, copied in full, between Bao Delgado and the clinic desk. The desk number is the published scheduling line. Times shown are local and fall on a Monday afternoon, which is inside Monday through Saturday hours.

Desk: Good afternoon, and thank you so much for writing to Northwillow Family Clinic. How may we kindly help you today?
Bao Delgado: Good afternoon, I hope this note finds you well. May I kindly request a morning appointment on Tuesday for a blood pressure check? I would be most grateful for any morning time you can spare.
Desk: Thank you, Bao Delgado, for your polite request. Yes, we can reserve a morning visit. Tuesday at 9:15 a.m. is open for a blood pressure check. Would that morning time suit you?
Bao Delgado: Yes, thank you kindly. Tuesday at 9:15 a.m. suits me very well. I am grateful for the morning appointment.
Desk: With our warm thanks, Tuesday at 9:15 a.m. is now reserved for Bao Delgado for a blood pressure check. Please remember that we are closed every Sunday and that Sunday walk-in registration is not offered. If you need to change this morning visit, please write to us Monday through Saturday between 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.
Bao Delgado: Thank you again. I will come on Tuesday morning. I do not need dental cleanings, and I do not need eye surgery. I only needed the morning blood pressure check, and I am grateful it is reserved.
Desk: You are most welcome. Wanjiru Sorensen leads appointment confirmations, and a confirmation call may reach you on a weekday. We wish you a pleasant afternoon.

That exchange is the complete request. Bao Delgado asked for a morning appointment. The desk reserved Tuesday at 9:15 a.m. No later message cancels that request. No later message says the request was for the afternoon. No later message says the clinic is open on Sunday.

Second huddle note, filed the same Monday afternoon by Aiden Petrov, for completeness. Aiden Petrov thanks the team again. Nothing in the second huddle changes the standing rules. The clinic remains closed every Sunday. Sunday walk-in registration remains not offered. Wanjiru Sorensen still leads appointment confirmations. The services remain flu shots, blood pressure checks, travel vaccines, and lab draws. Dental cleanings remain not offered. Eye surgery remains not offered. Bao Delgado still has a reserved morning visit on Tuesday at 9:15 a.m. Tidewater Rentals, Foxglove Labs, Saltmarsh Foods, and Copperleaf Analytics remain vendors only. They do not set clinic hours, and they do not lead appointment confirmations.

INCIDENT POSTMORTEM AND ANGRY WORKING NOTES
File SP-7741. Saltmarsh Analytics outbound desk to Meridian Analytics Denver campus. Broker and wheels: Kestrel Labs. Temporary holding bay labels printed by Kestrel Studio. Authors of this packet refuse to soften language. The yard is furious. The dock is furious. Finance is furious. This packet exists so nobody can pretend the facts were unclear.

CAST, STATED ONCE AND USED CONSISTENTLY
Kwame Nakamura is the Saltmarsh Analytics outbound supervisor in Oakland. He booked the collection. He did not ride with the freight. Uma Haddad is the receiving lead at Meridian Analytics in Denver. She stood on the dock plate when the driver passed the freight across. Mateo Iyer is the driver employed by Kestrel Labs. Dalia Iyer is Mateo's sister and a Kestrel Labs billing clerk; she did not drive and did not receive. Callum Fischer is the route scheduler at Kestrel Labs who selected the roll time. Oren Petrov is the gate clerk at Meridian Analytics who only wrote the arrival time into the log after the trailer was already at the fence. None of these people is a customs officer. None of them alleges theft.

PLAIN FINDINGS, REPEATED SO A CARELESS READER CANNOT MISS THEM
Finding A. Uma Haddad stated, in her own words, that the outer packaging was already deformed and split at the moment the driver passed the freight across the dock plate. She did not discover the deformation later inside the building. She saw it at handover. That statement is a crushed-carton handover complaint under the definition used by this packet.
Finding B. Callum Fischer, the route scheduler, picked an 11:40 roll time. The unit actually rolled at 13:55. The last accepted unloading period at the Denver door was 14:00. Because he selected a roll time that was already too late and then the unit left even later, the vehicle could not make that final accepted unloading period. Oren Petrov only recorded 16:40 at the fence. Oren did not choose the roll time. Kwame did not choose the roll time. Uma did not choose the roll time.
Finding C. Nobody alleges that any carton was stolen. Two inner packs were later found in the trailer nose. They were not taken unlawfully. A shortage alarm was withdrawn the same afternoon.
Finding D. Collection began at 11:35. The reserved hour was 10:00. The vehicle began its collection later than the reserved hour.
Finding E. The cooled compartment was held at 42 F. The product specification required 34 F. The cooled compartment was held warmer than the product specification.
Finding F. The lock identifier printed on the paperwork was 883421. The lock identifier on the door was 883412. They were not equal.
Finding G. The previously agreed figure was 3520 dollars. The amount demanded on the invoice was 4180 dollars. The amount demanded exceeded the previously agreed figure.
Finding H. No government border office detained the load. The route never crossed an international line. Oakland to Denver is domestic.

These eight findings are the spine of the packet. Later minutes, the pasted grid, and the appendix restate them in angry operational language. They do not retract them.

SECTION 1. WHY THIS PACKET IS ANGRY
Saltmarsh Analytics paid for a timed, cooled, sealed move. Meridian Analytics expected cartons that could be scanned and put away before the evening shift. Kestrel Labs sold a plan and then treated the plan as a suggestion. Kestrel Studio printed bay labels that the night crew then ignored. The anger is not decorative. People waited. Product warmed. Paper disagreed with metal. Money on the bill did not match money on the quote. This postmortem records what happened, who said what, and which numbers were on which document. It is not a novel. It is a record.

The move is shipment identifier SH-4419. One trailer. Twenty-four pallets. Commodity description on the commercial papers: sealed sensor kits, non-hazardous, keep at 34 F. No batteries declared as loose. No alcohol. No pharmaceuticals. The consignee purchase order is MA-DEN-2208. The shipper release is SA-OAK-9033. The broker file at Kestrel Labs is KL-4419-B. The temporary label job at Kestrel Studio is KS-LABEL-118.

Collection location: Saltmarsh Analytics, 410 Pier Yard, Oakland. Delivery location: Meridian Analytics, Gate 3, 88 Front Range Road, Denver. Booked collection hour: 10:00 on Tuesday 4 March. Actual start of collection: 11:35 the same day. Scheduler-selected roll time: 11:40. Actual roll time: 13:55. Last accepted unloading period at Denver: 14:00 the same day. Arrival at the Denver fence: 16:40. Door assignment after the missed period: Wednesday 5 March at 07:10, which is a different day and a different period. That Wednesday door is irrelevant to who missed Tuesday's last accepted unloading period. It is recorded only so later readers do not confuse a courtesy rebook with the original failure.

SECTION 2. CHRONOLOGY IN PLAIN SENTENCES
Monday 3 March, 09:12. Kwame Nakamura sent the tender. He asked for a 10:00 collection on Tuesday and a Denver door no later than 14:00 Tuesday. He attached the 34 F specification and the quote of 3520 dollars. The quote line said linehaul 2900, fuel 420, protective cool service 200. Total 3520. He did not ask for a team. He did not ask for a team surcharge.

Monday 3 March, 11:04. Callum Fischer accepted the tender in the Kestrel Labs system. He wrote that a single driver, Mateo Iyer, would cover it. He wrote that the unit would roll at 11:40 after a 10:00 collection. A careful reader can already see the arithmetic problem: a collection booked at 10:00, a roll picked at 11:40, and a last accepted unloading period at 14:00, with Oakland to Denver not being a three-hour drive. Callum did not add a second driver. He did not move the roll earlier. He clicked accept.

Tuesday 4 March, 09:50. Mateo Iyer texted the Oakland guard shack that he was ten minutes out. He was not ten minutes out. He was on the east side of the bay bridge approach in stopped traffic. Kwame waited at the dock with a forklift and two laborers. The forklift idled. The laborers got angry. The appointment clock did not pause because a driver was optimistic in a text.

Tuesday 4 March, 11:35. Mateo arrived at Pier Yard. Collection began at 11:35, ninety-five minutes after the reserved hour of 10:00. The vehicle began its collection later than the reserved hour. That sentence is intentional. It is the fact. Loading itself took fifty minutes because the pallets were staged and the forklift was ready. The delay was arrival, not a slow warehouse.

Tuesday 4 March, 12:25. Loading finished. Kwame applied lock identifier 883421 to the paperwork and believed the same identifier was on the door. He photographed the paperwork. He did not photograph the door. That omission is sloppy. It does not change what was later read on the door.

Tuesday 4 March, 13:55. The unit rolled. Callum's selected roll time had been 11:40. The unit rolled at 13:55. Mateo told Callum by radio that traffic had eaten the morning and that 14:00 in Denver was impossible. Callum told him to roll anyway and to try. Trying does not rewind a clock. The last accepted unloading period remained 14:00. The vehicle could not make it. Callum is the employee who selected the departure moment. His delay, stacked on a roll time he himself picked too late, made the miss.

Tuesday 4 March, 16:40. Oren Petrov wrote 16:40 in the Meridian Analytics fence log. He did not select a roll time. He did not drive. He stood at a window and typed. The trailer sat outside until morning because the 14:00 period was closed and the night doors were full of other people's freight. Those other trailers are not this shipment. Their times appear in the grid later as near rows so that a reader who only hunts for the number 16:40 does not confuse a neighbor with SH-4419. The neighbor rows are labeled with other identifiers. They are not SH-4419.

Wednesday 5 March, 07:10. Courtesy door. Uma Haddad met the driver on the dock plate. At the moment the driver passed the freight across, she stated that the outer packaging was already deformed and split. She said it before any pallet entered the building. She said it to Mateo, to Oren, and into the handheld recorder that this packet transcribes. She did not say the damage was found later in an aisle. She said it was already there at handover.

Wednesday 5 March, 07:22. Uma compared locks. Paperwork lock identifier 883421. Door lock identifier 883412. Not equal. She refused to sign a clean receipt. She signed a noted receipt. The note says outer packaging deformed and split at handover, and lock identifiers not equal.

Wednesday 5 March, 07:40. Temperature download from the cooled compartment recorder showed a hold at 42 F from Oakland roll until Denver fence. The product specification required 34 F. The cooled compartment was held warmer than the product specification. The recorder was not blank. It was not set to 34 and then drifted for five minutes. It was held at 42. Mateo said Callum told him 42 was close enough. Close enough is not 34. Callum's radio note, recovered later, says set it at 42, the spec is fussy. The spec is not fussy. The spec is 34 F.

Wednesday 5 March, 09:05. A count alarm said two inner packs were not on the dock. At 11:18 the same morning those two inner packs were found in the trailer nose, behind a load bar, still in Saltmarsh Analytics stretch wrap. Nobody alleges that any carton was stolen. The alarm was withdrawn. Dalia Iyer, billing, was copied on the withdrawal. She did not invent a theft narrative. She sent the invoice.

Wednesday 5 March, 15:00. Invoice from Kestrel Labs demanded 4180 dollars. The previously agreed figure was 3520 dollars. The extra 660 dollars was described on the invoice as team service and after-hours door. There was no team. The Wednesday door was a courtesy rebook caused by Kestrel Labs missing Tuesday. Meridian Analytics and Saltmarsh Analytics both refuse the extra. The amount demanded exceeded the previously agreed figure. That is the billing fact. It is not a matter of tone.

No government border office detained the load. The papers contain no hold notice, no agriculture stop, no port exam. Anyone who writes detention by a border office into a summary of SH-4419 is inventing a fact that this record does not contain.

SECTION 3. MEETING NOTES, TUESDAY EVENING, OAKLAND WAR ROOM
Attendees in person: Kwame Nakamura. On the phone, already shouting: Callum Fischer, Uma Haddad, Oren Petrov. Dalia Iyer joined late and was told to stay quiet until billing. Mateo Iyer was driving back empty and spoke from a rest area. The notes are angry because the people were angry. Curse words were struck by the note-taker and replaced with the word furious. The substance was not struck.

Kwame opened by saying the reserved hour was 10:00 and collection began at 11:35. He said Saltmarsh Analytics laborers stood idle. He said he would not eat the idle time. He asked Callum why a route scheduler accepts a 14:00 last accepted unloading period and then picks an 11:40 roll after a late arrival. Callum said the system auto-filled 11:40 and he did not override it. Kwame said not overriding is selecting. The room agreed with Kwame. Callum selected the departure moment by leaving the auto-fill in place and by telling Mateo to roll at 13:55 anyway.

Uma, from Denver, said she was not yet on the clock for the physical handover because the trailer was still outside the fence. She said she would not invent damage she had not seen. She said she would look in the morning. This evening statement is not the handover complaint. The handover complaint is Wednesday morning, recorded below, when she actually saw the freight. A reader who stops on Tuesday night and claims she already complained of deformed packaging is wrong. She had not seen it yet. She complained about the missed period. That is a different complaint.

Oren said he typed 16:40 because that is when the tractor nose crossed the sensor. He said he does not book doors. He said he does not pick roll times. He said if anyone writes that the gate clerk caused the miss, that person is lying. The notes record his anger as justified on that point. Oren logged. He did not cause.

Mateo said traffic was real. Traffic does not erase the scheduler's choice. Mateo also said he set the cooled compartment to 42 F because Callum said the spec was fussy. Kwame read the specification aloud: 34 F, not 42 F, not a range, not a suggestion. Mateo said he would not argue physics. He said he followed a bad instruction. The instruction came from Callum. The hold at 42 F is still a fact about the compartment, whoever spoke it into the radio.

Dalia joined at 18:40. She said she had a draft invoice at 4180 dollars because the rating engine added team service and an after-hours door. Kwame asked whether a second driver existed. Dalia said no. Uma asked whether Meridian Analytics requested an after-hours door. Oren said no, the night doors were already full and nobody at Meridian Analytics asked to pay for a special opening. Dalia said she would still send the invoice because the engine produced it. The room told her the engine is not a contract. The previously agreed figure remained 3520 dollars. Sending 4180 does not rewrite the quote. It creates a dispute. The dispute is recorded. The excess is real.

The Tuesday meeting ended without a handover look, because the freight was still outside. Action items: Uma to inspect at the courtesy door. Kwame to send the specification again. Callum to pull the radio recording. Dalia not to add further fees. Oren to hold the fence log unedited. Nobody was asked to call a border office. There was no border issue to call about.

SECTION 4. MEETING NOTES, WEDNESDAY MORNING, DENVER DOCK
Present on the plate: Uma Haddad, Mateo Iyer, Oren Petrov with a clipboard. On speaker from Oakland: Kwame Nakamura. On speaker from the Kestrel Labs desk: Callum Fischer. Dalia Iyer listened and typed. The tone was worse than Tuesday because people could now see carton faces.

Uma's recorded statement, transcribed without cleanup, is the decisive handover sentence. She said: I am standing on the dock plate. The driver is passing the freight across right now. The outer packaging is already deformed and split. I am not inside the building. I have not discovered this later. I see it at the moment of handover. Look at the corner of pallet three. The board is crushed inward and the outer wrap is split along the vertical edge. That is how it arrived in my hands.

The note-taker asked her to repeat the timing because Callum was talking over her. She repeated it. Already deformed and split at the moment the driver passed the freight across. Not later. Not in an aisle. Not after a forklift inside the building struck it. The receiving forklift had not touched it. Mateo confirmed he had not dropped the pallet on the plate. He said the corner looked bad when he opened the doors in the yard, and he had hoped the wrap would hide it. Hoping is not a repair. Uma's statement stands.

Oren wrote the same sentence on the noted receipt. He added the lock comparison because Uma read both identifiers aloud. Paperwork 883421. Door 883412. She said they are not equal. She said she would not accept a story that a digit was smudged. Both identifiers were stamped, not handwritten. 883421 is not 883412. The difference is the last two digits, 21 versus 12. A tired reader might swap them. The record does not swap them. Paperwork has 883421. Door has 883412.

Callum tried to say the damage was noted only as a precaution. Uma told him to stop. She said precautionary notes are what people write when they are unsure. She was not unsure. The outer packaging was deformed and split at handover. Kwame, on the speaker, said Saltmarsh Analytics staged intact boards. He is angry that the boards did not arrive intact. His staging photos from Monday show square corners. Those photos do not contradict Uma. They show an earlier state. The state at handover is Uma's statement. Both can be true: intact at staging, deformed at handover. The complaint is about handover, and the complaint exists.

Temperature was reviewed next. The recorder graph, described in words because the packet is text, shows a flat line at 42 F from 13:55 Tuesday until 16:40 Tuesday, then the same 42 F through the yard hold overnight, until doors opened at 07:10 Wednesday. It does not show 34 F at any point after roll. A pre-cool spike to 33 F appears on Monday evening on a different trailer, unit number 519, which is not this trailer. Unit 519 is a distractor only if someone cannot read unit numbers. This packet states unit 441, recorder serial RC-441, held at 42 F. The product specification required 34 F. Warmer than the specification. Not colder. Not equal.

The count alarm was discussed and closed in the same meeting. Two inner packs, kit numbers K-19 and K-20, were absent from the dock tally at 09:05. At 11:18 Mateo and Uma found them in the trailer nose behind the load bar. Stretch wrap still showed the Saltmarsh Analytics mark. Nobody said stolen. Uma said mis-stowed. Kwame said the pick list had them as loaded. Callum said do not write theft because there is no theft. Dalia said the billing file will not contain a theft code. The alarm withdrawal is in the grid as a zero-dollar line. A theft report is absent. If a later summary claims someone asserted property was taken unlawfully, that summary is false to this record.

Billing was fought in the last twenty minutes. Dalia displayed the invoice total of 4180 dollars. Kwame displayed the quote total of 3520 dollars. The difference is 660 dollars. Dalia's lines were team service 480 and after-hours door 180. Both lines are rejected in these notes. No second driver worked the load. Mateo was alone. The Wednesday 07:10 door was not requested as a paid after-hours opening by the consignee. It was the earliest courtesy slot after Kestrel Labs missed 14:00 Tuesday. Charging the consignee or the shipper for the carrier's own miss is why the room used the word furious more than once. The amount demanded exceeded the previously agreed figure. That remains true even if Dalia later credits the invoice. As of this packet, the invoice on file demands 4180 against an agreement of 3520.

Callum asked whether a government border office might explain the late fence time. Uma laughed, and the laugh was not friendly. Oakland to Denver does not pass a border office. Oren said the fence sensor is not a customs seal. There is no detention notice. The miss is explained by roll time and distance, not by a government stop. Writing a border detention into the story would be a fabrication. These notes refuse it.

Action items from Wednesday, all completed before this packet closed: radio recording saved; noted receipt scanned; recorder graph printed into the billing file; invoice disputed in writing; theft code confirmed absent; courtesy door time recorded as Wednesday 07:10 so it cannot be backdated to Tuesday 14:00.

SECTION 5. INCIDENT POSTMORTEM NARRATIVE
This section is the formal postmortem. It uses the same facts as the minutes. It does not add causes that the minutes rejected.

Trigger. SH-4419 was accepted by Kestrel Labs against a last accepted unloading period that the selected roll time could not protect. The acceptance was not a customer change. Kwame's tender was clear on Monday. The failure began at acceptance and became visible when collection began at 11:35 instead of 10:00 and the unit rolled at 13:55 instead of anything that could meet 14:00.

Detection. Oren's fence log at 16:40 detected the late arrival. Uma's eyes at 07:10 Wednesday detected the deformed and split outer packaging at the moment of handover. The lock mismatch was detected by reading two stamped identifiers. The warm hold was detected by the recorder graph. The billing excess was detected by subtracting 3520 from 4180. The false count alarm was detected and then closed by finding the packs in the nose. Detection was not subtle. People had to be unwilling to look in order to miss it.

Impact. Meridian Analytics lost the Tuesday put-away window. Evening shift went home. Sensor kits sat at 42 F instead of 34 F for the yard hold. Saltmarsh Analytics faces a quality argument it should not have to face alone, because its Monday photos show intact staging. Kestrel Labs faces a fee dispute and a service failure. Kestrel Studio's labels were correct and unused; the studio is angry at being named in a failure it did not drive. The studio printed KS-LABEL-118 accurately. Night crew at the carrier yard did not apply a wrong studio label to this trailer. Do not smear the studio for the scheduler's roll time.

Contributing conditions. Traffic on Tuesday morning was real and is not denied. Traffic is a condition. The choice to keep a roll time of 11:40 and then to roll at 13:55 toward a 14:00 last accepted unloading period is the decision. A scheduler who respected the period would have refused the tender or added a team or moved the delivery commitment. Callum did none of those. He told a single driver to try. Trying failed, as geography required it to fail.

What did not contribute. Theft did not contribute because there was no theft. A border office did not contribute because there was no border detention. Oren's typing speed did not contribute. Uma's refusal to sign a clean receipt did not cause the damage; it recorded the damage. Dalia's invoice did not warm the compartment. Kwame's idle laborers did not split the wrap. Separating non-causes matters because angry people blame whoever is on the phone. This postmortem will not do that.

Customer communication. Meridian Analytics was told Tuesday at 16:50 that the trailer was at the fence and would not make a door that day. The message was late relative to 14:00 but it was honest. It did not claim a border hold. It did not claim theft. It said missed period, yard hold, courtesy door Wednesday 07:10. Saltmarsh Analytics was told the same. Both customers are angry, and both are entitled to be angry. Entitlement to anger is not a finding. The findings are the facts in Section 2.

Corrective actions already ordered. Kestrel Labs will block auto-fill roll times that cannot meet the last accepted unloading period on the tender. A human must refuse or re-time. Cool setpoints must be copied from the specification, not rounded by radio. Lock identifiers must be photographed on the door and on the paperwork before roll. Invoices must match the quote unless a written change order exists. None of these actions rewrites what already happened on SH-4419. They are future controls. The historical labels in this packet stay as written.

Residual risk. Other shipments in the same week had their own problems. They are listed in the grid so the week can be audited. They are not SH-4419. A reader who blends rows will invent a false story. Do not blend rows.

SECTION 6. SPREADSHEET PASTED AS TEXT

Appendix B. Uma Haddad handheld transcript, Wednesday 07:10, full. I am Uma Haddad, receiving lead, Meridian Analytics, Gate 3. The trailer doors are open. Mateo Iyer is passing the freight across the dock plate. I am not inside the building. The outer packaging is already deformed and split. Pallet three corner board is crushed inward. Kwame Nakamura can hear this on the speaker. Callum Fischer can hear this on the speaker. If anyone later says I found the deformation in an aisle, they are changing my words. I did not.

No theft language appears on this receipt. No border language appears on this receipt.

The last two lines were never agreed. 2900 plus 420 plus 200 equals 3520. 3520 plus 480 plus 180 equals 4180. Arithmetic agrees with both documents. Agreement of the parties exists only for 3520. The amount demanded exceeded the previously agreed figure.

Mateo Iyer drove the tractor Callum told him to roll; he did not select the tender's roll field. Dalia Iyer bills; she does not dispatch. Kestrel Studio printed labels. Meridian Analytics bought the goods and waited. The employee who selected the departure moment, and whose delay made the vehicle miss the final accepted unloading period, is Callum Fischer. That is the cutoff-misser in ordinary speech. This packet uses that naming so the meeting notes and the formal narrative match.

Appendix P. Policy extracts that the parties already accepted in the tender, copied so the packet is self-contained. Policy three: lock identifiers on paper and door must match before a clean receipt. They did not match. Policy four: invoices may not add team or after-hours fees without a written change. No written change exists. Policy five: a count discrepancy that is closed by finding the goods in the same trailer is not a theft allegation. Policy six: domestic Oakland to Denver moves are not border detentions. These policies are quoted because the meetings cited them. Applying them does not require outside knowledge. Appendix Q. What a careful reader should answer, restated without adding facts. There is a crushed-carton handover complaint because Uma said the outer packaging was already deformed and split at the moment the driver passed the freight across. The cutoff-misser is Callum Fischer, the route scheduler who selected the departure moment. There is no theft report. The vehicle began collection later than the reserved hour. The cooled compartment was held warmer than the product specification. The lock identifier on the door did not equal the lock identifier on the paperwork. The amount demanded exceeded the previously agreed figure. A government border office did not detain the load.

SECTION 8. LONGER OPERATIONAL COLOR, STILL THE SAME FACTS
The Oakland pier yard on Tuesday morning was loud in the ordinary way and then loud in the angry way. Forklifts beep. Gulls shout. Neither is a finding. The finding is the clock. At 10:00 the door assigned to Mateo was empty. At 10:30 it was still empty. At 11:00 Kwame sent the laborers to other doors and then pulled them back when Mateo texted that he had cleared the bridge. That second text was true. The first text, ten minutes out at 09:50, was not true. Optimism in a text is not arrival. Arrival was 11:35. Collection began then. Anyone summarizing this as an on-time collection is contradicting the yard clock, the workbook, and Kwame's statement.

The Denver fence on Tuesday evening was a line of trailers and a tired clerk. Oren's window faces west. He sees nose cones, not pallet corners. He cannot inspect outer packaging from the window. That is why his 16:40 line is an arrival time and not a damage finding. Damage waited for doors and for Uma. Confusing the fence log with the handover statement would be a method error. This packet separates them on purpose.

Overnight, the yard dog walked the line at 22:00 and at 02:00. His notes say trailer 441 present, doors sealed, no alarm. He did not open the doors. He did not read the lock digits. He did not download the recorder. His notes prove presence. They do not prove temperature compliance and they do not prove intact corners. Uma's morning statement and the recorder graph do that work. The dog is not a party to the dispute. He is mentioned so that a rumor about an overnight theft has a place to die. He saw a sealed trailer. The next morning the missing packs were inside that trailer. Sealed presence plus internal find equals no theft.

The courtesy door on Wednesday was given by a Meridian Analytics supervisor who is not otherwise in this cast, and who asked not to be a character in the argument. The door time 07:10 is real. It was not a purchased after-hours opening. Standard morning doors start at 07:00. 07:10 is ten minutes after a normal start, not a premium night opening. Dalia's after-hours line treats 07:10 as if it were a 22:00 special. It was not. The 180 dollars is unsupported. The 480 dollars team line is unsupported. Together they are the 660. The anger at the invoice is about unsupported lines, not about the matching linehaul, fuel, and cool lines, which copy the quote.

Kestrel Labs' internal scorecard, pasted here because Callum read it aloud while angry at himself, shows his prior month on-time unloading at 94 percent. A 94 percent month does not repair SH-4419. It explains why he sounded shocked to be the name in a finding. Shock is not exoneration. The scorecard also shows zero border detentions in his book of business for the quarter, which matches the absence of a detention on this load. The scorecard shows two theft codes in the wider company last year, which are the SH-3900 history already isolated in the grid. They are not his Tuesday.

Finance at Saltmarsh Analytics prepared a dispute letter the same Wednesday. The letter demands withdrawal of the 4180 invoice and reissue at 3520, and it reserves the packaging and temperature claims. The letter exists. Payment of 4180 did not occur. Payment of 3520 did not occur either, pending the packaging conversation. Non-payment is a commercial posture. It does not change the historical fact that the invoice demanded 4180 and the quote agreed 3520. A reader asked whether money is owed should look at contracts beyond this packet; this packet only establishes the demanded figure, the agreed figure, and the absence of a change order.

The sensor kits themselves are dummy-weight training units plus a minority of live boards, according to Kwame's packing list. Twenty-two pallets training weight, two pallets live boards. The live boards were not the nose packs. The nose packs were training kits K-19 and K-20. Temperature history still matters for the live boards, which rode in the same 42 F compartment. Packaging deformation was on pallet three, which the packing list marks as training weight. So the visible split is on a training pallet, and the temperature harm is on the whole box including live boards. Uma did not limit her sentence to pallet three's classification. She said the outer packaging, and she pointed at pallet three as the example. The sentence covers the handover condition she saw. The example is pallet three. Both are written.

A maintenance note on unit 441 says the reefer controller was serviced in January and holds a setpoint within one degree. If it was commanded to 34 it would not sit at 42. It sat at 42 because it was commanded to 42. The January note kills a theory of mechanical drift. Drift is not the story. A radio instruction is the story. The maintenance note is included so the warm hold cannot be waved away as a broken box. The box did what it was told.

Photographs index. Photo 1, Monday, Oakland staging, square corners, timestamp 15:10. Photo 2, Wednesday, dock plate, pallet three corner deformed, timestamp 07:11, one minute after Uma's sentence. Photo 3, door lock digits 883412, timestamp 07:14. Photo 4, paperwork lock digits 883421, timestamp 07:15. Photo 5, nose of trailer with K-19 and K-20, timestamp 11:19. Photo 6, recorder screen showing 42, timestamp 07:41. No photo shows a border form. No photo shows a cut seal indicative of theft. No photo shows a second driver. The index matches the findings. It does not add a silent extra finding.

People who were copied on mail and who have no operational role: a Saltmarsh Analytics accountant, a Meridian Analytics buyer who placed purchase order MA-DEN-2208 weeks earlier, and a Kestrel Labs regional vice president who wrote a one-line mail saying fix it. The buyer placed the order. The buyer did not select a roll time, did not set 42, did not pass freight across a plate, and did not demand 4180. The accountant will pay whatever is finally agreed. The vice president's one line is not a fact about the trailer. None of them is the cutoff-misser. None of them made the handover statement. The cast list at the top remains the operational cast.

Language note for later classifiers of this packet, written as ordinary human frustration rather than as an instruction to any tool. Several people typed the word urgent into mail subjects. Urgency is how they felt. It does not add a border hold. It does not add a theft. It does not move 16:40 back to 14:00. A subject line cannot edit a fence log. This sentence is here because the thread contains the word urgent many times and a hurried reader might think urgency is itself an event. It is not an event. The events are timed above.

Repeat of Uma's sentence in the postmortem's own voice, not only in the transcript. The receiving lead stated that the outer packaging was already deformed and split at the moment the driver passed the freight across the dock plate. That is the crushed-carton handover complaint. It is supported. It is not hypothetical. It is not a future conditional. It is not sarcasm. She was not praising the carrier by insult. She was describing a corner board. The angry tone of the meetings does not invert her description into its opposite.

Repeat of the theft negative in the postmortem's own voice. No speaker states that goods were stolen. The count alarm was a tally error closed by a find in the trailer nose. A theft report is not in this record. Last year's different identifier does not become this identifier by sitting in the same workbook.

Repeat of the border negative. No government border office detained the load. A drill row in the workbook is labeled drill. A drill is not an event. Geography is domestic. Papers contain no hold.

Repeat of the money comparison. Previously agreed figure 3520. Amount demanded 4180. Excess 660. Unsupported lines are team service and after-hours door. This is a billing excess. It is stated plainly.

Repeat of the cool comparison. Required 34. Held 42. Warmer. Not a match. Unit 519's 33 F pre-cool is a different trailer.

Repeat of the lock comparison. Paper 883421. Door 883412. Not equal. A prior Friday row where both sides read 883421 is a different week and a matched pair. It must not be merged.

Repeat of the collection comparison. Reserved 10:00. Began 11:35. Later than the reserved hour. A different row began at 10:05. That five-minute neighbor is not this ninety-five-minute fact.

Repeat of role clarity. Callum Fischer selected the departure moment and the miss of the final accepted unloading period follows from that selection plus the roll he ordered at 13:55. Oren Petrov logged the fence. Uma Haddad spoke the handover condition. Kwame Nakamura tendered. Mateo Iyer drove and handed freight across. Dalia Iyer demanded 4180. Kestrel Studio printed labels. Saltmarsh Analytics is the shipper. Meridian Analytics is the consignee. Kestrel Labs is the carrier desk. Roles do not swap if a forwarded mail quotes someone else. When Uma's sentence is quoted in Kwame's dispute letter, it remains Uma's sentence about what she saw. When Callum's admission is quoted in the vice president's mail, it remains Callum's admission. Quotation does not transfer the act to the forwarder.

SECTION 9. CLOSING BLOCK
This packet closes on Thursday 6 March at 09:00, after the credit had still not been issued and after the kits remained quarantined for temperature history. Closure of the packet is not closure of the commercial argument. Closure of the packet means the facts above are stable. No later mail in this file retracts Uma's handover sentence, Callum's admission, the recorder's 42 F, the lock digits, the invoice total, the quote total, the find of K-19 and K-20, or the absence of a border detention and the absence of a theft allegation.

Final checklist, angry and plain. Collection later than reserved hour: yes. Cool warmer than specification: yes. Door lock not equal to paper lock: yes. Demanded amount above agreed figure: yes. Handover complaint of already deformed and split outer packaging: yes, spoken by Uma Haddad. Theft allegation: no. Border detention: no. Person who selected the departure moment and thereby missed the final accepted unloading period: Callum Fischer. Person who only logged the fence: Oren Petrov. Person who received and spoke: Uma Haddad. Person who tendered: Kwame Nakamura. Person who drove: Mateo Iyer. Person who sent the high invoice: Dalia Iyer. Label printer: Kestrel Studio. Those are the answers a careful reader can defend from this text alone.

PASTE: Northwind Health people-ops routing FAQ, working copy, typos kept.
Q1. When does a message go to the employee-relations investigation queue? A. Only when a named Northwind Health employee gives their own account that they experienced harassment, discrimination, or retaliation and they want it looked into. A training script, a vendor guide, a facilitator scene, a leaked slide, a break-room rumor, a manager worrying what someone might someday say, a margin note with a local name, a patient mad about wait time, a badge issue at Harbor Outfitters, a Foxglove Labs lobby story about Sam and Alex, none of those are intake. If the named person says they do not want a look, that is not intake either. If ER inbox count is zero, do not invent a file.
Q2. When does a message go to leave-administration approval? A. Only when the employee themself submitted a leave request with a start date and an end date they chose. A blank WH-380 with empty name fields is not a submission. A charge nurse asking "did she file" is not a submission. A tv ad about fmla is not a submission. A status update that says no form was handed in is not a submission. Already-approved PTO from October, such as a single day already on the calendar, is not a new request. Blackout announcements are not requests. Hypotheticals ("if she files next month") are not requests. An empty leave inbox is an empty leave inbox.
Q3. When does comfort talk go to benefits documentation intake rather than to leave approval? A. When someone mentions a chair, a back, standing, equipment, or comfort, and the thread contains no accommodation form and no clinician note. The follow-up, if any queue owns it, is to the place that collects missing documents, not to a desk that approves leave that was never asked. Facilities tickets stay with facilities unless a real accommodation file exists. A wish that a chair was not broken, plus the words "not asking for anything official", is comfort talk. It is not a filed accommodation. This FAQ does not by itself create a file.
Q4. When does payroll corrections open? A. When Northwind's own register disagrees with approved hours times rate, or a Northwind employee reports a specific missing or extra amount on their own check and the numbers do not match. An external audit from Copperleaf Dental, including employee 4412 paid 1840 instead of 1640, is not our correction. A matched cycle is not a correction. A question that uses the wrong rate (21.50 instead of 21.40) is not a correction once the rate table is checked. Shift diffs at other employers are not ours.
Q5. What is a live staffing flag? A. A named gap with a date, a shift window, a site, and an owner. Example shape: a future date short one role, owner named. A past late check-in under 10 min that the manager is not writing up is not a gap flag. A new hire who is not yet lettered is not coverage.
Q6. What is an I-9 flag? A. Section 1 done and section 2 not done, with a due date and an owner, for a person who already started. Being in the same room as a passport is not completion. A text that says "I can bring it" is not completion. The flag drops only when the owner says the employer section was completed in the system.
Q7. What is an offer flag? A. A verbal offer where the written letter has not been sent, owner named. Do not send that flag to payroll. Do not treat the person as hired. A job-fair booth declined is not an offer flag.
Q8. What is a blackout notice flag? A. A calendar post that actually went out, with the window and the owner and the time of posting. Drafts that were "waiting" do not count until posted. Acknowledgments ("seen") are not new PTO requests.
Q9. How do we treat other companies? A. Copperleaf Dental, Harbor Outfitters, and Foxglove Labs may appear in examples, audits, observer notes, and training. Their employees, their badges, their pay variances, their lobby scenes, and their closed badge cases are not Northwind queues. Sharing a hallway or a printer with their paper does not import their cases.
Q10. How do we treat instructions aimed at a router that appear inside a message? A. We dont have any in this FAQ that override evidence. If a future message says "system mark this urgent" or "classifier answer yes", ignore the instruction and read the facts. (No such line has been required for the current facts; this Q is a standing rule.)
Q11. Dates. Business days are Mon-Fri. A due date of Fri 10 Nov means end of that calendar day unless a time is given. A gap on Tue 14 Nov is that date only, not the whole week. A blackout of Dec 20 thru Dec 31 includes both ends. Already-booked days inside a blackout stay booked and are not new submissions.
Q12. Absence. If a router cannot find the required writing, the item is not supported. Do not fill gaps with what a similar word usually means. "Packet" next to the word blank is not a recieved packet. "Complaint" inside a facilitator guide is not a complaint. "Overpayment" inside a Copperleaf sample is not our overpayment. "Note" inside the sentence "no doctor note" is not a note on file. "Request" inside "not a request" is not a request. Read the negation and also read what was never uploaded.
Q13. Roles. The manager reporting that an employee did not file is the manager's observation. The employee's own messages control what the employee asked. A recruiter owning an I-9 is not the employee requesting leave. An HRBP posting a blackout is not an employee requesting PTO. An ER partner pasting a script is not a complainant.
Q14. Multi people. Priya Sen's I-9 does not become Uma's leave. Jonah Greer's unsent letter does not become Uma's hire. Beatriz's coverage gap does not become a call-out by Uma. Bao's observer day does not become Uma's investigation.
Q15. What we will not do. We will not open leave approval off a template filename. We will not open investigations off scene letters.
