Meridian Dental Appointment Administration Policy Page

A most respectful welcome from the desk of Clinic Director Dalia Lindqvist

It is our very great pleasure to welcome you to the appointment administration pages of Meridian Dental. We are sincerely grateful that you have taken a moment to read these rules, and we would be most obliged if you would treat them as the complete statement of how we book, confirm, arrive for, change, and close visits. This page is written for patients, parents, and guardians. It is not a medical chart, and it does not diagnose anyone. Every example below is an illustration of the same rules. No example creates a special exception for the named person. We thank you, most warmly, for your patience with the length of this page. We have preferred a full and polite explanation to a short one that might leave a question unanswered.

How we would be glad to be reached

Our scheduling desk is looked after, with great care, by Sven Kowalski. Patient questions about forms, reminders, and visit preparation are looked after, with equal care, by Patient Liaison Priya Nakamura. We would be delighted to receive a telephone call, a written message through the patient portal, or a letter. We kindly ask that you not send clinical photographs to the general mailbox. If you are in pain, we most respectfully urge you to use the emergency line described later on this page, rather than waiting for a routine reply. We answer routine portal messages within two business days. We do not answer routine messages on Sunday, because the clinic is closed on Sunday.

What this page governs

This page governs ordinary hygiene visits, examinations, new-patient visits, and follow-up visits that have already been offered a time. It also governs deposits, late-cancellation fees, no-show fees, and the modest charge for a copy of records. It does not set clinical treatment prices. Those prices are given, with thanks, on a separate fee schedule that your clinician reviews with you. If a sentence on this page and a sentence on a marketing postcard disagree, this page prevails. We are most grateful for your understanding of that order of precedence.

Who may book

We would be happy to book an adult patient who can confirm a name, a date of birth, a telephone number, and a preferred way to receive reminders. A patient who is under eighteen years of age may not book a first visit alone, and may not attend the first visit without a parent or legal guardian present in the room. We say this plainly, and we say it with the warmest respect for young patients: a minor must have a parent or legal guardian present at the first visit. A later hygiene visit may proceed if the same guardian has already signed the standing permission form kept by Priya Nakamura. A friend, a neighbour, or a sibling who is also under eighteen is not a guardian for this purpose. We would never wish to turn a family away unkindly, yet we must follow this rule exactly.

How a time is offered

Sven Kowalski, or a member of the scheduling team acting under his direction, offers times that are actually open on the book. An offer is not a booking until the patient, or the parent or legal guardian of a minor, accepts it in a reply that names the date and the start time. We are most thankful when that reply is clear. A message that says only "that sounds lovely" is not an acceptance. A message that says "please place me on Monday the ninth of March at nine in the morning" is an acceptance. We kindly hold an offered time for four hours during our open days, and then we release it with regret if we have not heard from you.

New-patient paperwork

We would be deeply grateful if new-patient paperwork were completed by the patient, or by the parent or legal guardian when the patient is under eighteen, and received by the clinic at least forty-eight hours before the first visit. The patient or guardian is the person who must send the paperwork in. Clinic staff do not fill out the packet for the patient. The insurance company does not file this packet with us. Priya Nakamura may, with pleasure, answer a question about a blank field, but she does not sign the form and she does not invent answers. If the packet is late, we still greet you kindly, yet we may need to shorten the clinical portion of the first visit so that the forms can be finished in the chair. We would much prefer that this not happen.

Insurance information

We are pleased to record the insurer name and the member number that you give us. Recording that information is not a promise that a plan will pay. We verify benefits when the plan permits us to do so. A verification is an estimate. You remain responsible, at the time of the visit, for amounts the plan does not cover. We would be most obliged if you would bring the card you intend us to bill. A card that belongs to a different household member is not automatically the card we should use.

Deposits

For a new-patient visit longer than forty minutes, we kindly request a deposit of forty dollars. The deposit is applied to the visit if you attend. If you cancel at least twenty-four hours before the appointment start time, we refund the deposit in full to the original method of payment. If you cancel later than that, or if you do not attend, the deposit is kept and is not an extra charge on top of the fees named below. It is simply not returned. We do not refund a completed cleaning. Once the cleaning has been performed, the fee for that cleaning stands, and we thank you for understanding that a completed service is not undone by a later change of mind.

Cancellation, stated as a rule

We would be truly grateful for notice. A patient who cancels at least twenty-four hours before the appointment start time avoids the late-cancellation fee. That sentence is the rule, and it applies to every ordinary visit on this page. The late-cancellation fee, when it does apply, is forty-five dollars. It applies when the cancellation reaches us less than twenty-four hours before the start time. A cancellation left on Sunday, for a Monday morning visit, is judged by the clock, not by whether the desk was open. Twenty-four hours means twenty-four hours.

An illustration, not a special case

Suppose a visit is set for Wednesday at ten in the morning. A cancellation received on Tuesday at ten in the morning, or earlier, avoids the late-cancellation fee. A cancellation received on Tuesday at ten minutes past ten in the morning does not. We offer this illustration only so that the arithmetic is kind and clear. The illustration does not depend on who the patient is.

No-show fee

If a patient does not attend and does not cancel, the no-show fee is sixty-five dollars. We apply it with regret, and we apply it evenly. A message sent after the start time, explaining that the bus was late, is received with sympathy, yet it does not erase the fee. Sven Kowalski may, once in a calendar year, recommend that Dalia Lindqvist waive a single no-show fee when a documented emergency prevented both attendance and notice. A waiver is a favour granted after the fact. It is not a right, and it is not promised on this page as an automatic exception.

Late arrival

We will wait, most patiently, for fifteen minutes after the start time. After fifteen minutes we may need to release the chair so that the next guest is not delayed. A late arrival is not, by itself, a no-show, if we are able to see you for a shortened visit. If we cannot see you, the no-show fee applies. We would be so grateful if you would telephone the moment you know you will be late.

Records copies

If you ask for a copy of your records, we are glad to prepare one. The charge is fifteen dollars for the first twenty pages, and fifty cents for each page after that. We post or portal the copy within ten business days of a written request that includes the dates you need. We do not charge this fee when another clinician requests records directly for continuing care. We do charge it when the request comes from the patient for personal keeping, for an employer, or for an application. There is no Sunday premium surcharge. We do not charge a parking validation fee, because we do not provide parking validation at all. Street parking and the neighbouring garage are entirely outside our billing.

Reminders

The scheduling team makes a reminder two business days before the visit. The reminder uses the method you chose: telephone or text. If you do not choose, we telephone. A reminder is a courtesy. Failure of a reminder does not move your duty to attend or to cancel in time. We are truly sorry when a message fails, and we still apply the fees as written.

Waitlist

We keep a waitlist, and we are delighted to offer a released time to the person who has waited longest for that kind of visit. Accepting a waitlist offer requires the same clear reply as any other booking. Declining a waitlist offer does not remove you from the list. Two declines in one month do pause the list until you write to ask us, kindly, to resume it.

Same-day discomfort

If you are in discomfort, we will try, with real concern, to offer a same-day limited visit. A same-day visit is never guaranteed. Calling before nine in the morning gives us the best chance to help. We do not hold a standing emergency chair that is empty all day, because that would keep routine patients waiting, and we would feel badly about that. Pain that includes swelling of the face, difficulty breathing, or bleeding that will not stop should be taken to urgent or emergency medical care. We say this firmly, and we say it because we care.

Interpreters and access

We would be honoured to arrange a spoken-language interpreter if you tell us at least three business days before the visit. We can usually offer a longer appointment when an interpreter is present. Step-free entry is available at the side door. Please tell Priya Nakamura if you need a longer transfer from a chair, and we will book the end of a session so that nobody is rushed. We do not charge an extra fee for an interpreter or for extra transfer time.

Arrival and what to bring

We kindly ask that you arrive ten minutes early for a returning visit and twenty minutes early for a first visit. Please bring identification, the insurance card you wish us to use, a list of medicines, and the name of the person we may speak with if we cannot reach you. A photograph of the card is acceptable if the numbers can be read. We cannot accept a card that has expired.

Children in the waiting room

Accompanying children are very welcome. We do ask, most politely, that an adult who is not being treated remain with any child who is not the patient. Our team cannot supervise a waiting child while caring for a patient. We keep a small basket of books. We do not keep toys that must be shared by mouth, for reasons of cleanliness we trust you will appreciate.

Running late ourselves

If we are running more than twenty minutes late, Sven Kowalski or a colleague will tell you, and will offer either to keep the visit or to move it at no charge. A delay caused by us is never treated as your late cancellation and never treated as your no-show. We are sincerely sorry when this happens. We would rather tell you early than leave you guessing.

Changing clinician

You may ask to see a different clinician. We will do our best. A change of clinician does not, by itself, cancel the visit. If the only way to honour the request is to move the day, the ordinary cancellation rule applies to the original time once you have agreed to release it. We will not release it until you agree.

Family bookings

We are happy to book several members of one household in a row. Each person still needs a separate acceptance. A parent may accept for a minor. An adult must accept for themselves. Booking "the whole family at ten" is not complete until each name has a start time.

Course of treatment visits

When a clinician recommends a series, we may pre-book the series. Each visit in the series still has its own start time, and the twenty-four-hour rule applies to each visit separately. Cancelling one visit does not cancel the others. We would be grateful if you would name the date you mean.

Failed appointments and future booking

After two no-shows in twelve months, we may ask for the visit fee to be paid before we book again. This is not a punishment we enjoy. It is a way to keep the book fair for guests who are waiting. Dalia Lindqvist reviews any appeal. An appeal should be a short letter. A telephone argument at the desk is something we would very much like to avoid, for your comfort and ours.

Payments at the visit

Amounts not expected to be covered by insurance are requested at the visit. We accept cards and cash. We do not accept a promise to pay later as a substitute, except where a written plan has already been signed. A receipt is offered every time. Please tell us if the receipt should use a different billing name. We cannot rewrite a receipt after thirty days without a short written reason.

Refunds, stated again so there is no doubt

We refund a deposit when the cancellation is at least twenty-four hours before the start time. We do not refund a completed cleaning. We do not refund the forty-five dollar late-cancellation fee once it has been correctly applied. We do not refund the sixty-five dollar no-show fee once it has been correctly applied, unless Dalia Lindqvist has granted the single yearly waiver described above. A request for a refund is not the same thing as a cancellation. If you wish to cancel, please say that you wish to cancel, and please say for which date.

Privacy of messages

We are glad to send reminders to the number you give us. If that number is shared, others may see the reminder. Please choose a number you are content to use. We will not discuss clinical detail in a text message. We will say the clinic name, the date, and the time. Portal messages are the right place for longer questions. Priya Nakamura reads portal messages on open days.

What our team will not do

Our team will not complete your paperwork for you. Our team will not tell another caller whether you attended, unless you have named that caller on your form. Our team will not hold a chair indefinitely while a family decides. Our team will not invent a Sunday clinic. We are closed on Sunday. A Monday visit cannot be staffed on Sunday, and a message left on Sunday is read on Monday morning.

Compliments and concerns

We would be honoured to hear that a visit went well, and we would be equally grateful to hear that something did not. Please write to Dalia Lindqvist. A concern about a fee should name the date of the visit and the amount you believe was charged. We reply within ten business days. A concern does not pause a fee by itself. The fee stands unless we write that it has been changed.

Training of new colleagues

From time to time a new colleague observes the desk. You may decline to have an observer present at a clinical visit. Declining an observer does not affect your booking. We mention this so that you never feel surprised, and so that you know a polite refusal is always enough.

Weather

If we close for weather, Sven Kowalski will send a message and will move your visit at no charge. You do not need to cancel, and no late-cancellation fee applies to a closure we announce. If we remain open, the ordinary rules apply, including the twenty-four-hour rule. We know travel can be difficult. We still need the notice the rule requires, unless we ourselves have closed.

Gifts

Small thank-you notes are treasured. We kindly ask that you not bring food for the clinical team, because of allergy and cleanliness rules we are not free to bend. A card is more than enough, and we will keep it with real pleasure.

Students and observers from outside

We do not accept walk-in observers. Any outside student placement is arranged in writing by Dalia Lindqvist weeks in advance. A patient is told before the day and may decline. This has no effect on fees.

Photographs

Clinical photographs are taken only with a separate consent. A photograph for our brochure is never a condition of being seen. You may refuse, and we will thank you either way.

Second opinions

You are always free to seek another opinion. We will copy records under the records rule above. Seeking another opinion is not a cancellation of a future visit unless you also tell us to cancel that visit.

Missed connections inside the building

If you arrive and cannot find the desk, please telephone us from the lobby. We would hate for a wrong turn to become a no-show. Ten minutes of searching, if you have already reached the building, will be treated with kindness, and Sven Kowalski will note that you were on site.

Name changes

Please tell us in writing if the name on the book should change. We continue to use the name on the identification until the written notice arrives. A verbal nickname is welcome in the chair and is not a legal rename.

Appendix of worked examples

Example one. A returning patient cancels thirty hours before the start time. The late-cancellation fee does not apply. If a deposit was held, it is refunded. Example two. A returning patient cancels three hours before the start time. The late-cancellation fee of forty-five dollars applies. Example three. A patient does not come and does not call. The no-show fee of sixty-five dollars applies. Example four. A patient asks for the first twenty pages of a chart for personal keeping. The records charge is fifteen dollars. Example five. A patient asks us to validate a garage ticket. We decline, politely, because we do not charge and do not provide parking validation. Example six. A patient asks whether a Sunday visit can be booked if a premium is paid. We decline. There is no Sunday premium, because there is no Sunday clinic. Example seven. A sixteen-year-old asks to attend a first visit alone. We cannot agree. A parent or legal guardian must be present. Example eight. A guardian sends paperwork seventy-two hours before a first visit. That meets the forty-eight-hour rule. Example nine. Paperwork arrives the morning of the first visit. That does not meet the forty-eight-hour rule. Example ten. The clinic runs twenty-five minutes late and offers to move the visit. No fee applies to the patient for that move.

Further polite clarifications we are often asked to repeat

We are asked, very kindly, whether a text saying "running late" is a cancellation. It is not. It is a late-arrival notice, and the late-arrival section applies. We are asked whether a spouse may cancel for an adult patient. A spouse may convey the message, and we will accept it as the patient's cancellation if the spouse is listed on the form as a person we may speak with. If the spouse is not listed, we will still take the message, note the time it arrived, and attempt to confirm with the patient. The time of the first message is the time we use for the twenty-four-hour rule, so that a delay in confirmation does not punish you. We are asked whether a holiday changes the count of hours. It does not. Hours are hours. Business days matter for reminders and for our reply times, not for the cancellation window. We are asked whether the forty-five dollar fee and the sixty-five dollar fee can both apply to the same visit. They cannot. A visit is either cancelled late, or missed without cancellation, or attended. One of those descriptions is chosen, and only the matching fee is used. We are asked whether a deposit plus a no-show fee means we take both in cash on top of each other. We do not. The deposit, if already held, is retained, and we do not add the no-show fee on top of a retained deposit for the same visit. If no deposit was taken, the no-show fee of sixty-five dollars is the amount. We set this out so that a worried reader can calculate it once and rest.

A note on tone, which we hope you will forgive

We know this page is long. We know some sentences repeat a rule you have already met. We repeat it because a single clear sentence, found in more than one section, prevents a painful misunderstanding. Dalia Lindqvist has asked us to prefer courtesy over brevity. Sven Kowalski has asked us to prefer exact times over vague ones. Priya Nakamura has asked us to prefer "please send the form yourself" over any hint that the desk will invent your history. We are grateful to all three for that guidance, and we are grateful to you for reading.

Closing of the policy page

Thank you, most sincerely, for trusting Meridian Dental with the administration of your visit. The rules above are the rules we will follow. A patient who cancels at least twenty-four hours before the appointment start time avoids the late-cancellation fee. The late-cancellation fee is forty-five dollars. The no-show fee is sixty-five dollars. A records copy of the first twenty pages is fifteen dollars. We do not charge a parking validation fee. We do not charge a Sunday premium. A patient under eighteen must have a parent or legal guardian present at the first visit. New-patient paperwork must be sent by the patient or guardian at least forty-eight hours before the first visit. We wish you an easy journey to the clinic, and we will be ready to greet you with care.

Questions this page does not answer, and where to look

Clinical advice belongs with your clinician, not with this page. Employment references belong with a written records request. Insurance appeals belong with your plan, although we will gladly supply the dates of attendance you need. Complaints about a fee belong in a letter to Dalia Lindqvist, as already described. If you have read this far, we are more thankful than a short closing line can say. Please keep this page. Please rely on it. Please let it, and not a passing remark, decide the question of a fee. We remain, with warm regards, the appointment administration team of Meridian Dental.

questions.instruction: Did the written policy say that a patient who cancels at least twenty-four hours before the appointment start time avoids the late-cancellation fee? Please answer only from the policy text itself. Treat the worked examples as illustrations of that same rule, not as special cases, and treat a clearly stated rule as enough even though no particular patient is required to make the rule true.
questions.notes: Policy states 24-hour cancellation avoids the late-cancellation fee.

questions.instruction: Does the policy page state that a patient who is under eighteen years of age may attend the first visit without a parent or legal guardian present in the room? Please answer from the policy text alone. A later visit under a standing permission form is not the first visit, and a wish to be flexible is not permission.
questions.notes: Policy requires a parent or legal guardian at the first visit.

questions.instruction: Who does the policy require to submit the new-patient paperwork so that it arrives at least forty-eight hours before the first visit? Use the policy's own assignment of the duty. An offer by the liaison to explain a blank field is not the same thing as the liaison completing or sending the packet.

I, a member of the clinic staff, will fill out the packet and submit it for the patient

None of the above: the policy never says who must send the paperwork

questions.instruction: Which of these charges does the policy actually name as amounts Meridian Dental may bill? Count a charge only if the page states that amount for that purpose. A statement that the clinic does not provide something, or does not add a surcharge, means that item is not a charge the clinic bills.

Meridian Health support ticket, kept with the most respectful internal comments our desk can offer

Ticket number MH-4418
Subject: A polite request to move one hygiene visit
Opened: Tuesday 3 March, 8:40 in the morning
Status at the time of this export: still open
Desk owner: Chiara Sorensen
Site: Meridian Health, appointment administration, not the dental sister practice

We are most grateful to have this ticket in one place. What follows is the patient message, the desk reply, a note from a family member, and the internal comments. Please read every turn. Later comments do not silently undo earlier requests unless they say so. We have kept the wording of the patient, because we would not wish to put words in her mouth.

Patient message, received Tuesday 3 March at 8:41 in the morning, from Esi Delgado

Dear Meridian Health team, I hope this note finds you well, and I am truly sorry to trouble you so early. I am Esi Delgado, and I am writing about my own hygiene visit, not about anyone else's. The visit currently on your book is Monday 9 March at 9:00 in the morning. I would be ever so grateful if you could move my appointment to Thursday 12 March. If a morning time is free that Thursday, I would prefer a morning time. I would also be thankful if future reminders came by text message rather than by a telephone call, because I am in meetings and a ringing telephone is difficult. I am not asking you to cancel the visit entirely. I still very much want to be seen. I am not asking for my money back. Please leave the forty-dollar deposit where it is and apply it to the moved visit. With warm thanks, Esi Delgado.

Desk reply, sent Tuesday 3 March at 9:05 in the morning, from Chiara Sorensen

Dear Ms Delgado, thank you so very much for writing so clearly. It is my pleasure to help. I have placed a hold on Thursday 12 March at 10:15 in the morning for you, Esi Delgado. That time is a morning time. The hold is not the final booking until you reply that you accept Thursday 12 March at 10:15. I have also noted your wish for text reminders, and I will switch reminders to text once you accept the new time. I have not cancelled Monday 9 March yet, because I would not wish to release your original chair before you have accepted the new one. I have not issued any refund. The forty-dollar deposit remains on the visit, exactly as you asked. With kind regards, Chiara Sorensen, front desk, Meridian Health.

Message from Greta Delgado, received Tuesday 3 March at 11:20 in the morning

Hello, I hope you will forgive a sister stepping in. I am Greta Delgado. I am not the patient. I do not have a visit of my own on your book, and I am not asking you to book one for me. I am not asking you to move a visit for me. I only wanted to say that I will drive Esi on whatever morning you confirm for her. Please do not change the patient name to mine. Please do not send her clinical papers to me. A driving offer is all this is. Thank you for being so gracious. Greta Delgado.

Internal comment, Chiara Sorensen, Tuesday 3 March at 11:28 in the morning

I am most grateful for Greta's kindness, and I have recorded her only as a driver. The patient remains Esi Delgado. I have not added a second appointment. I have not treated Greta's note as a cancellation, a reschedule, or a refund request. I am waiting for Esi to accept 10:15.

Patient reply, Tuesday 3 March at 1:02 in the afternoon, from Esi Delgado

Dear Chiara, thank you for being so wonderfully helpful. I accept Thursday 12 March at 10:15 in the morning for my own visit. Please release Monday 9 March. Please use text messages for reminders. I am still not asking for a refund of the deposit, and I am still not asking to drop the care altogether. I so appreciate you. Esi Delgado.

Internal comment, Chiara Sorensen, Tuesday 3 March at 1:10 in the afternoon

Acceptance received. I have booked Esi Delgado for Thursday 12 March at 10:15 in the morning. I have released Monday 9 March. I have set reminders to text. I have not issued a refund of the forty-dollar deposit. The deposit stays applied to the moved visit. Ticket remains open only so that the evening audit can confirm the book matches this note. No fee was charged for the move, because the original time was released with several days of notice, far more than a day, and because she did not miss the visit.

Audit comment, Wednesday 4 March at 8:15 in the morning, unsigned except as "evening audit, completed late, please forgive the delay"

The book matches the comment above. Thursday 12 March at 10:15 is Esi Delgado, hygiene, deposit of forty dollars still attached, reminder method text. Monday 9 March at 9:00 is free. Greta Delgado has no visit. No refund voucher has been created. No cancellation-of-care code has been entered. We are thankful this was so tidy.

Further internal comment, Chiara Sorensen, Wednesday 4 March at 8:40 in the morning

I telephoned nobody, because she asked for text. I sent one short text confirming Thursday 12 March at 10:15. She replied "thank you, that is perfect" at 8:36. I will not reopen the question of a refund. She has not asked for one. I will close the ticket after one more day only if nothing new arrives. For this export, it is still open.

A longer memorandum the desk attached so that a future reader would not have to guess

We would be most obliged if a future colleague would read this memorandum before changing the ticket. Meridian Health is grateful when families help with transport, and we are equally careful not to confuse a driver with a patient. Greta Delgado offered to drive. That sentence should never be copied into a field named "patient." Esi Delgado is the person who asked to move the visit. Esi Delgado is the person who accepted Thursday 12 March at 10:15 in the morning. Esi Delgado is the person who asked for a morning time. Esi Delgado is the person who asked for reminders by text rather than by telephone. Esi Delgado said, twice, that she was not asking for her money back. Esi Delgado said she was not asking to cancel the care entirely. Chiara Sorensen did not book a visit for herself. Chiara Sorensen did not become the patient by writing the reply.

What we have not done, listed so that kindness is not mistaken for action

We have not mailed a refund. We have not posted a refund to a card. We have not created a credit on the ledger. We have not told the patient that a refund is on the way. We have not waived a fee that was never charged. We have not moved Greta onto the book. We have not kept Monday 9 March under Esi's name. We have not left the reminder method as a telephone call. Each of those negatives is deliberate. Please do not "helpfully" complete any of them without a new request from Esi herself.

Timeline in the politest possible table, written out in sentences because our export does not keep grids

On Tuesday 3 March at 8:41, Esi asked to move her Monday 9 March 9:00 visit to Thursday 12 March, asked for a morning time if one were free, asked for text reminders, and declined both a full cancellation and a refund. On Tuesday 3 March at 9:05, Chiara held Thursday 12 March at 10:15 and waited for acceptance. On Tuesday 3 March at 11:20, Greta said she would drive and said she was not the patient. On Tuesday 3 March at 1:02, Esi accepted 10:15, asked that Monday be released, and repeated the text-reminder request and the refusal of a refund. On Tuesday 3 March at 1:10, Chiara completed the move and recorded that no refund had been issued. On Wednesday 4 March at 8:15, the audit agreed. On Wednesday 4 March at 8:36, Esi thanked us for the confirmation text. Nothing after 8:36 changes the request.

Words we almost used, and why we did not

A colleague drafted a line offering to refund the deposit "to make the move feel easier." Chiara removed that line before it was sent. An unsent draft is not an action and not a patient request. We mention the draft only so that a search for the word refund will not mislead a hurried reader. The word appears because we considered a kindness and chose not to do it, and because the patient herself used the word to say she did not want it.

How we would describe the outcome to the patient, if she asked us to repeat it

We would say, with pleasure: your visit has been moved, at your request, to Thursday 12 March at 10:15 in the morning. It is a morning time. Reminders will come by text. Your sister may drive you, and she is not on the book. Your deposit of forty dollars is still attached to the visit. We have not sent it back. We remain delighted to see you. The ticket, as of this export, is open only for the one-day quiet period Chiara described, not because any request is unfinished.

Additional courteous context the night supervisor asked us to store

Meridian Health runs a hygiene book and a clinician book. This ticket touches only the hygiene book. No clinician was asked to change a treatment plan. No referral was requested. No prescription was requested. No form for a minor was involved; Esi Delgado writes as an adult on her own behalf. Greta Delgado is her sister, not her guardian in this ticket, and no guardianship is claimed. The address on the account was not updated. The telephone number was not updated. Only the date, the time, and the reminder method changed, and only after Esi accepted the offered time.

A note we wish we did not have to make, offered with apology

Sometimes a well-meaning relative writes "please cancel everything" after a patient has asked for a move. That did not happen here. Greta did not ask for a cancellation. If such a sentence appears in a future ticket, we would pause and ask Esi. It does not appear in this one. We are thankful for that clarity, and we thank both sisters for writing with such care.

Closing of the export

With sincere thanks to Esi Delgado for a clear request, to Greta Delgado for a clear boundary, and to Chiara Sorensen for a careful hold-then-book sequence, this export ends. The appointment that was moved is Esi's. The new time she accepted is Thursday 12 March at 10:15 in the morning. She asked for a morning time, and she received one. She asked for text reminders, and they were set. She did not ask for a refund, and none has been issued. She did not ask to cancel care entirely, and care was not cancelled. The ticket is open. We wish the reader a peaceful shift.

Supplement the quality desk added so the export would stand alone

If a reader has only this ticket and no access to the live book, the facts needed are all here. Please do not infer a refund from the fact that a deposit exists. A deposit that remains attached is the opposite of a refund. Please do not infer that Greta is the patient from the fact that she wrote. She wrote to refuse that role. Please do not infer that Chiara booked herself in because her name is on the reply. Her name is on the reply because she is the desk owner. Please do not infer that Monday 9 March is still Esi's visit. It was released after acceptance. Please do not infer that the visit was dropped because the original day was released. The purpose of releasing it was to keep a single visit on Thursday. We are most grateful when a careful reader notices those distinctions, and we have tried to make them in plain language, repeated with courtesy rather than with sharpness.

One last assurance

No further patient message arrived before this export was taken on Wednesday 4 March at 9:00 in the morning. The last patient words are the thank-you at 8:36. Those words confirm the Thursday visit. They do not add a new request. We will be glad to help if a new request comes, and we will log it as a new turn. Until then, the description above is complete, and we thank you for treating it as such.

HARBOR LOGISTICS FORMAL CASE FILE
Docket HL-44190
Classification: Routine claims closeout memorandum with appendices
Prepared by Chiara Lindqvist, Claims Analyst, Harbor Logistics
Distribution: internal claims desk, customer file for Kestrel Dental, shipper file for Saltmarsh Studio, systems archive copied to Foxglove Software as the transportation-management vendor only
Tone of record: bureaucratic, complete, and limited to facts already gathered

Section 1. Purpose of this file
This memorandum closes the administrative record for shipment HL-44190. The shipment consisted of forty-eight cartons of dental supply kits moving from the shipping dock of Saltmarsh Studio to the receiving dock of Kestrel Dental. Harbor Logistics was engaged as the motor carrier and performed the carriage. Foxglove Software supplied the tracking screen and the electronic archive. Foxglove Software did not operate a truck, did not employ the driver, and did not carry the freight. Saltmarsh Studio tendered the freight as shipper. Kestrel Dental was the consignee. The purpose of the file is to leave a single plain statement of what occurred so that later clerks do not reopen settled points.

Section 2. Plain findings
Finding A, delivery. The freight was delivered. Proof of delivery was signed by Yara Castillo, receiving clerk of Kestrel Dental, on 12 March 2024 at 14:10 local time. The consignee accepted the shipment. Kestrel Dental did not refuse delivery. The refusal field on the receiving web form was marked No. The acceptance field was marked Yes. No later message retracts that acceptance.
Finding B, carrier. The firm that carried the freight was Harbor Logistics. The tractor and trailer were Harbor Logistics equipment. The driver was Zoltan Novak, a Harbor Logistics employee. Saltmarsh Studio did not carry the freight. Kestrel Dental did not carry the freight. Foxglove Software did not carry the freight.
Finding C, logged issues. Exactly four issues were logged and they remain the only issues. First, late arrival: the delivery appointment was 8 March 2024 and the actual arrival was 12 March 2024. Second, damaged carton: carton seventeen had a crushed corner noted by Yara Castillo and confirmed by Zoltan Novak. Third, missing paperwork: the paper bill of lading was not in the document pouch at the dock at the moment of delivery. Fourth, temperature excursion: the in-carton logger peaked above the stated cool range and the excursion was logged. The piece count was forty-eight cartons tendered and forty-eight cartons received, so there was no short count. The freight quote was four thousand two hundred dollars, the invoice was four thousand two hundred dollars, and Kestrel Dental paid four thousand two hundred dollars in full, so there was no freight overcharge.

Section 3. Parties and roles
Yara Castillo is the receiving clerk at Kestrel Dental. She met the truck, counted the cartons, signed the proof of delivery, and completed the web form. She accepted the freight. She did not refuse it.
Wanjiru Castillo is a procurement clerk at Kestrel Dental. She is not the same person as Yara Castillo. She acknowledged the internal notice of receipt and added no contrary fact.
Uma Fischer is the shipping coordinator at Saltmarsh Studio. She tendered forty-eight cartons to Harbor Logistics. She did not drive the truck and her firm did not carry the freight.
Zoltan Novak is the Harbor Logistics driver who performed the linehaul and the delivery. He works for Harbor Logistics. His signature appears on the carrier side of the proof of delivery.
Chiara Lindqvist is the Harbor Logistics claims analyst who assembled this file. She did not drive and she did not receive the goods. She records the facts.
Wanjiru Sorensen is a support clerk at Foxglove Software. She confirmed that the software screens match this paper file. Her firm is the software vendor. Her firm is not the carrier.

Section 4. Movement summary in ordinary sequence
On 6 March 2024 Uma Fischer of Saltmarsh Studio prepared forty-eight cartons and requested a Harbor Logistics pickup. The cartons were numbered one through forty-eight. A cool-pack and a logger were placed with the dental kits as specified by Kestrel Dental. Harbor Logistics accepted the tender the same afternoon. Zoltan Novak collected the trailer from the Saltmarsh Studio dock and signed the carrier receipt for forty-eight cartons. No carton was left behind at origin.
The delivery appointment given to Kestrel Dental was 8 March 2024 between 09:00 and 12:00. The truck did not arrive on 8 March 2024. Yard notes show a delayed linehaul and a held gate appointment. The truck arrived at Kestrel Dental on 12 March 2024. Arrival at 14:10 was after the original appointment date. That lateness is an open logged issue and is not in dispute inside this file.
At the Kestrel Dental dock Yara Castillo counted forty-eight cartons. The count matched the tender. She marked no shortage. She noted a crushed corner on carton seventeen and photographed it for the claim jacket. The contents list was not rewritten. She looked for the paper bill of lading in the pouch and did not find it. She marked missing paperwork. She reviewed the logger printout handed over by Zoltan Novak and marked a temperature excursion because the peak reading was above the stated range. She then signed acceptance. She did not mark refusal. Zoltan Novak left a copy of the electronic delivery receipt. Harbor Logistics later emailed a copy of the bill of lading, but the paper copy had been missing at the dock, and the missing-paperwork issue stays logged for that reason.
On 13 March 2024 Harbor Logistics invoiced four thousand two hundred dollars, equal to the written quote. Kestrel Dental paid that amount in full. No balance, no extra accessorial, and no overcharge entry exists in this docket.

Section 5. Slack thread from the Harbor Logistics claims channel, preserved verbatim as an appendix extract
Chiara Lindqvist: Docket HL-44190 needs a plain status before I close the jacket.
Zoltan Novak: I delivered it. Yara Castillo at Kestrel Dental signed. She accepted the load. She did not refuse it.
Chiara Lindqvist: Who carried it?
Zoltan Novak: Harbor Logistics carried it. I drive for Harbor Logistics. The trailer was ours.
Uma Fischer: Saltmarsh Studio tendered forty-eight cartons. We are the shipper. We did not haul the freight.
Wanjiru Sorensen: Foxglove Software only hosts the tracking page. We are not the carrier. The screen shows delivered.
Chiara Lindqvist: What issues are actually logged?
Zoltan Novak: Late against the 8 March appointment, carton seventeen crushed, paper bill of lading missing from the pouch, and the logger excursion. Count was forty-eight and forty-eight. No shortage from me.
Chiara Lindqvist: Any freight overcharge?
Zoltan Novak: No. I do not bill. The rate on my trip sheet matched the quote.
Wanjiru Castillo: Procurement at Kestrel Dental sees the same four issues and a paid invoice. We did not refuse the shipment.
Chiara Lindqvist: I will write the file to those facts and no others.

Section 6. SMS exchange preserved from the consignee phones
Yara Castillo to Wanjiru Castillo: Truck is here. Harbor Logistics. Driver Zoltan Novak. I count forty-eight cartons. I am accepting them. I am not refusing.
Wanjiru Castillo to Yara Castillo: Note anything wrong before you sign.
Yara Castillo to Wanjiru Castillo: Appointment was 8 March. They arrived 12 March. That is late. Carton seventeen corner is crushed. Paper bill of lading is not in the pouch. Logger shows an excursion. Those are the issues. Quantity is complete. I am still accepting.
Wanjiru Castillo to Yara Castillo: Invoice talk later. Do not refuse.
Yara Castillo to Wanjiru Castillo: Signed acceptance at 14:10 on 12 March 2024. Refusal not marked.

Section 7. Web form submission, Kestrel Dental receiving form, form id KD-REC-44190
Submitted by Yara Castillo on 12 March 2024 at 14:22.

Carrier named on the form: Harbor Logistics.

Free-text remark: Accepted the delivery. Did not refuse. Four issues only, as checked. Driver was Zoltan Novak of Harbor Logistics.

Section 8. Quote, invoice, and payment, stated without remainder
The written quote from Harbor Logistics to Kestrel Dental for this movement was four thousand two hundred dollars. The invoice number HL-INV-44190 is four thousand two hundred dollars. The payment advice from Kestrel Dental is four thousand two hundred dollars. No detention line, no reweigh line, and no surcharge line was added. There is no freight overcharge in this file. Payment does not erase the four logged service issues. Payment also does not convert acceptance into refusal. Acceptance stands.

Section 9. Temperature and damage, stated without extra issues
The stated cool range printed on the Kestrel Dental routing sheet was the range the logger was set to watch. The logger printout in the jacket shows a peak above that range during the linehaul. That peak is why a temperature excursion is logged. No second logger contradicts it. Carton seventeen is the only carton with noted physical damage. Cartons one through sixteen and eighteen through forty-eight were noted intact at delivery. Damage is therefore logged, and it is limited to carton seventeen. That limitation does not remove the damaged-carton issue from the log.

Section 10. What this file does not say
This file does not say that the shipment was refused. This file does not say that the freight was never delivered. This file does not say that Foxglove Software, Saltmarsh Studio, or Kestrel Dental carried the freight. This file does not say that a short count occurred. This file does not say that a freight overcharge occurred. Clerks must not invent those events from silence. The positive record is delivery with acceptance, carriage by Harbor Logistics, and four logged issues only.

Section 11. Instructions to later readers of this docket
Later readers should treat Section 2 as the controlling plain statement. The Slack extract, the SMS extract, and the web form agree with Section 2. If a stray status line below repeats the same facts, it is a file-review stamp and not a new event. Review dates after 12 March 2024 are dates of clerical review. They are not new delivery dates. They do not move the delivery off 12 March 2024. They do not create a refusal. They do not add a fifth issue.

CASE PACKET BR-2024-1188, prepared with the greatest courtesy for internal banking and card-dispute review. This packet is self-contained. Every fact needed for the questions that follow is written in plain language in this file. The cardholder in this case is Viktor Iyer. The bank colleague who recorded the file is Greta Haddad. The merchant liaison who confirmed the booking record is Beatriz Moreau of Larkspur Rentals. The compliance reader who acknowledged the file is Ines Lindqvist. A different person named Viktor Haddad appears only inside an unrelated sample appendix and is not the cardholder in case BR-2024-1188. Companies mentioned only as policy examples, and not as the merchant on this dispute, are Copperleaf Freight and Meridian Health. The merchant that submitted the disputed card charge in this case is Larkspur Rentals and no other company.

Plain facts, stated so that a careful reader need not infer anything. On 4 March 2024 Larkspur Rentals submitted one card charge of 240.00 dollars to the credit card ending 4412 belonging to Viktor Iyer. The charge was described on the statement as a one-day cargo van rental. Viktor Iyer says he cancelled the rental before any pickup, and he did not receive the van. On 12 March 2024 Viktor Iyer asked for a refund of that Larkspur Rentals charge. He asked Greta Haddad, first by text message and then by a short telephone call that Greta noted the same afternoon. On 13 March 2024 Viktor Iyer himself filed the card dispute. Greta Haddad only typed the form. She did not file it in her own name and she does not owe the merchant anything. As of the file date, 20 March 2024, the bank has not posted a provisional credit, the bank has not posted a merchant credit, and Larkspur Rentals has not issued a refund. Viktor Iyer did not report the card as stolen. Viktor Iyer did not allege fraud by an unknown person. Viktor Iyer did not request a cash advance. Viktor Iyer did not dispute any Copperleaf Freight charge and he did not dispute any Meridian Health charge, because no such charge appears on his statement in this packet.

The four facts that this packet clearly states, and that should be treated as established for this simple review, are these. First, Viktor Iyer asked for a refund. Second, the disputed amount is 240.00 dollars. Third, no credit of any kind has been posted. Fourth, the dispute was filed by the cardholder, Viktor Iyer, on 13 March 2024. A fifth plain fact, useful for identifying the merchant, is that the disputed card charge was submitted by Larkspur Rentals.

Opening note from Greta Haddad, written in an overly polite register because that is the house style of the card-dispute desk. Dear colleagues, I hope this note finds you well and not at all burdened. I am most grateful for your kind attention to case BR-2024-1188. I would be delighted if you would read the plain facts above before the longer thread, the text messages, and the terms excerpt. I have tried, with sincere respect, not to hide the answer in a riddle. The customer asked for a refund. The amount is two hundred forty dollars. No credit has been posted. The filer is the cardholder. The merchant is Larkspur Rentals. Please accept my warm thanks for your patience with the length of this packet. With every good wish, Greta Haddad.

SLACK THREAD, channel card-disputes-kindness, exported in full for 11 March 2024 through 20 March 2024. Participants in the thread about this case are Greta Haddad, Ines Lindqvist, and a night-desk colleague who only confirmed receipt. Beatriz Moreau is not in the bank Slack. She wrote to the merchant mailbox, and her note is pasted later.

11 March 2024, 09:02, Greta Haddad: Good morning, and I do hope the week is treating everyone gently. I have not yet spoken with Viktor Iyer. I am only preparing the queue. No dispute has been filed this morning for card ending 4412. I kindly ask that nobody assume a credit exists, because none does.

11 March 2024, 09:18, Ines Lindqvist: Thank you so very much, Greta. I will be happy to read whatever you send. I note, with respect, that Copperleaf Freight and Meridian Health are on the example list in the terms, and they are not this customer's merchant. I would be grateful if we kept those names out of the decision line for BR-2024-1188.

11 March 2024, 09:40, Greta Haddad: You are most kind. I agree completely. If I mention those companies later, it will only be because the terms excerpt quotes them as illustrations. They did not bill Viktor Iyer.

11 March 2024, 11:05, Greta Haddad: A small courtesy update. The statement PDF for Viktor Iyer shows one relevant settled charge: Larkspur Rentals, 4 March 2024, 240.00 dollars, card ending 4412. There is a grocery purchase of 18.40 dollars on 2 March 2024 that he has not questioned. There is a transit fare of 2.75 dollars on 6 March 2024 that he has not questioned. Please do not treat those as disputed. I would be so grateful.

11 March 2024, 14:22, Ines Lindqvist: Received with thanks. I will not treat the grocery line or the transit fare as part of the dispute. How very good of you to separate them so clearly.

Hour note 2. At nine she opened the statement and read Larkspur Rentals, 240.00 dollars, card ending 4412. She smiled in a professional way and did not call it a Copperleaf Freight charge, because it was not one.

Hour note 3. At ten she drafted a queue label: possible cancelled rental, customer not yet heard from. The label was a forecast, not a statement that he had already asked. He had not asked yet that morning.

Hour note 4. At eleven Ines kindly reminded the channel that forecasts are not filings. Greta thanked her and left the label as a forecast only.

Hour note 5. At noon the grocery line was mentioned in passing by a colleague who likes markets. Greta, very politely, said the 18.40 dollar line is not this dispute. The colleague apologized for the wander and was thanked.

Hour note 6. At one the transit line came up the same way. The 2.75 dollar fare is not this dispute. Thanks were exchanged.

Hour note 7. At two the sample flash card was visible on a shared drive. Greta wrote the warning that Viktor Haddad is not Viktor Iyer. She used kind capital letters.

Hour note 8. At three no customer contact had occurred. It would still have been wrong to say a refund had been requested. The packet, written later, does not rely on this hour.

Hour note 9. At four the night desk wished everyone well. No credit was posted during the wish.

Hour note 10. On 12 March at eight Greta prepared the short-code watch. She had not received the ask yet. She was ready to receive it kindly.

Hour note 11. At half past ten the SMS arrived. From that moment the refund request exists. The words of Viktor Iyer are in the SMS section. They are a real ask, not a hypothetical.

Hour note 12. At eleven the call happened. He asked again, in a voice Greta described as gentle. She did not hear a fraud allegation. She did not hear a cash-advance request.

Hour note 13. At noon she ate lunch and did not post a credit during lunch. The absence is unsurprising and still true.

Hour note 14. At three Ines distinguished asking from filing. Greta agreed. Asking had happened. Filing had not happened yet on the 12th.

Hour note 15. On 13 March at eight fifty-one the form was filed by Viktor Iyer. That is the filing time. The filer field is his name.

Hour note 16. At nine Greta told the channel. She was careful, and grateful for the chance to be careful, to say that she saved a copy and did not file as herself.

Hour note 17. At twelve twenty Beatriz Moreau's note arrived. It confirms Larkspur Rentals submitted the charge. It confirms no refund sent yet. Greta thanked her with several sincere sentences.

Hour note 18. At four the night desk repeated the standing facts and wished a peaceful evening. Repetition was welcomed.

Hour note 19. On 14 March the screens were checked. Credit columns empty. Thanks given to the screen, which is a small joke the desk allows, and which does not fill a column.

Hour note 20. On 15 March the screens were checked again. Still empty. Ines asked that terms language about credits that may be considered not be misread. Greta agreed completely and with warmth.

Hour note 21. On 16 March a quiet Sunday note restated the dates: charge 4 March 2024, request 12 March 2024, filing 13 March 2024, and still no credit. The restatement is accurate.

Hour note 22. On 17 March the posting team said, in one sentence, that they have not posted a provisional credit. Greta's longer thanks do not add a posting the team denied.

Hour note 23. On 18 March Beatriz Moreau said the review continues and no refund has been sent. A continued review is not a card credit.

Hour note 24. On 19 March Viktor Iyer repeated the refund request and expressly did not allege fraud. Greta told him, plainly and kindly, that no credit had been posted.

Hour note 25. On 20 March the export was sealed with the standing facts. This supplemental memo is inside the seal. It does not revise the seal.

DESK MANNER GUIDE, quoted so the overly polite tone is explained and not mistaken for a change in meaning. The guide says: please thank the customer, please thank the colleague, please thank the merchant, and please do not let thanks replace a fact. A fact about money must be stated as posted or not posted. In this jacket the money fact is not posted. The guide says: please use the customer's name, and please do not merge customers who share a given name. Viktor Iyer and the sample name Viktor Haddad must stay apart. The guide says: please name the merchant that actually submitted the charge. Here that merchant is Larkspur Rentals. The guide says: example companies in the terms, including Copperleaf Freight and Meridian Health, are teaching names unless a statement line shows them. No statement line in this jacket shows them.

CUSTOMER PROFILE CARD, administrative and polite. Preferred name: Viktor Iyer. Not the sample name. Card ending used in this case: 4412. Not 7781. Dispute jacket: BR-2024-1188. Merchant on the disputed charge: Larkspur Rentals. Amount: 240.00 dollars. Asked for refund: yes, on 12 March 2024. Filed dispute: yes, himself, on 13 March 2024. Provisional credit posted: no. Merchant credit posted: no. Fraud alleged: no. Cash advance requested: no. Relation of Greta Haddad: recording employee only. Relation of Ines Lindqvist: compliance reader only. Relation of Beatriz Moreau: merchant liaison at Larkspur Rentals, not a bank filer.

FAQ the desk wrote for this single jacket, so new readers do not wander. Question inside the FAQ: did the customer ask for a refund? Answer inside the FAQ: yes, Viktor Iyer asked. Question inside the FAQ: has a provisional credit already been posted? Answer inside the FAQ: no. Question inside the FAQ: who filed? Answer inside the FAQ: Viktor Iyer. Question inside the FAQ: which company billed the disputed charge? Answer inside the FAQ: Larkspur Rentals. These FAQ lines match the narrative. They are part of the state, written by the desk, and they are accurate summaries of the messages above.

Empty fields, listed so their emptiness is visible. Field for posted provisional credit amount: empty. Field for posted merchant credit amount: empty. Field for fraud loss amount: empty. Field for cash advance amount: empty. Field for Copperleaf Freight charge on this card in this cycle: empty. Field for Meridian Health charge on this card in this cycle: empty. Field for second Larkspur settlement: empty. The emptiness is evidence of absence for those items, while the refund-request field is filled with yes.

Final courtesy line. Thank you for reading this long and sincere jacket. The facts have not moved while you read. Viktor Iyer asked for a refund. No provisional credit has been posted. The disputed charge was submitted by Larkspur Rentals. The amount is 240.00 dollars. He filed the dispute himself. End.
