state:
From: Dalia Kaur
To: Northridge Community School arts office list
Subject: September studio notes, fees, open house, and a long catch-up because I promised I would write it all down

Hi everyone, this is Dalia again, writing from the little office above the kiln room with the window that sticks, and I am going to ramble a bit because there is a lot to pass along before Friday and I would rather put it all in one place than send six short notes that people miss. The Northridge Community School adult and teen arts office is open this week from nine to four, except Wednesday when we close at two for the fire drill practice that facilities scheduled without asking us, which is fine, truly, we love a surprise drill, said no one, but we will smile and walk outside anyway. Coffee is in the usual pot. The good mugs are in the left cabinet. Please stop using the chipped blue one for guests. It looks charming in a photo and less charming when it leaks on a parent’s sleeve.

Official note, and I am putting this near the top so nobody has to hunt: Greta Tanaka is the registrar for this term. If you need a form stamped, a drop processed, or a waitlist moved, Greta Tanaka is the staff member officially named to run registration this term. I am the studio coordinator. Chiara Delgado teaches wheel throwing on Tuesday nights and helps with the kiln schedule. Yara Kowalski runs the teen Saturday lab and the after-school clay club. Mateo Bergstrom and Leila Bergstrom are students, siblings, not staff. None of the rest of us is the registrar. Greta Tanaka is the registrar.

Leila Bergstrom wrote, in the note we typed up from her handwriting and filed on September 12: I withdraw from Intermediate Ceramics. She handed that note to the front desk on September 12. She is not staying in the class. She said she will keep the community wheel time on Sundays, which is a different program and not the course. So the course withdrawal is clear. She leaves Intermediate Ceramics. I am repeating it because three people asked me in the hallway as if the note were a maybe. It is not a maybe. Leila Bergstrom withdraws from Intermediate Ceramics.

Mateo Bergstrom asked whether his late fee could be dropped because the online cart froze. We looked. The cart did freeze for eleven minutes on September 3, and then it worked, and he paid the tuition on September 6, which is three days after the September 3 tuition deadline. The late fee is twenty-five dollars. Mateo Bergstrom’s twenty-five dollar late fee is not waived. The late fee stands. He still owes that twenty-five dollars on top of tuition, which he already paid. Please do not tell him we cancelled it. We did not. A frozen cart for eleven minutes is annoying and we are sorry about the annoyance, and the fee still stands.

The studio still needs twenty pounds of stoneware clay, four boxes of cone six glaze, one replacement kiln shelf, one sponge set, and extra rolling pins. The pottery wheels have already arrived. The cotton aprons are already in the closet. Those two items are not still needed. I will say that again later in the inventory section so the purchasing folks can copy it without calling me.

--- quoted reply from Chiara Delgado, Tuesday night, sent from her phone while the wheels were still slowing down ---

Dalia, I am quoting your note back so you can see I read it, and then I am going to wander, because that is how my brain works after a three-hour throwing class. Yes, I saw that Greta Tanaka is the registrar. I am not going to stamp anything. Students keep handing me forms because I am the one with clay on my hands and they think the person with clay on her hands is in charge of money. I am not. Greta is.

Leila came by before class and left the handwritten note. I did not talk her into staying. I asked if she wanted a minute to think. She said she had already thought. The words on the paper were clear. I withdraw from Intermediate Ceramics. That is a withdrawal. Sunday community wheel time is a drop-in and she can keep that if she pays the drop-in fee, which is separate and already paid for September. Do not put her back on the Intermediate roster because she still likes clay. Liking clay is not the same as being enrolled.

Mateo stopped me at the door and said the cart froze so maybe the late fee should vanish. I told him I do not vanish fees. I told him Dalia and Greta already looked at the dates. Tuition deadline was September 3. He paid September 6. The twenty-five dollar late fee stands. It is not waived. He was polite about it. He also asked if his sister’s withdrawal cancelled his fee. It does not. They are two different students with two different records.

While I have you, the new wheels are in the room and they work. We do not need more pottery wheels. The cotton aprons from last spring are folded in the closet and they are fine. We do still need clay, glaze, a kiln shelf, sponges, and rolling pins, exactly as you wrote. The shelf that cracked is the wide one on the middle rack, not the small test shelf. Please do not order the small one by mistake.

Class tonight was good. Twelve wheels, eleven students, one empty station because Leila is out. Beginners centered better than I expected. The tall kid in the green hoodie, I think his name is Owen but I will not swear to it, made a bowl that actually looked like a bowl. Yara says the Saturday teens want to carve stamps next week. Fine by me if they clean the stamps before they leave. Last time a stamp dried to a bat and I had to soak it for an hour.

I am also pasting the typed-up version of Leila’s note below so it lives in the thread and not only on the paper clipped to the clipboard, which someone will absolutely lose.

--- handwritten-style note typed up, September 12, front desk intake, paper still smells like the lavender hand cream Leila uses ---

Hi, this is Leila Bergstrom. I am writing this by hand because the form kiosk was busy and Greta said a signed note is enough if the desk types it in the same day. I withdraw from Intermediate Ceramics. Please take me off the roster. I am not asking for a different section. I am not asking to switch to the Thursday class. I am leaving the course. I will still come to Sunday community wheel time, which I already paid for as a drop-in, and that is not this course. Thank you for the first two weeks. The wheels are nice. Sorry about the late note. Leila Bergstrom. September 12.

Desk staff typed it as written. No words were added. Chiara watched the typing and nodded. Greta Tanaka entered the withdrawal in the registrar system the same afternoon. Status on the roster: withdrawn. That is the whole story of the withdrawal.

--- product review, pasted in by Yara Kowalski, who said the purchasing committee asked for a plain review of the studio projector we borrowed and then bought ---

Review of the Larkspur Hall portable projector, the one we used for the glaze chemistry slideshow and then decided to keep. I am writing this the way I talk, so it will wander, and that is on purpose because the committee said they wanted a real teacher voice and not a brochure.

The projector is fine. It is not magic. It throws a clear picture on the cinder-block wall if you do not stand in front of it, which teenagers will do, every time, as if the light is a doorway they have to block. Brightness is enough for the studio if we kill the overheads on the kiln side and leave the wheel side on. Color is a little cool, so the photos of copper red glaze look more purple than they fire, and I told the students that, and most of them believed me. One of them did not, and he will learn when the kiln opens. Sound is weak. We do not need sound for glaze slides. If someone wants a film night, borrow a speaker from the music room and do not blame the projector.

Setup takes about four minutes if the cart is where we left it, and twelve minutes if someone rolled the cart into the closet behind the aprons. The remote eats batteries. We already bought batteries. The lens cap keeps vanishing. I tied it on with a piece of wire. It looks silly and it works. Focus is easy. Keystone correction is easy. The menu is full of settings nobody should touch. Please leave the menu alone. I am looking at you, volunteer who set it to ceiling mode and then wondered why the slide was upside down.

Would I recommend it for a classroom that mostly shows slides and a few short clips? Yes. Would I recommend it as a movie theater? No. It is a school projector. It does the school job. We paid for it from the supply line, not from the still-needed list. It is not clay. It is not glaze. It is not a kiln shelf. It is not sponges. It is not rolling pins. Do not let anyone tell purchasing that the projector review means we are done shopping. We are not done shopping. The studio still needs twenty pounds of stoneware clay, four boxes of cone six glaze, one replacement kiln shelf, one sponge set, and extra rolling pins.

Stars, if they insist: four out of five, with one star lost to the lens cap and the weak speaker. I would buy it again. I already sort of did, because the committee asked me and I said yes and then they bought it. That is the review.

--- email from Yara, quoting my earlier message and then wandering into Saturday lab news ---

Dalia, quoting you: The studio still needs twenty pounds of stoneware clay, four boxes of cone six glaze, one replacement kiln shelf, one sponge set, and extra rolling pins. The pottery wheels have already arrived. The cotton aprons are already in the closet.

Yes. That list is right. Saturday lab used the last of the good sponges. The ones left are the sad thin ones that fall apart. We need a sponge set. Kids keep asking for rolling pins because three of ours split. Extra rolling pins are still needed. We are not asking for wheels. The wheels arrived last Thursday and Chiara already used them. We are not asking for aprons. The cotton aprons are in the closet, stacked, labeled, a little dusty, perfectly usable.

Saturday teens were chatty. They want to know if the open house will have food. I told them Harbor Foods is catering the simple tray, sandwiches and fruit, not a banquet. Meridian Rentals is bringing extra chairs for the hallway because our folding chairs are ugly and also short by twenty. Parents asked if a dentist booth is appropriate at an arts open house. I said Kestrel Dental and Granite Dental are local sponsors who bought the banner and the fruit cups, and they will have a table with toothbrushes, and nobody has to stop if they do not want a toothbrush. It is a school event with sponsors. It is not a dental clinic.

A parent also asked if Leila’s withdrawal means the Saturday lab is cancelled. It does not. Leila is not in Saturday lab. Saturday lab is Yara’s teen group. Intermediate Ceramics is the weeknight course Leila left. Different rooms on the roster, even though they share a kiln. Please do not merge them in conversation just because both involve clay.

Another parent asked about Mateo’s fee in the parking lot, which is a bold place to ask about money. I said I do not handle fees and the office already decided. The late fee stands. It is not waived. I did not quote the dollar amount in the parking lot because I was holding a box of stamps and a teenager’s backpack. The amount is twenty-five dollars, and it stands.

--- minutes, loosely typed, September 8 staff huddle, chatty on purpose because our formal minutes get ignored ---

Present: Dalia Kaur, Greta Tanaka, Chiara Delgado, Yara Kowalski. Absent: the facilities lead, who sent a text that said running late and then did not arrive, which we have decided to treat as a genre of absence rather than a mystery.

Greta opened by reminding us she is the registrar this term. She said it in a calm voice. She said please send drops to her, not to the studio group chat, not to a teacher’s personal email, not to a note on the kiln. She will enter them. She entered Leila’s withdrawal on September 12, which is after this huddle, but I am leaving this sentence here so the thread stays honest about the sequence. On September 8 we did not yet have Leila’s note. On September 12 we did.

Fee talk on September 8: tuition deadline is September 3. Late fee is twenty-five dollars if tuition arrives after September 3. Mateo had already paid on September 6 by the time we huddled, so his name was on the late list. Greta said the policy does not have a cart-freeze exception for an eleven-minute outage that resolved the same evening. Mateo Bergstrom’s twenty-five dollar late fee is not waived. The late fee stands. We all heard it. Chiara wrote it on the whiteboard and then erased it because students walk past the whiteboard. It is in these minutes instead.

Supply talk: purchasing will order what we still need and will not reorder what we have. Still needed: twenty pounds of stoneware clay, four boxes of cone six glaze, one replacement kiln shelf, one sponge set, extra rolling pins. Already here: pottery wheels, cotton aprons. Yara added that the projector purchase is separate and already done. Dalia added that Harbor Foods needs a headcount by September 18 for the open house trays. Meridian Rentals needs the chair count by September 16. Greta said she will not be the person who calls the rental company, because she is the registrar, not the events desk. Dalia will call.

We talked about the kiln schedule for twenty minutes longer than we needed to. Cone six on Friday. Bisque on Monday. Do not mix student tests into the glaze firing without a shelf tag. The cracked shelf stays out. That is why we need a replacement kiln shelf. Chiara described the crack in loving detail. It runs from the left edge toward the center and it shed a chip onto a test tile. We are not using it. Ordering a small test shelf instead would be the wrong order. The replacement we need is the wide middle-rack shelf.

We ended because the bell rang and a tour group was in the hall. Greta stayed to answer a registration question from a parent who wanted to know if a cousin could join mid-term. The cousin was not enrolled. Greta did not enroll the cousin in the hallway. She gave the parent the form. That is what a registrar does, and she is the registrar.

--- course notes, rambling catalog blurbs the office asked Dalia to refresh, included so families can read them in this same packet ---

Intermediate Ceramics. This is the weeknight course that meets in the kiln-side studio. It assumes you have centered a cylinder at least once without crying, or with crying, we do not police feelings, but you should know which end of a rib tool is the useful end. We throw, we trim, we talk about feet and rims, and we glaze with cone six. The course has a roster. If you withdraw, you are off the roster. Leila Bergstrom withdrew. She is not in this course anymore. Community Sunday wheel time is not this course. Please stop telling new students that Sunday drop-in counts as Intermediate. It does not. Tuition is due by the posted deadline. A late tuition payment brings a twenty-five dollar late fee. Mateo Bergstrom paid late and his late fee stands. His late fee is not waived. That sentence is about Mateo and about the fee, not about the curriculum, but families read these blurbs looking for money answers, so I am putting the money answer where they will see it.

Beginning Wheel. Chiara’s Tuesday class for people who have never sat at a wheel or who sat at one once at a party and made a sad pancake. We start with wedging. We talk about water. We talk about how much water is too much water, which is almost always the amount a beginner is using. Aprons are provided. The cotton aprons are already in the closet. You do not need to buy an apron for this class. Wheels are in the room. We do not need new pottery wheels for this class. You might get clay on your shoes. Wear shoes you like less than your other shoes.

Teen Saturday Lab. Yara’s group. Stamps, slabs, a little wheel if there is time, a lot of cleanup, because teens are fast at making and slow at sponging. We need a sponge set. The thin leftover sponges are not enough. Extra rolling pins are still needed because slab work without a decent pin turns into a argument with the clay. This lab is not Intermediate Ceramics. A withdrawal from Intermediate Ceramics does not cancel Saturday lab. A student who was never in Saturday lab is still not in Saturday lab. Leila is not in Saturday lab.

Glaze Chemistry Chat, the short Thursday talk, not a full course. We look at slides on the Larkspur projector. We talk about why a glaze crawls. We do not mix experimental recipes in the sink. If you want to test a recipe, you book a test tile and you label it. Unlabeled tests do not go in the kiln. This is not a punishment. It is how we avoid opening the kiln and finding a puddle where a shelf used to be. The cracked shelf is already a lesson. We need a replacement kiln shelf. We do not need a lecture about it, but I am giving a short one anyway, because that is the tone of this packet.

Open Studio Sundays. Drop-in. Not a course. Pay the drop-in fee at the desk. Leila Bergstrom is keeping this and leaving Intermediate Ceramics. Those are two different sentences and both are true. If you only read one of them you will annoy the registrar, and the registrar is Greta Tanaka, and she has a patient face and a finite afternoon.

Family Clay Night. One evening a term. Parents and kids. Harbor Foods brings a simple tray if we give them a headcount. Meridian Rentals brings chairs if the headcount is large. Kestrel Dental and Granite Dental have offered toothbrushes as sponsor gifts. You may take a toothbrush. You may also not take a toothbrush. The arts office does not grade your dental habits. This event is not a class and it does not replace tuition.

Kiln Basics for Volunteers. A short training, not a credit course. You learn how to read a cone, how not to lean on a hot brick, and how to write a shelf tag that another human can read. If your handwriting looks like a seismograph, please print. The replacement kiln shelf, when it arrives, will be introduced in this training so nobody stacks a wide shelf on a post spacing meant for the small test shelf. We still need that wide replacement. It has not arrived.

Waitlist Workshop. A half hour with Greta Tanaka, because she is the registrar, where people learn that a waitlist is a list and not a promise. Being friendly to Chiara does not move you up. Bringing Yara coffee does not move you up. Emailing Dalia three times does not move you up. Greta moves you up when a seat opens, in the order the list says. Leila’s withdrawal opens a seat in Intermediate Ceramics. Greta will offer that seat to the first person on the waitlist. That person is not Mateo. Mateo is already enrolled in a different section and his issue is a late fee, not a seat.

--- parent questions, typed from the front-desk notebook, answers in Dalia’s voice so the packet stays one voice even when the questions wander ---

Question from a parent named I do not have permission to publish, so I will call them Parent A. They asked if the school owes them money because their child tried a wheel for ten minutes and did not like the feeling of clay. Answer: no refund is being processed in this packet, and a trial spin is not a withdrawal. A withdrawal is a student saying they leave the course. Leila did that. Parent A’s child did not. Parent A’s child can stay or can file a real withdrawal with Greta. Until then they are enrolled and the fee schedule in the catalog applies.

Question from Mateo, forwarded by a parent. The cart froze. Can the late fee go away? Answer, already given, given again: Mateo Bergstrom’s twenty-five dollar late fee is not waived. The late fee stands. Tuition deadline was September 3. Payment posted September 6. Eleven minutes of cart trouble on the evening of September 3 does not erase a three-day late payment. We are sorry the cart froze. The fee stands.

Question from a neighbor who is not enrolled and wandered in during the tour. They asked who to call about registration. Answer: Greta Tanaka, the registrar for this term. Not the neighbor’s cousin who took a class in 2019. Not the dentist sponsors. Kestrel Dental and Granite Dental are sponsors. They do not register students. Harbor Foods does not register students. Meridian Rentals does not register students. Greta Tanaka does.

Question about supplies from a volunteer who wants to donate. They offered a box of plastic beads. We do not need beads. They offered old wheels from a garage. We do not need pottery wheels. The pottery wheels have already arrived, and a garage wheel with a wobbly flywheel is not a gift, it is a project. They offered aprons. The cotton aprons are already in the closet. If they want to help, the studio still needs twenty pounds of stoneware clay, four boxes of cone six glaze, one replacement kiln shelf, one sponge set, and extra rolling pins. A gift card to the clay supplier is also welcome. Beads are not.

Question about the projector. Answer: we bought it, Yara reviewed it, four stars, weak speaker, tied-on lens cap, good enough for slides. It is not on the still-needed list.

--- inventory section, plain, for purchasing, written in full sentences because the last spreadsheet got misread ---

The studio still needs twenty pounds of stoneware clay. We are not asking for porcelain this month. We are not asking for fifty pounds. Twenty pounds of stoneware clay are still needed.

The studio still needs four boxes of cone six glaze. Not cone ten. Not a single pint of clear. Four boxes of cone six glaze are still needed. The boxes we have are the odd colors from the sample shelf, and they are not the class set.

The studio still needs one replacement kiln shelf. It is the wide shelf for the middle rack. The cracked one is out of service. A small test shelf is not the item. A replacement kiln shelf, the wide one, is still needed.

The studio still needs one sponge set. The thin leftovers do not count as a set. A sponge set is still needed.

The studio still needs extra rolling pins. Three pins split. Extra rolling pins are still needed.

The studio does not still need pottery wheels. The pottery wheels have already arrived. They are in the room. Chiara used them on Tuesday.

The studio does not still need cotton aprons. The cotton aprons are already in the closet. They are stacked and usable.

If a purchase order lists wheels or aprons as still needed, that purchase order is wrong. If a purchase order leaves out clay, glaze, the kiln shelf, the sponge set, or rolling pins, that purchase order is incomplete. The complete still-needed list is clay, glaze, kiln shelf, sponge set, and rolling pins.

--- more of the email thread, quoted replies, because people keep replying to the reply ---

From Greta Tanaka, registrar, September 13, morning:

Dalia, thank you for the packet draft. I am the registrar for this term. Please keep saying that in the plain way you already said it, because a poetic way will confuse people. I entered Leila Bergstrom’s withdrawal on September 12 after the desk typed her note. Her note says she withdraws from Intermediate Ceramics. The roster shows withdrawn. I offered the open seat to the first waitlist name this morning. That person accepted. Their name is not going in this public packet. Mateo Bergstrom remains enrolled in his section. His late fee of twenty-five dollars is not waived. The late fee stands. I sent him a short receipt note that says the same thing, without the rambling, because my notes are shorter than yours and that is fine.

I will not be at the open house table for the first hour. Yara can point families to the registration clipboard. The clipboard is not a workaround. It is a way to write a name so I can enter it later. Sponsors may sit at their own tables. Kestrel Dental and Granite Dental asked if they could hand out appointment cards. Yes, appointment cards are fine. They may not collect student registration forms. Harbor Foods should deliver to the side door, not the kiln door. Meridian Rentals should stack chairs in the hall, not in front of the wheels.

From Chiara, quoting Greta and adding a kiln paragraph:

Greta, quoting you so I do not mess it up: I am the registrar for this term. Good. Students heard me say it last night and one of them still tried to hand me a drop form. I walked them to the clipboard. Leila’s withdrawal is already in. I am not reopening it because her bowl from week one is still on the drying rack. A bowl on a rack is not enrollment. She may pick up the bowl during Sunday drop-in. If she does not, we will keep it for the usual thirty days and then recycle the clay, which is the normal policy and not a punishment.

Mateo helped wipe wheels after class, which was kind, and which does not waive a fee. I told him the late fee stands. He said he understood. I believe him. Please do not let a helpful wipe turn into a story that the fee was cancelled. It was not.

Kiln note: Friday cone six is full except for the gap where the cracked shelf would have been. That gap is why we need the replacement kiln shelf. Do not fill the gap with a board. A board is not a shelf. I should not have to write that, and yet I am writing it, because last spring someone tried a board and we had a conversation I do not wish to repeat.

From Yara, later the same day:

All of this matches what I am telling Saturday families. Greta Tanaka is the registrar. Leila Bergstrom withdraws from Intermediate Ceramics and is not thereby cancelled from a lab she was not in. Mateo’s late fee is not waived. The late fee stands. Still needed: twenty pounds of stoneware clay, four boxes of cone six glaze, one replacement kiln shelf, one sponge set, extra rolling pins. Not needed: pottery wheels, cotton aprons. Projector: already bought, review attached above, four stars, do not buy a second one just because the lens cap is ugly. Harbor Foods headcount is my job to estimate for the teen tables. I estimate forty teens plus the adults who pretend they are only dropping off and then stay for the fruit. Meridian Rentals should bring twenty extra chairs. If they bring forty, we will have a chair forest, and I will live with a chair forest more easily than I will live with people sitting on the wheel stools, because the wheel stools are not chairs and they roll.

--- open house ramble, included because the events paragraph kept getting separated from the course paragraph and then people made up details ---

The open house is Saturday after next, in the main hall and the studio doorway, not inside the kiln cage. Families can look through the doorway. They cannot lean on the kiln. Harbor Foods is catering sandwiches and fruit. They are not catering a hot dinner. If someone tells you there will be a pasta bar, that someone is inventing a pasta bar. Meridian Rentals is bringing chairs. They are not bringing tables. We have tables. Kestrel Dental will have a small sponsor table with toothbrushes and a banner. Granite Dental will share that table, because two dental offices and one banner is the deal they made with our fundraising lead. Neither office is teaching a class. Neither office is the registrar. Neither office decides fees. If a child asks a dentist whether a late fee can be waived, the correct answer is that the dentist does not know and the school already decided. Mateo Bergstrom’s late fee is not waived.

Music will be low. Yara’s playlist, which is mostly instrumental and slightly too cheerful, which is the right amount of cheerful for a hallway full of damp clay samples. We will show three slides on the Larkspur projector: a wheel, a bowl, a calendar. We will not show a film. The projector review already said the speaker is weak. We are not discovering that again in front of families.

Volunteers should wear the cotton aprons if they are helping at the wheels demo. The aprons are in the closet. We are not buying more aprons for the open house. Demo clay will come from the scrap bucket, not from the twenty pounds we still need to order. Please do not use the new stoneware, when it arrives, as demo clay for people who are only visiting. That clay is for classes.

--- student comments, typed from index cards, chatty, names limited to people already in this packet or left unnamed ---

Card from an Intermediate student who is staying: The class is good. I was worried when Leila left that the class would shrink into a sad small circle. It did not. Her seat went to the waitlist person. Chiara still talks the whole time she demonstrates, which helps, because the silence of a wheel can make you think you are doing it wrong even when you are only doing it slowly. I paid on time. I do not have a late fee. I am only writing that so nobody folds my card into Mateo’s fee story.

Card from Mateo Bergstrom, short, which is unusual for this family, apparently, given how long our packet is: I paid tuition on September 6. I know the deadline was September 3. I asked about the late fee. I was told it stands and is not waived. I am not asking again in this card. I am signing up for the volunteer wipe-down because I like the studio, not because I think wiping waives twenty-five dollars. It does not.

Card from Leila Bergstrom, Sunday drop-in, not a course assignment: I withdrew from Intermediate Ceramics on September 12. I am only here for community wheel time. Please do not mark me present in the course. I was not in the course. My bowl from week one is on the rack. I will pick it up. The wheels are nice. The new ones do not wobble. You do not need more wheels. You might need more pins, because I watched a Saturday kid borrow a pin and the handle was taped. That matches what Yara said. I am not on the purchasing committee. I am just a person who withdrew and still likes Sundays.

Card from a teen in Saturday lab: We need sponges. The thin ones ripped. We need rolling pins. Mine split and I used a jar, and the slab looked like a moon. Yara said the studio still needs a sponge set and extra rolling pins. She also said we do not need aprons. I agree. The aprons in the closet are soft and they have pockets. Pockets are the whole point.

Card from a beginner: I do not know who the registrar is. Someone told me it was the teacher with clay on her hands. Then Chiara said no, Greta Tanaka is the registrar. I am writing it down so I remember. Greta Tanaka is the registrar for this term. I am not withdrawing. I am also not paying a late fee, because I paid before September 3. This card is only about the name, plus a small brag about paying on time, which I will allow myself.

--- fee ledger narrative, not a spreadsheet, because the spreadsheet and the story got out of sync last term ---

Tuition deadline for fall studio courses: September 3. Late fee if tuition arrives after that date: twenty-five dollars. Mateo Bergstrom’s tuition payment posted on September 6. That is after September 3. The late fee was charged. The office reviewed the cart outage. The cart was frozen for eleven minutes on September 3 and then worked. Mateo did not pay during the minutes after it worked. He paid on September 6. Mateo Bergstrom’s twenty-five dollar late fee is not waived. The late fee stands. He owes twenty-five dollars. He does not owe a second late fee. He does not owe Leila’s anything. Leila’s withdrawal does not create a balance for Mateo and does not clear his balance.

Leila Bergstrom’s Intermediate Ceramics tuition was paid on time, before September 3. She then withdrew on September 12. This packet is not a refund decision. This packet records the withdrawal. The withdrawal is real. Whether any money returns is a separate registrar calculation that Greta handles under the catalog rule, and I am not inventing a refund amount here. What I am stating is the enrollment fact: she withdraws from the course. Anyone who needs the money outcome should ask Greta Tanaka, the registrar, and should not invent a number from this paragraph. I am being careful because last year a chatty paragraph was misread as a promise, and I have learned.

No other student in this packet is described as withdrawing. No other student in this packet is described as having a waived late fee. If your name is not Mateo, do not assume the Mateo sentence applies to you. If your name is not Leila, do not assume the Leila sentence applies to you.

--- kiln room log, narrative form, a week of ordinary lines so the packet matches what the clipboard says ---

Monday: bisque load, small, labeled, no cracks in the posts, the cracked shelf stayed on the side table and was not loaded. Dalia wrote a paper sign that says do not use. The sign is still there. We still need a replacement kiln shelf.

Tuesday: Chiara’s class, new pottery wheels in use, no wobble worth reporting, one student forgot to turn a wheel off and Chiara noticed before leaving. Aprons used and returned to the closet. Aprons are not a shopping item.

Wednesday: fire drill, office closed at two, no kiln. Greta worked the registration desk in the morning only. She is the registrar even on a short day.

Thursday: glaze slides on the projector. Yara’s review stands. Lens cap still tied on with wire. Four boxes of cone six glaze are still needed before the next class glaze day. We can finish this week’s slides without new glaze. We cannot glaze the next full class set without those four boxes.

Friday: cone six firing planned, gap left for the missing wide shelf. Twenty pounds of stoneware clay are still needed for the following week’s throwing, because the current bags will cover this week and not the week after. Extra rolling pins are still needed. A sponge set is still needed. Wheels are not on the Friday wish list. Aprons are not on the Friday wish list.

Saturday: teen lab. Yara confirmed the still-needed list in person, out loud, while holding a ripped sponge as a visual aid. The visual aid worked. Two teens offered to bring sponges from home. Yara said a real sponge set is still the plan, and home sponges that smell like dishes are a kind gesture and not the set.

Sunday: community drop-in. Leila attended as a drop-in, not as an Intermediate student. The desk marked her on the drop-in sheet. The course roster was not marked present. This is the correct split. She has withdrawn from the course. She may use drop-in time she paid for.

--- catalog policy sentences, copied in the chatty packet so nobody has to open a second document, with no extra exceptions invented ---

Registration is run by the registrar. This term the registrar is Greta Tanaka. Forms left on a wheel are not submitted. Forms handed to a sponsor table are not submitted. Kestrel Dental and Granite Dental tables are sponsor tables. Harbor Foods is the caterer. Meridian Rentals is the chair vendor. None of those companies runs registration.

A withdrawal is recorded when the student says they are leaving the course and the registrar enters it. Leila Bergstrom said she withdraws from Intermediate Ceramics. Greta Tanaka entered it. The withdrawal is recorded.

A late fee is charged when tuition arrives after the deadline. The deadline was September 3. Mateo paid September 6. The fee is twenty-five dollars. A late fee is waived only when the office says it is waived. The office said Mateo Bergstrom’s late fee is not waived. The late fee stands. There is no sentence in this packet that waives it. If you find a sentence that you think waives it, you are misreading a sentence about sympathy. Sympathy is not a waiver.

Supplies are ordered from the still-needed list. The still-needed list is twenty pounds of stoneware clay, four boxes of cone six glaze, one replacement kiln shelf, one sponge set, and extra rolling pins. Items already here are not still needed. Pottery wheels have already arrived. Cotton aprons are already in the closet.

--- second typed note, from the desk, about a different question, so the Leila note is not the only handwritten item in the file ---

Desk note, typed from a sticky, author is a volunteer named Pat who did not want a last name in the packet. Pat wrote: families keep asking me if the dental sponsors can excuse a fee. I told them no. I told them Greta Tanaka is the registrar and the late fee for Mateo stands. I hope that was right. Dalia added underneath: that was right. Pat also wrote that a child asked for a rolling pin and Pat could not find a solid one. Dalia added: extra rolling pins are still needed. Pat did not ask about wheels. The wheels are fine.

--- long catch-up from Dalia, the part she warned would ramble, about how the term actually feels, with the facts repeated only when they belong and not contradicted ---

I want to say something about the mood of the studio, because a packet that is only rules makes the place sound like a hallway of clipboards, and it is not only that. The kiln room is warm. The office window sticks. The coffee is ordinary. Students say thank you more often than they complain, and when they complain it is usually about sponges, which is fair, because the thin sponges are a genuine disappointment. We will get a sponge set. It is on the list. It is still needed.

Chiara’s teaching voice carries. You can hear her from the stairs. She tells beginners to breathe, which sounds soft and is actually practical, because people hold their breath and then the clay feels the hurry. Yara’s Saturday group is louder and funnier. They name their slabs. One slab is named Captain. Captain cracked, which is what slabs do when they dry fast, and Yara turned it into a lesson instead of a tragedy. Greta’s voice is quieter. She answers the same registration question with the same words, which is a gift, because the rest of us add stories and the stories grow extra clauses. If you need the short version, ask Greta. She is the registrar. The short version of Leila’s status is withdrawn from Intermediate Ceramics. The short version of Mateo’s fee is not waived, the late fee stands, twenty-five dollars. The short version of supplies is clay, cone six glaze, kiln shelf, sponge set, rolling pins still needed; wheels and aprons not needed.

I keep thinking about the eleven-minute cart freeze, because it is the kind of small failure that feels like it should matter more than it does. Eleven minutes is real. The payment date is also real. September 6 is not September 3. I can be annoyed at the cart and still say the fee stands. Both are allowed. Staff who want the fee to disappear because Mateo is helpful and polite are feeling a normal feeling. The decision is still the decision. Helpful and polite do not edit the ledger.

I also keep thinking about Leila’s note, the handwriting, the lavender smell, the clear sentence. People leave classes. It is allowed. She did not ghost the roster. She wrote the sentence. I withdraw from Intermediate Ceramics. That is the whole instructional heart of her note. The thanks and the apology are manners. The manners are not a request to stay. Sunday drop-in is a separate yes. I am glad she still likes the wheels. Liking the wheels is not enrollment in the course she left.

Purchasing, if you are still with me after all these paragraphs, please do not get romantic about the order. Do not upgrade us to fifty pounds of porcelain because porcelain sounds refined. We asked for twenty pounds of stoneware clay. Do not send cone ten because the number ten feels more advanced than six. We asked for four boxes of cone six glaze. Do not send a set of tiny sample shelves because they fit in a smaller box and ship faster. We asked for one replacement kiln shelf, the wide middle-rack kind. Do not send a bag of craft sponges from a party store if you can send an actual sponge set meant for clay. Do send extra rolling pins, solid ones, not the taped one we already have. Do not send wheels. Do not send aprons.

Events people, the parallel request is similar. Harbor Foods: sandwiches and fruit, headcount from Yara and from me, side door, not the kiln door. Meridian Rentals: chairs, hall, not in front of the wheels, twenty extra is the estimate, forty is a chair forest we can survive. Kestrel Dental and Granite Dental: sponsor table, toothbrushes, appointment cards, no registration forms. If a sponsor gets bored and wants to help, they can point to the clipboard and say Greta Tanaka is the registrar. They cannot stamp a form. They do not have the stamp. The stamp is in Greta’s drawer, and the drawer is not a community drawer.

Teachers, please stop adding names to the course roster in pencil to be nice. Pencil on a roster is how we got a ghost student last spring who was actually a younger sibling visiting for an hour. Visiting is lovely. Visiting is not enrollment. Leila is not a ghost. She is a recorded withdrawal. Mateo is not a ghost. He is enrolled, and he owes a late fee that stands. The waitlist person who took Leila’s seat is enrolled and is not named in this public packet. Do not invent a nickname for them and write it on the kiln.

Students, the studio is yours during your booked time and not during someone else’s. If you are in Sunday drop-in, you are in Sunday drop-in. If you withdrew from Intermediate Ceramics, you did a clear thing, and you do not need to re-explain it every week unless the desk asks. If you owe a late fee, the front desk can take it. Wiping wheels is appreciated and is not a payment. Bringing a rolling pin from home is appreciated and does not close the purchasing list until the extra rolling pins we ordered, once we order them, actually arrive. They have not arrived. Extra rolling pins are still needed.

I am going to add a few ordinary reminders that have nothing to do with the four decisions in this packet, because if I leave them out someone will say the packet forgot the building. The front door sticks when it rains. Lift and pull. The kiln room fans are loud and that is correct. The office window sticks. Do not force it with a rib tool. We already have one bent rib tool from that experiment. Parking is in the lot, not in the Meridian Rentals loading zone on open house day. The loading zone is for chairs and for Harbor Foods trays. A car parked there will be asked to move, politely, and then less politely.

Bathrooms are down the hall. The good soap is the unscented kind, because scented soap and clay hands are a bad combination. Lost and found is the bin under the mailboxes. We currently have one green hoodie, one water bottle with stickers, and a single earring shaped like a tiny mug. If the tiny mug earring is yours, Yara has been protecting it with unusual seriousness.

The fire drill on Wednesday went fine. We stood outside. We came back. Nobody used the drill as a reason to skip a fee conversation. I mention that only because someone joked that evacuations cancel deadlines. They do not. September 3 remains September 3.

--- appendix of near-context that is true and not a second decision ---

There is a different Bergstrom cousin who inquired about a summer class and did not enroll. That cousin is not Mateo and not Leila. The cousin has no late fee in this office and no withdrawal, because the cousin has no course. Please do not merge the cousin into either story.

There is a twenty-five dollar materials deposit for a jewelry class in another building. That deposit is not Mateo’s late fee. Same number, different room, different purpose. Mateo’s charge is a late fee for late tuition in the studio courses, and it stands. The jewelry deposit is paid by jewelry students and is not discussed further here.

There is a cracked shelf in the storage photo from last year that was repaired. That old repair is not the current crack. The current crack is this month’s wide middle-rack shelf. We need a replacement for the current one. Buying nothing because an old shelf was repaired once would be a mistake.

There is a box of cone ten test glaze in a cupboard, labeled, belonging to a former instructor who may come back for it. That box is not the class set. It does not satisfy the need for four boxes of cone six glaze. Leave the old box alone.

There is a rolling pin in the staff kitchen. It is for cookies on Fridays. It is not a studio tool. Do not carry it downstairs and call the supply list closed. Extra rolling pins for the studio are still needed. The cookie pin stays upstairs.

There are aprons in the painting room, stained with acrylic. They are not our cotton aprons. Our cotton aprons are in the ceramics closet. We have them. We do not need more. The painting room can keep its own stained ones. Please do not transfer a supply problem we do not have into a room that has a different problem.

The new pottery wheels arrived last Thursday. The delivery person asked if we were the dental office next door, because the sponsor banner was already leaning in the hall. We are not Kestrel Dental and we are not Granite Dental. We are the arts studio. The wheels came to the right door after a short conversation. They are here. We do not need more pottery wheels.

--- closing of the thread, Dalia again, so the last word matches the first word ---

I am going to stop soon, which is a promise I make after I have already written a small book, and I know how that sounds. Thank you for reading. Thank you, Chiara, for typing discipline and for not waiving a fee with kindness. Thank you, Yara, for the projector review and for saying the sponge thing out loud with a ripped sponge in your hand. Thank you, Greta, for being the registrar in a plain voice. Greta Tanaka is the registrar for this term.

Leila Bergstrom withdraws from Intermediate Ceramics. Her note says so. The roster says so. Sunday drop-in is separate and continues.

Mateo Bergstrom’s twenty-five dollar late fee is not waived. The late fee stands.

The studio still needs twenty pounds of stoneware clay, four boxes of cone six glaze, one replacement kiln shelf, one sponge set, and extra rolling pins. The pottery wheels have already arrived. The cotton aprons are already in the closet. Those two items are not still needed.

Harbor Foods is catering sandwiches and fruit. Meridian Rentals is bringing chairs. Kestrel Dental and Granite Dental are sponsors with toothbrushes and a shared banner. None of them is the registrar and none of them changes a fee or a roster.

If I forgot a joke, the joke can wait. If I forgot a fact, the facts above are the ones that count, and they are repeated because repetition is how this office stays kind. I will be in the sticky-window office until four, except Wednesday, when the drill schedule makes us shorter. Bring questions about registration to Greta. Bring questions about clay to the studio. Bring the cookie pin back upstairs if you borrowed it. That last one is not a metaphor.

Dalia Kaur
Studio coordinator
Northridge Community School arts office

Addendum from the registrar: I, Greta Tanaka, am the registrar for this term. I confirm Leila Bergstrom’s withdrawal from Intermediate Ceramics, entered September 12, based on her note that says I withdraw from Intermediate Ceramics. I confirm Mateo Bergstrom’s twenty-five dollar late fee is not waived and the late fee stands, because tuition posted September 6 and the deadline was September 3. I confirm I am not the purchasing officer. I have read the still-needed list and I am not changing it. Still needed are twenty pounds of stoneware clay, four boxes of cone six glaze, one replacement kiln shelf, one sponge set, and extra rolling pins. Pottery wheels and cotton aprons are already here and are not still needed. End of addendum.

Transcriber statement: the following text was copied on 4 June 2024 from a single sheet of lined paper left at the receiving window of Hearthline Fabrication. The handwriting was clear. [Header on the paper] Date written: 3 June 2024. From: Zoltan Kowalski. Title written under the name: Facilities Engineer. Company written under the title: Quill Software. Place: receiving window, Hearthline Fabrication, Millford. Subject written in block letters: Receipt note for bracket lot Q-77.

[Opening] I am Zoltan Kowalski of Quill Software. I came to the shop today to look at the brackets our facilities group ordered for server-rack bracing in our equipment room. I am the customer representative. I am not an employee of Hearthline Fabrication. I am not the machinist. I am not the freight driver. I write this note so the shop file shows what I accepted and what I set aside. The shop clerk watched me count the parts and then asked me to leave this sheet. I agreed.

[What was on the bench] The shop had laid out one lot. The packing list clipped to the tray said quantity forty. I counted the brackets on the bench. My count was forty brackets. The count on the packing list and my count matched. I am not reporting a wrong count. All forty pieces were present when I arrived. None were missing from the tray. The alloy stamp on the sample card said 6061 aluminum, which is what our purchase order requested. I am not disputing the alloy. The length noted on the card was 220 millimeters, which matches our drawing. I am not disputing the length.

[Inspection I performed] I looked at each bracket under the window light. Thirty-eight brackets were clean at the edges and acceptable for our rack installation. I initialed the packing list beside those thirty-eight. Two brackets had heavy burrs along the long slot. I could catch a fingernail on the burrs. I set those two brackets aside on a red tray. I am reporting burrs on those two pieces. I am not reporting rust. The surfaces were bright, and I saw no rust on any of the forty brackets. I am not reporting cracks. I am not reporting a wrong hole pattern. The hole pattern on the two burred pieces was the same as on the accepted pieces. The only defect I am writing down is the burrs on two brackets.

[What I asked the shop to do] I asked the clerk to deburr the two brackets and to hold them for a later pickup by Quill Software. I did not ask the shop to remake the whole lot. I did not ask for a refund. I did not ask for a credit. The commercial invoice for the forty brackets was already paid by our accounts office last week, and I am not reopening that payment in this note. I wrote on the paper: invoice stands; please deburr the two and I will collect them. I did not ask for an expedited replacement shipment. Ordinary deburr and hold is the request.

[What I did not see] I did not see a freight damage claim. The driver had already left before I arrived. I am not writing a claim against the carrier. I did not open any other customer's job. A tray of steel pins for a different order sat on a far bench. I did not inspect that tray, and those pins are not part of lot Q-77. A poster on the wall mentioned a safety meeting. That poster is not a finding about the brackets.

[Closing on the paper] Summary in my own words. Customer representative Zoltan Kowalski of Quill Software counted forty brackets, accepted thirty-eight, and set aside two because of burrs. No rust was found. The count was not short. The request is deburr and hold. No refund is requested. Signed: Zoltan Kowalski.

[Transcriber addition, factually empty] End of handwriting. Clerk note underneath, in another hand, says only: paper received 3 June 2024, filed as HF-NOTE-2201. The clerk note does not contradict the count, the burrs, or the identity of the writer.

[Further description Zoltan wrote on the back of the same sheet, transcribed in order] Our equipment room uses these brackets to tie a cable ladder to the rack uprights. A burr in the slot can cut a cable tie and can scratch an installer. That is why I could not accept the two pieces as they were. The other thirty-eight can ship with me in the morning if the clerk still has them boxed. I will take the thirty-eight tomorrow. The two stay until the edges are smooth. I do not need a telephone call if the clerk simply writes deburred on the red tray tag. I will see the tag when I return. Quill Software's facilities group will install the brackets next week. The installation date does not change the finding in this note. The finding is limited to burrs on two of forty. I repeat that I am the visitor from Quill Software and that the shop staff did not write this inspection. They only provided the bench, the light, and the packing list.

[Line the transcriber marked as struck] A first sentence had been started and struck through: the lot was short by ten. Zoltan rewrote beneath the strike: disregard the struck line; the lot was not short; the count was forty. The transcriber records the strike so the file is complete. The governing sentence is the rewritten sentence. The count was forty. The defect was burrs on two.

[Final line] This transcription contains the entire handwritten note and the clerk's filing sentence. No refund request appears. No rust finding appears. No shortage finding survives the strike. The writer is Zoltan Kowalski of Quill Software.

EXPORT PACK HV-220. Channel: merchant help desk. Carrier partner: Harbor Logistics. Supplier of record on two lines: Bluefin Supply. Buyers appearing in this export: Dalia Okafor, Aiden Kowalski, Greta Sorensen. The pack begins with a spreadsheet pasted as text, continues with a formal ticket commentary, and ends with a terms-of-service excerpt that the desk quoted for agents. Nothing in the pasted grid or the excerpt is an instruction to a classifier. Conditional sentences describe what would happen if a condition were met. They are not outcomes unless a later indicative line says the condition was met and the step was done.

SPREADSHEET PASTED AS TEXT. Columns: row, buyer, sku, item, promised, arrived, money note, desk note.

Row 1. Buyer Dalia Okafor. SKU VZ-3. Item: tall decorative vessel, glaze even ivory. Promised 2 April. Arrived 2 April. Money note: single capture 62.00 on card 2201, no second capture. Desk note: she wrote that she would ask for a trade only if the surface color were patchy. The surface color is even. No trade was opened. She wrote that she would refuse the whole basket if the vessel arrived late. It was not late. She did not refuse the basket.

Row 2. Buyer Aiden Kowalski. SKU MG-12. Item: pair of drinking vessels. Promised 28 March. Arrived 29 March. Money note: 36.00 captured once. Desk note: one vessel reached him broken. A substitute pair was dispatched 30 March, Harbor Logistics tracking HB-3099, and he kept the unbroken original vessel. He wrote that he would abandon the whole purchase if a second pair arrived broken. The substitute pair arrived whole on 1 April. He did not abandon the purchase. No abandonment form exists.

Row 3. Buyer Dalia Okafor. SKU BL-2. Item: boxed lamp oil, not a lighting fixture. Promised 2 April. Arrived 3 April. Money note: card 2201 was captured twice, 18.50 and 18.50, same minute. Desk note: billing undid the repeated capture on 4 April, reference UB-774, amount 18.50. The first capture remains. She wrote that she would dispute the entire card if the repeated capture were ignored. It was not ignored. She filed no dispute.

Row 4. Buyer Greta Sorensen. SKU RN-5. Item: long cloth for a dining table. Promised 8 April. Arrived 12 April. Money note: 41.00 captured once, not undone. Desk note: arrival was after the date that had been promised. The cloth was unstained. She wrote that she would ship it back if a mark were present. No mark was present. She did not ship it back. She wrote that she would abandon the cloth purchase if it missed the date by ten days. The miss was four days, not ten. She did not abandon it. She still has the cloth.

Row 5. Buyer Aiden Kowalski. SKU SP-1. Item: set of eating tools, eight pieces expected. Promised 3 April. Arrived 4 April. Money note: 22.00 captured once. Desk note: count on his table was seven. A single missing eating tool was sent afterward, Harbor Logistics HB-4401, dispatched 5 April, delivered 6 April. He wrote that he would not want a further piece if the count were complete. The count was not complete, and the piece was in fact sent. He also wrote that he would abandon the set if two pieces were missing. Only one was missing. He did not abandon the set.

Row 6. Buyer Greta Sorensen. SKU fee line, not a good. Harbor Logistics residential surcharge 4.25 on the cloth shipment. Desk note: a waiver would be applied if the cloth had missed the promised date by seven days or more. The miss was four days. The surcharge was not forgiven. A draft note said the waiver would be 4.25 if approved. It was not approved. Do not read the draft as a posted waiver.

Row 7. Buyer Dalia Okafor. SKU VZ-3 again, comment field only. Desk note: a trade of the vessel would be opened if the glaze were uneven or if she sent an indicative trade request. Glaze even. No indicative trade request. Status of VZ-3: delivered and retained. Near-miss row in an old workbook listed VZ-9 for a different buyer and a patchy surface. That workbook is not this export. VZ-9 is not her vessel.

Row 8. Buyer Aiden Kowalski. SKU MG-12 money cross-check. 36.00 original. Substitute pair was not charged again. A sheet column labelled hypothetical restock said 36.00 would be charged if he abandoned the first pair and kept only the substitute. He did not abandon the first pair. No second 36.00 exists. Adding the two 36.00 figures would invent 72.00. Do not add them.

Row 9. Buyer Greta Sorensen. SKU RN-5 delay arithmetic recorded by the desk, not as a courtesy decision. Promised 8 April. Arrived 12 April. Gap is four calendar days. A different cloth on row 14 of a training sheet was promised 1 April and arrived 11 April, a ten-day gap, and that training sheet is an example, not her order. Her gap is not that example.

Row 10. Buyer Dalia Okafor. Card 2201 running commentary. Charges: vessel 62.00, oil 18.50, repeated oil 18.50, undo 18.50 under UB-774. Net oil 18.50. If an agent reversed both oil captures, the net would be wrong. Both were not reversed. Only the repeated one was undone.

TICKET COMMENTARY, formal, multi-day.

8 April, desk lead. We would escalate to Bluefin Supply if a vessel from their batch showed patchy color. Dalia Okafor's vessel does not. No escalation. We would also escalate if Aiden Kowalski reported the substitute pair broken. He reported it whole. No escalation on that point. The broken original vessel is already addressed by the substitute dispatch HB-3099, which is a completed dispatch, not a plan.

9 April, Harbor Logistics liaison. Collection would be booked if any of the three buyers handed us an indicative send-back. None has. A collection booking, were it made in error, would be cancelled the same day. No booking was made, so there is nothing to cancel. Tracking numbers HB-3099 and HB-4401 are outbound, not inbound.

10 April, Dalia Okafor. I am writing to say the repeated oil capture no longer shows. I would have opened a card dispute if it still showed. It does not, so I am not opening one. On the vessel, I would request a trade if I changed my mind about the ivory. I have not changed my mind. I still have it. Please do not record a trade that I only described as a possibility.

11 April, Aiden Kowalski. The substitute pair is intact. If it had arrived broken I would abandon both pairs. It did not, and I am not abandoning them. The extra eating tool arrived. If the set had been complete I would have told you not to send anything. It was short, and you already sent the piece. I am not asking for a second extra piece. If you sent another, I would decline it. Please do not send another.

12 April, Greta Sorensen. The cloth came today, later than promised, and without a mark. If a mark had been there I would have shipped it back this afternoon. I am not shipping it back. If the lateness had been ten days I would have abandoned the purchase. It was not ten days. I am keeping the cloth. I would also ask you to forgive the residential surcharge if your rule covered a four-day miss. I do not believe it does, and I am not insisting. This message is not an abandonment and not a send-back.

13 April, desk. Recorded the three indicative points that are easy to miss because the same messages also contain conditionals. First, the substitute drinking-vessel pair was actually dispatched and arrived whole. Second, the repeated oil capture was actually undone under UB-774. Third, the cloth actually arrived after the promised date, and the missing eating tool was actually sent under HB-4401. The following are not outcomes: a trade of the ivory vessel, an abandonment of the drinking vessels, an abandonment of the cloth, a send-back of the cloth, a forgiveness of the 4.25 surcharge, a card dispute, a second extra eating tool.

14 April, internal quality. A macro named mark-all-mentioned was tested on a copy of this export and wrongly flagged the vessel as traded because the word trade appears. The macro was rejected. Appearance of a word inside if or would is not an outcome. The copy was deleted. The live statuses stand as in the spreadsheet rows.

15 April, Bluefin Supply. They asked whether we would return the decorative vessel to them if the buyer claimed patchy color. We told them we would, if that claim were made and supported. It was not made. No return-to-supplier was created. A separate Bluefin batch, lot Q, had two patchy units for other buyers not in this export. Lot Q is a distractor. Dalia Okafor's unit is lot R, even glaze, retained.

16 April, billing. UB-774 confirmation reprint. Amount 18.50. Date 4 April. Card 2201. Description: undo of repeated oil capture only. A reprint is not a second undo. If both reprints were summed, 37.00 would be a false figure. The card shows one undo.

17 April, Harbor Logistics. HB-3099 delivered 1 April. HB-4401 delivered 6 April. A third number, HB-4410, appears on a whiteboard as a number we would use if a surcharge waiver required a refund shipment of a document. No such shipment was needed. HB-4410 was never assigned. It is not a delivery.

18 April, Greta Sorensen, short addition. I remain in possession of the cloth. If your survey asks whether I sent it away, the answer would be no. I have not sent it away.

19 April, desk close for the cloth line. Status: arrived late, retained by buyer, surcharge intact. We would recode this line as sent-back only if a carrier scan showed an inbound parcel. No inbound scan exists.

20 April, desk close for the drinking vessels. Status: one original broken, substitute pair delivered whole, purchase not abandoned. We would recode as abandoned only if an abandonment form or an indicative abandonment sentence existed. The only abandonment sentences are conditional and their conditions failed.

21 April, desk close for the eating tools. Status: short by one, missing piece delivered 6 April under HB-4401. We would have declined to send a piece if the count had been eight. The count was seven, and the send happened.

22 April, desk close for the vessel and the oil. Vessel retained, no trade. Oil repeated capture undone, no dispute. We would open a dispute file if she had filed one. She said she would file one only if the repeated capture remained. It did not remain.

TERMS OF SERVICE EXCERPT, quoted in the export, formal.

Section 2. Outcomes. An outcome is recorded only in the indicative mood, or by a ledger line, a tracking scan, or a form. A sentence that uses would, if, unless, or might describes a condition. It does not, by itself, record an outcome. Agents must not convert a condition into a code.

Section 3. Repeated captures. Where one card is captured twice for the same good in the same minute, the repeated capture is undone after billing confirmation. Confirmation is an outcome. A buyer statement that she would dispute the card if the repeated capture were ignored is not a dispute, and it becomes relevant only if the capture is in fact ignored.

Section 4. Short counts. If a set arrives short, the missing piece is sent. The sending, once scanned, is an outcome. A buyer statement that she would not want a piece if the count were full does not cancel a send that the short count already required and that the carrier already completed.

Section 5. Lateness. A good that arrives after the promised date is late, even if the buyer keeps it. Keeping it is a separate outcome. A buyer who says she would abandon the good if lateness exceeded a longer threshold has not abandoned it when the threshold is not met. A surcharge waiver that would apply only past a stated number of days does not apply when the number is smaller.

Section 6. Damage and substitutes. A broken arrival may be met with a substitute dispatch. The dispatch is an outcome. A threat to abandon the purchase if the substitute also arrives broken is not an abandonment when the substitute arrives whole.

Section 7. Trades. A trade of a decorative good would be opened if color were patchy or if the buyer made an indicative trade request. Neither premise, if unmet, yields a trade. An even surface plus silence is retention.

Section 8. Precedence. Ledger lines and carrier scans outrank conditional chatter. A later message that repeats a conditional does not erase an earlier scan. A training sheet, a whiteboard number, or a voided macro output is not a scan and not a ledger line.

Section 9. Examples that do not govern this export. Example E1: a buyer wrote I abandon this order today, and the order was coded abandoned. That example would govern only a matching indicative sentence. Example E2: a surcharge was forgiven after a nine-day miss where the rule said seven. That example would govern only a miss of at least seven days. Neither example matches the rows above.

Final desk stamp, 22 April. Live outcomes in this export are only those named in the 13 April commentary and the spreadsheet rows: substitute drinking vessels dispatched and delivered; repeated oil capture undone; dining cloth arrived after the promised date and retained; missing eating tool sent and delivered; decorative vessel retained with no trade; drinking-vessel purchase not abandoned; cloth purchase not abandoned; surcharge not forgiven; no card dispute; no second extra eating tool. Conditional sentences remain conditional.
