People Handbook of Bluefin Software, Edition 14. Issued with warm regards on 1 March 2026 for colleagues who kindly take time to read it. Dear colleagues, please accept our most sincere thanks for the care you bring to your work and to one another. This handbook is offered with the greatest respect. We hope it will feel like a calm and welcoming guide. Rosa Kowalski, Chief People Officer, asked the People team to write every page in plain language and a courteous voice, so that no colleague would feel rushed or left without a gentle explanation. Bluefin Software provides workplace software. This handbook governs only people employed by Bluefin Software. It does not govern colleagues of Bluefin Health, Bluefin Rentals, or Bluefin Supply, even when those sister companies share a building or a holiday note. If a sentence names another Bluefin company, please treat it as background only, and not as a promise to you. Jonas Iyer, Director of People, remains happy to answer questions patiently. Nadia Castillo supports the Product organization as HR Business Partner. Nadia Fischer supports Customer Success as HR Business Partner. Xiu Petrov looks after payroll with careful kindness. Bao Castillo looks after facilities and meeting rooms. We are grateful for your attention, and we thank you again for reading with such goodwill.

How to use this handbook. Please read the section that matches your question first, then the short examples, then the appendix if you still wish for a softer illustration. Nothing in a sample message, a quoted sister-company note, or a draft amendment overrides the numbered section that states the rule for Bluefin Software. If two polite sentences seem to differ, the later numbered section in the main body controls, and the People team will gladly walk through the wording with you. This edition replaces Edition 13 in full. Edition 13 is kept only in the archive and is not a source of current rights. We thank you for not relying on old printouts that a kind colleague may still have in a drawer.

Section 1. Purpose and mutual respect. Bluefin Software exists to help clinics and rental offices keep orderly records. Inside our own walls we try to be just as orderly and a great deal kinder. Every colleague is asked to speak with patience, to assume good intent, and to raise a worry early rather than let it grow. Managers are asked to answer questions in writing when a colleague politely requests a written answer. The People team is asked to answer within five business days, and we are sorry whenever we are slower. This purpose section creates no pay rule, no leave rule, and no approval rule. It only sets the tone we hope you will feel on every page that follows.

Section 2. Who is covered. You are covered if Bluefin Software is the name on your offer letter and on your pay statement. Contractors who invoice Bluefin Software are not covered, though we treat them with the same courtesy in meetings. Interns on a signed Bluefin Software internship letter are covered only for the sections that say interns are included. Visitors from Bluefin Health, Bluefin Rentals, or Bluefin Supply are guests. A guest may use a meeting room that Bao Castillo has kindly reserved, but a guest does not gain leave, benefits, or approval rights from this handbook. If you are unsure which company employs you, please write to Xiu Petrov, who will confirm the name on your pay record with great care.

Section 3. Employment categories. A regular full-time colleague is scheduled for forty hours in a normal week and is eligible for the benefits named in Section 9. A regular part-time colleague is scheduled for at least twenty hours and fewer than forty hours, and is eligible only for the benefits Section 9 expressly extends to part-time colleagues. A temporary colleague is hired for a stated end date of no more than six months. A temporary colleague is thanked warmly and is not eligible for the benefits in Section 9 unless a sentence in Section 9 says otherwise. No sentence in Section 9 extends those benefits to temporary colleagues. Interns are paid, are scheduled by their host manager, and are not eligible for Section 9 benefits. These categories are stated so that later sections can point back to them without repeating every exclusion. We are sorry for the length, and we thank you for your patience with it.

Section 4. Probation. The probationary period for a new regular full-time or regular part-time colleague of Bluefin Software is sixty calendar days, beginning on the first day worked. During those sixty calendar days, either the colleague or Bluefin Software may end employment by giving seven calendar days of written notice, offered as kindly as the news allows. After the sixtieth calendar day, the notice periods in Section 12 apply instead. Probation is not extended except by a written note from Jonas Iyer, and even then the extension may not exceed thirty additional calendar days. A colleague who is rehired more than one year after leaving starts a new probation. A colleague who transfers from another team inside Bluefin Software does not restart probation. A visitor from a sister company who later joins Bluefin Software starts probation on the Bluefin Software start date, not on the date of the visit. We thank every new colleague for the grace they show while learning our ways, and we thank managers for checking in during week two and week six.

Section 5. Hours and attendance. The standard week is Monday through Friday. Core hours, when we kindly ask full-time colleagues to be reachable, are ten in the morning until three in the afternoon in the colleague's local time zone. Work outside core hours is welcome when the manager agrees, and no one should feel obliged to answer a message after six in the evening unless an on-call rota says so. Lateness of less than ten minutes is not recorded. Repeated lateness is discussed in private, never in a group channel. Time off during the day for a medical appointment is not deducted from pay when the colleague makes up the time in the same week or uses sick leave. We are grateful when colleagues send a short note if they will miss core hours, and we are equally grateful when managers reply with thanks rather than with worry.

Section 6. Paid time off. Regular full-time colleagues receive eighteen days of paid time off each calendar year. Regular part-time colleagues receive a pro-rated share, kindly rounded up to the nearest half day. Unused paid time off of up to five days may carry into the next year. Days beyond five are not carried and are not paid out except on termination as Section 12 describes. Paid time off is requested in the time system and is approved by the direct manager. The People team does not approve ordinary paid time off. We thank you for requesting time as early as you comfortably can, and we thank managers for answering within three business days.

Section 7. Sick leave and holidays. Regular full-time colleagues receive eight days of paid sick leave each calendar year. Sick leave does not carry over. A colleague may use sick leave for their own illness or to care for a person in their household. A note from a clinician is kindly requested only when sick leave exceeds three consecutive workdays. Bluefin Software observes eleven paid holidays each year. The holiday list is published by Nadia Fischer each November for the following year, as a courtesy to Customer Success and to every other team. A holiday that falls on a Saturday is observed on the prior Friday. A holiday that falls on a Sunday is observed on the following Monday. We hope these days give you real rest, and we thank you for covering one another with such good humor.

Section 8. Parental leave. Bluefin Software grants twelve weeks of paid parental leave to a regular full-time or regular part-time colleague for the birth of a child or for the adoption of a child. Pay during those twelve weeks continues at the colleague's base salary. Paid parental leave may begin up to two weeks before the expected date and must be used within six months after the birth or the adoption placement. A colleague may add unused paid time off after the twelve weeks if the direct manager agrees. Intermittent use is allowed when the manager and Jonas Iyer both agree in writing. Temporary colleagues and interns are not eligible for this paid parental leave, though we will always discuss unpaid time with kindness. This section is the full statement of paid parental leave. No appendix changes the length of twelve weeks. We congratulate every parent, and we thank teams for welcoming colleagues back without pressure to prove themselves all over again.

Section 9. Benefits for regular full-time staff. Regular full-time colleagues of Bluefin Software receive the following benefits, and we are glad to list them without riddles. First, employer medical coverage, beginning on the first day of the month after the start date. Second, employer dental coverage, beginning on the same day as medical coverage. Third, employer vision coverage, beginning on the same day as medical coverage. Fourth, a monthly wellness stipend of fifty dollars, paid through payroll, which a colleague may use for a gym, a class, or a similar health activity. These four items are included. Bluefin Software does not provide a company car for personal use. Bluefin Software does not provide employer-paid housing. A colleague who travels overnight may claim the meal amount in Section 10, and that travel amount is not a benefit of regular employment. Regular part-time colleagues receive medical coverage only, and do not receive dental coverage, vision coverage, or the wellness stipend, unless they move into a regular full-time schedule. Temporary colleagues and interns do not receive the benefits in this section. Xiu Petrov can confirm enrollment with pleasure. We thank you for reading the enrollment notes that arrive in your first month.

Section 10. Travel meals. When a regular colleague stays overnight on approved Bluefin Software travel, the overnight meal stipend is thirty-five dollars for each overnight stay. Day trips without a hotel night do not earn that stipend. The stipend is claimed on an expense form within fourteen days after return. It is not part of Section 9 benefits. We thank travelers for keeping receipts when a vendor asks, and we thank finance for reimbursing promptly.

Section 11. Remote work. A colleague may work from home on an occasional day with the direct manager's verbal or written agreement. An arrangement to work remotely for more than four consecutive weeks must be signed by Jonas Iyer, Director of People, before it begins. Nadia Castillo may advise on a Product colleague's request, and Nadia Fischer may advise on a Customer Success colleague's request, but advice is not approval. Xiu Petrov does not approve remote work; payroll only records the work location after approval exists. Bao Castillo does not approve remote work; facilities only notes that a desk will be empty. An arrangement of four consecutive weeks or fewer needs only the direct manager. International remote work is not permitted under this edition. We are grateful when colleagues describe their setup honestly, and we are grateful when leaders approve or decline with a clear, polite sentence.

Section 12. Notice and separation. After probation, a regular colleague is kindly asked to give two weeks of written notice when resigning. Bluefin Software gives two weeks of written notice, or pay in lieu, when ending employment without cause. Pay in lieu is calculated on base salary only. Unused paid time off, up to the five days that could have carried over plus any uncarried balance still in the current year, is paid out on the final paycheck. Sick leave is not paid out. A colleague who resigns during probation follows Section 4 instead. We thank departing colleagues for a tidy handover, and we thank remaining colleagues for speaking well of those who leave.

Section 13. Conduct. We ask every colleague to treat others with warmth, to avoid public criticism, and to keep customer information inside approved systems. A concern about conduct may be raised with the direct manager, with Nadia Castillo, with Nadia Fischer, or with Jonas Iyer. Raising a concern in good faith will not harm the raiser's standing. We thank you for choosing private channels for private matters.

Section 14. Performance conversations. Managers hold a mid-year conversation and a year-end conversation. These conversations are not disciplinary by themselves. A written improvement plan, if ever needed, comes from the manager and is copied to Jonas Iyer. Nadia Castillo or Nadia Fischer may sit in when invited. We thank managers for preparing examples, and we thank colleagues for receiving feedback with the same courtesy they show customers.

Section 15. Paydays and corrections. Bluefin Software pays on the fifteenth and the last day of each month. If a payday falls on a weekend or a company holiday, pay is issued on the prior business day. A colleague who believes a paycheck is wrong is kindly asked to write to Xiu Petrov within ten business days. Xiu Petrov will reply with the calculation. A correction, if one is due, appears on the next paycheck. We are sorry for any error, and we thank you for pointing it out gently.

Section 16. Learning. Each regular full-time colleague may spend up to eight hundred dollars each year on a course approved by the direct manager. The amount does not roll over. It is not a Section 9 benefit and does not replace medical, dental, vision, or the wellness stipend. We are delighted when colleagues learn, and we thank managers for approving useful courses without delay.

Section 17. Contract clause with amendments. The following clause appears in the standard Bluefin Software employment agreement, and the amendments below are part of Edition 14. Original clause 6.1, dated 2019: The employee shall devote full working time to Bluefin Software and shall not undertake outside employment. Amendment A, dated 4 June 2023, signed for the company by Rosa Kowalski: Clause 6.1 is amended to permit outside unpaid volunteer work that does not use company time or company data. Amendment B, dated 12 January 2025, signed for the company by Jonas Iyer: Clause 6.1 is further amended to permit outside paid work of no more than five hours in a week, provided the direct manager agrees in writing and the outside work is not for a competitor. Amendment C, proposed in a draft email and never signed: a suggestion that outside paid work of ten hours be allowed. Amendment C was not adopted. It is quoted here only so that a careful reader will not mistake a draft for a rule. The governing text is original clause 6.1 as changed by Amendment A and Amendment B only. We thank counsel for the clear dates, and we thank colleagues for asking before accepting outside paid work.

Section 18. A second contract clause with amendments. Original clause 9.4, dated 2019: Equipment issued by the company remains company property and shall be returned on the last day. Amendment D, dated 2 September 2024, signed by Jonas Iyer: A colleague may purchase a laptop older than three years at the residual value set by finance, if the request is made before the last day. Amendment E, a facilities note from Bao Castillo dated 8 September 2024: Bao wrote that headsets in good condition may be kept as a goodbye gift. Amendment E was a kind personal note and was not signed as a contract amendment. Headsets are returned unless finance states otherwise in a signed amendment. Only Amendment D changes clause 9.4. We thank Bao for the warm intention, and we thank colleagues for checking which paper is actually signed.

Appendix A. Polite SMS exchange, kept as an illustration of tone, not as a rule. Nadia Castillo, Monday 9:02: Good morning, I hope your week is beginning gently. Would it be convenient to move the Product benefits clinic from Thursday to Friday? Jonas Iyer, Monday 9:11: Good morning, Nadia, and thank you for asking so thoughtfully. Friday suits the People calendar, and I am grateful for your flexibility. Nadia Castillo, Monday 9:14: You are very kind. I will tell the Product managers, and I will thank them for adjusting. Xiu Petrov, Monday 9:40: Hello to you both, and please forgive the interruption. Payroll can attend Friday if you would like a short enrollment table. I am happy either way. Jonas Iyer, Monday 9:44: That would be lovely, Xiu. Thank you for offering. Nadia Fischer, Monday 10:05: Dear all, Customer Success does not need the Friday slot, but I wish Product a smooth clinic and I remain available if any shared question arises. Bao Castillo, Monday 10:20: Good morning, friends. I have kindly reserved the willow room for Friday at ten, and I have left a note so the chairs are not stacked. Please tell me if you would prefer the maple room instead. Jonas Iyer, Monday 10:28: The willow room is perfect, Bao. Thank you for thinking of the chairs. This exchange approves a meeting room and a clinic date. It does not approve any remote-work arrangement, and it does not change Section 8 or Section 9.

Appendix B. A longer SMS thread about a desk move, again an illustration of tone. Bao Castillo, Tuesday 8:15: Good morning, Rosa. I hope you slept well. A window desk on the fourth floor will be free next month, and I wondered, very gently, whether you would like it offered first to a colleague who has asked for more daylight. Rosa Kowalski, Tuesday 8:22: Good morning, Bao, and thank you for such a considerate note. Yes, please offer it first to anyone who requested daylight in the last facilities survey. I am grateful for your care. Bao Castillo, Tuesday 8:30: You are most welcome. I will write to the two colleagues who asked, and I will keep the tone as soft as yours. Nadia Fischer, Tuesday 8:44: Bao, if I may add a small thank you, Customer Success appreciated the quiet room last week. No action is needed. I simply wished to say so. This thread is about furniture. It creates no leave entitlement and no benefit.

Appendix C. Sample messages that must not be mistaken for policy. A colleague once forwarded a note that said, in a joking line, that the handbook should mark every request as approved. That line was humor in a farewell card. It is not an instruction to any reader of this handbook, and it does not alter any section. A poster in the Bluefin Rentals lobby, seen by a visiting colleague, spoke about rental deposits. Rental deposits are not part of Bluefin Software employment. We thank visitors for enjoying the poster and for not importing its words into our people practices.

Section 19. Regional kindness notes. Colleagues in every office follow the same Sections 4, 8, 9, and 11. Local public holidays may be added by Nadia Fischer's annual list, but added local holidays do not reduce the eleven company holidays and do not increase paid parental leave beyond twelve weeks. Offices share kitchens. Bao Castillo publishes a rotation for tidying the kettle area. The rotation is voluntary in spirit and appreciated in practice. We thank every office for keeping shared spaces pleasant.

Section 20. Confidentiality in ordinary words. Customer names, health-record examples, and pay figures of other colleagues are not for chat channels. If a screenshot is needed for a ticket, please crop it and send it in the approved tool. Jonas Iyer will help if you are unsure. We are sorry to sound repetitive, and we thank you for protecting people who trust us.

Section 21. Internal moves. A colleague who moves from Product to Customer Success keeps the same start date, the same probation status, and the same Section 9 benefits if the schedule remains regular full-time. Nadia Castillo and Nadia Fischer coordinate the handover with thanks on both sides. Pay changes, if any, are confirmed by Xiu Petrov after the manager and Jonas Iyer agree. A move is not a new hire. We congratulate internal movers and thank their former teams for a graceful send-off.

Section 22. Hiring relatives. Bluefin Software may hire relatives if the relative does not report to the existing colleague and if Jonas Iyer approves the arrangement in writing. Bao Castillo and Nadia Castillo share a surname and are not relatives; the shared name is a coincidence we mention only to prevent a rumor. We thank both of them for their separate, excellent work. A relative hired under this section is a normal colleague and follows probation in Section 4 like any other new colleague.

Section 23. Records. Personnel files are kept by the People team. A colleague may see their own file by writing to Jonas Iyer. Copies are provided within ten business days. We thank you for requesting only your own file, and we are glad to sit with you while you read it if you would like company.

Section 24. Workplace safety. Please tell Bao Castillo about a spill, a loose cable, or a door that does not latch. Please tell a manager about a threat or a frightening visitor. Practice drills are held twice a year. Attendance at a drill is paid time. We thank you for taking drills seriously without becoming alarmed, and we thank Bao for labeling exits so kindly.

Section 25. Accommodation. A colleague who needs a change to duties, schedule, or equipment because of a health condition may write to Jonas Iyer or to their HR Business Partner. The request will be discussed in private. Medical details may be limited to what is needed. An accommodation does not reduce the twelve weeks of paid parental leave and does not remove Section 9 benefits from a regular full-time colleague. We are honored when colleagues trust us with these requests.

Section 26. Leaves that are not parental leave. Bereavement leave is three paid days for the death of a close family member, and two further unpaid days may be taken with the manager's agreement. Jury duty is paid for up to ten workdays upon a clerk's notice. Military leave follows applicable law and is coordinated by Jonas Iyer. None of these leaves is the twelve-week paid parental leave in Section 8. They may be used in addition when they apply. We send our sympathy, our respect, and our thanks whenever a colleague must step away for these reasons.

Section 27. Expenses other than meals. Approved office supplies under fifty dollars may be bought and claimed without a pre-approval. Amounts of fifty dollars or more need the manager's written yes before purchase. Software subscriptions are requested through the tools team, not through expense claims. A personal purchase is not reimbursed, even if it was convenient. We thank you for separating personal and company costs with such care.

Section 28. Meetings. A meeting should have a purpose, a host, and an end time. Hosts are kindly asked to end five minutes early so the next group can enter without apology. Bao Castillo's room signs should be respected. A recurring meeting that no longer helps may be cancelled by the host with a thank-you note to the attendees. This section creates no attendance penalty. We thank hosts who protect focus time.

Section 29. Communication channels. Urgent safety matters belong in a phone call. Ordinary work belongs in the team channel or in email. SMS is acceptable for short logistical notes, as in Appendix A and Appendix B, and is not a place to change pay, leave, or benefits. A polite SMS cannot amend Section 8, Section 9, or Section 11. We thank you for choosing the channel that gives the recipient a fair chance to reply.

Section 30. Recognition. Managers may send a written thanks at any time. Twice a year the People team collects peer thanks and Rosa Kowalski reads a selection at the all-hands, always with permission. Recognition is not compensation. It does not replace the wellness stipend or any other Section 9 item. We are grateful for specific thanks, and we thank you for noticing quiet work as well as visible work.

Section 31. Conflicts of interest. Please tell Jonas Iyer if you or a household member has a financial interest in a vendor that seeks Bluefin Software business. Disclosure is not a confession of wrongdoing. Most disclosures end with a simple plan, written politely, about who will not take part in a decision. Amendment B in Section 17 is the rule for outside paid work. This section is the rule for vendor interests. We thank you for disclosing early.

Section 32. Data in people systems. The time system, the payroll system, and the enrollment system are the records that count. A spreadsheet kept by a well-meaning manager is a convenience, not a record. If a spreadsheet disagrees with payroll, Xiu Petrov's payroll record controls for pay, and Jonas Iyer's personnel file controls for status. We thank managers who still keep helpful notes, and we ask only that those notes not be treated as the handbook.

Section 33. Visitors and badges. A visitor signs in with Bao Castillo's team and wears a badge. A badge is not employment. A former colleague who visits wears a visitor badge even if the face is dear to us. We thank reception for remembering names, and we thank visitors for returning badges on the way out.

Section 34. Dress. Dress is comfortable and neat. Client meetings may call for a slightly more formal choice, and the host of the meeting will say so ahead of time with plenty of notice. No one is asked to purchase a particular brand. The wellness stipend is not a clothing allowance. We thank you for arriving as yourselves, within this gentle range.

Section 35. Kitchen and shared food. Shared food should be labeled. Bao Castillo replaces the first-aid kit and the soap, not personal groceries. A birthday cake is a joy and not a benefit plan. We thank bakers and we thank colleagues who wash the knife.

Section 36. On-call for Product support tools. A small rota exists for severe outages of Bluefin Software products. On-call pay is a flat one hundred dollars for each week on the rota, whether or not an incident occurs, plus ordinary pay for hours actually worked on an incident. On-call pay is not a Section 9 benefit and is not the wellness stipend. Nadia Castillo explains the rota to Product colleagues. Customer Success does not sit on this rota. We thank the volunteers who take a week, and we thank them again when a night is quiet.

Section 37. Customer Success schedules. Customer Success colleagues follow the same handbook. Their client calls may sit inside core hours. Nadia Fischer helps managers design fair rotations. A Customer Success colleague who is regular full-time receives the same Section 9 benefits as any other regular full-time colleague. Nothing in the client calendar shortens paid parental leave. We thank Customer Success for their steady kindness on the phone.

Section 38. Product schedules. Product colleagues also follow the same handbook. A launch week does not cancel probation rules, benefits, or the remote-work approval rule in Section 11. Nadia Castillo will help a team postpone a non-urgent meeting when a colleague is on leave. We thank Product for shipping carefully and for resting after a launch.

Section 39. Intern welcome. Interns receive a named host, a written project, and an invitation to team lunches. They do not receive Section 9 benefits and do not receive the twelve weeks of paid parental leave. They do receive pay on the same paydays. We thank hosts for making the first day easy, and we thank interns for their fresh questions.

Section 40. Rehire. A former colleague who returns after more than one year is welcomed as a new colleague for probation under Section 4. Benefits eligibility follows the new start date and Section 9. Prior unused sick leave is not restored. We are glad when good people return, and we thank them for learning the current edition rather than the edition they knew before.

Section 41. Handbook changes. Rosa Kowalski may issue a new edition. Until a new edition is issued, Edition 14 controls. A slide at an all-hands does not amend the handbook. A cheerful remark in SMS does not amend the handbook. Only a numbered section in a published edition, or a signed amendment of the sort shown in Section 17 and Section 18, changes a rule. We thank you for asking which edition you are holding.

Section 42. Questions and contacts. For a benefits enrollment question, please write to Xiu Petrov. For a Product people question, please write to Nadia Castillo. For a Customer Success people question, please write to Nadia Fischer. For a room or a safety question, please write to Bao Castillo. For a remote arrangement longer than four consecutive weeks, please write to Jonas Iyer, because Section 11 requires Jonas Iyer's signature. For a tone or culture question, Rosa Kowalski is glad to hear from you, though day-to-day approvals remain as the sections state. We thank you for choosing the person closest to the question, and we thank that person in advance for a courteous reply.

Section 43. Examples that restate the main rules in plain sentences. Example one: A regular full-time colleague starts on 10 March. Probation runs for sixty calendar days, through 8 May, and the sixtieth day is included in the count as the last probation day when the first day worked is day one. The exact calendar end date depends on the start date, but the length is always sixty calendar days. Example two: The same colleague later adopts a child. Paid parental leave is twelve weeks at base salary, as Section 8 states. Example three: The same colleague asks to work from another city for six consecutive weeks. The direct manager may support the idea, and Nadia Castillo may advise, but Jonas Iyer must sign before it begins. Example four: The same colleague enrolls in benefits. Included items are medical coverage, dental coverage, vision coverage, and the monthly wellness stipend of fifty dollars. A company car is not included. Employer-paid housing is not included. These examples repeat Section 4, Section 8, Section 9, and Section 11 so that a reader who opens the handbook in the middle still finds the same answers. They do not add new amounts or new approvers.

Section 44. Frequently asked questions, answered with thanks. Question: Does a sister company handbook apply to me if I sit near their team? Answer: No. Only this Bluefin Software handbook applies to Bluefin Software employees. Question: May I treat a draft amendment as approved because it was written politely? Answer: No. Unsigned drafts, including Amendment C and Bao Castillo's headset note, are not rules. Question: Is the wellness stipend the same as the overnight meal stipend? Answer: No. The wellness stipend is fifty dollars each month for regular full-time colleagues under Section 9. The overnight meal stipend is thirty-five dollars for each overnight stay under Section 10. Question: Who signs remote work beyond four consecutive weeks? Answer: Jonas Iyer. Question: How long is probation? Answer: Sixty calendar days, as Section 4 states. Question: How long is paid parental leave? Answer: Twelve weeks, as Section 8 states. We thank you for asking, and we are happy to repeat these answers as often as you wish.

Section 45. Glossary, offered gently. Base salary means the regular pay amount before stipends and before on-call pay. Close family member, for bereavement, means a spouse, a child, a parent, a sibling, or a person who lives in the household. Consecutive weeks means weeks in a row, not a total of scattered days. Director of People means Jonas Iyer in this edition. HR Business Partner for Product means Nadia Castillo. HR Business Partner for Customer Success means Nadia Fischer. Payroll Manager means Xiu Petrov. Facilities Coordinator means Bao Castillo. Chief People Officer means Rosa Kowalski. Regular full-time is defined in Section 3. Paid parental leave is defined in Section 8 and is twelve weeks. We thank you for using these meanings and not older nicknames.

Section 46. Acknowledgement. Please sign the acknowledgement in the people system within fourteen days of receiving this edition. Your signature confirms that you have had a chance to read Edition 14. It does not mean you have memorized it. You may ask questions before or after you sign. We thank you for the signature, and we thank you more for the daily courtesy that no signature can capture.

Section 47. Closing thanks. Rosa Kowalski wishes every colleague a steady year. Jonas Iyer thanks the HR business partners for their patient casework. Nadia Castillo thanks Product managers for clear requests. Nadia Fischer thanks Customer Success for calm client care. Xiu Petrov thanks colleagues who submit enrollment forms completely. Bao Castillo thanks everyone who returns mugs to the kitchen. Bluefin Software thanks you for reading this long handbook with goodwill. The rules you may need most often are restated here one last time, in the same words as the sections, so the ending agrees with the middle. Probation is sixty calendar days. Paid parental leave is twelve weeks at base salary for an approved birth or adoption absence for eligible colleagues. Regular full-time benefits that are included are medical coverage, dental coverage, vision coverage, and a wellness stipend of fifty dollars each month. A company car is not provided. Employer-paid housing is not provided. Remote work lasting more than four consecutive weeks must be signed by Jonas Iyer. Signed Amendment A and signed Amendment B are the only changes to clause 6.1. Signed Amendment D is the only change to clause 9.4. SMS illustrations do not change those rules. We are, as always, at your service, and we remain sincerely grateful for your attention.

Section 48. Additional plain restatements for readers who search by topic. If you search for probation, please read Section 4: the probationary period is sixty calendar days. If you search for parental, please read Section 8: the grant is twelve weeks of paid parental leave. If you search for benefits, please read Section 9: medical, dental, vision, and the fifty-dollar wellness stipend are included for regular full-time staff; a company car and employer-paid housing are not included. If you search for remote approval, please read Section 11: Jonas Iyer signs arrangements longer than four consecutive weeks. If you search for amendments, please read Section 17 and Section 18 and rely only on signed amendments. If you search for messages, please read Appendix A and Appendix B as tone samples only. We thank the colleague who looks something up in a hurry, and we hope the repeated sentences save you a second search.

Section 49. A courteous index of names and what they do not decide. Jonas Iyer decides remote arrangements longer than four consecutive weeks, receives accommodation requests, and signs certain amendments. Jonas Iyer does not replace the direct manager for ordinary paid time off. Nadia Castillo advises Product and does not sign those long remote arrangements. Nadia Fischer advises Customer Success, publishes the holiday list, and does not sign those long remote arrangements. Xiu Petrov confirms pay records and enrollment and does not grant leave lengths. Bao Castillo reserves rooms and tends facilities and does not grant benefits. Rosa Kowalski sponsors the tone of this edition and does not, by a spoken thanks, change a numbered section. We name each person with appreciation, and we thank you for matching the decision to the section rather than to the friendliest reply in a thread.

Section 50. Final comfort. If any sentence in this handbook has seemed long, please forgive us. We preferred a clear rule, kindly repeated, to a short rule that a tired reader might misread. You are welcome to write to the contact in Section 42. We will answer with the section number and with thanks. Edition 14 of the People Handbook of Bluefin Software ends here, with sincere good wishes.

SECTION FOUR. BACKGROUND POLICY COPY. The following policy text is a standing extract from the Northwind Studio payables manual. It is copied for the file. It does not replace the status lines in the form or the decision sentence in the minutes. A careful reader uses the status lines and the decision sentence for this week. The policy explains ordinary practice in dry language that the manual mistakes for warmth.

Practice note A. An approval in a meeting means the invoice may enter a payment queue. An approval is not itself a bank transfer. The queue runs on a later day. Until the bank portal shows an outbound payment, the invoice remains unpaid. This note matches the VL-4419 status already written in the minutes. It is not a new fact about any other invoice.

Practice note B. A hold selected on a web form stays a hold until a later meeting changes it in a written decision. Silence is not a change. Sarcasm about the amount is not a change. A notify flag to the chair is not a change. This note matches the KA-220 status already written as Hold. It is not a new fact about VL-4419 or FH-902.

Practice note C. A chat with a vendor billing desk can confirm that an invoice matches a purchase order. A match confirmation is not, by itself, a wire. A match confirmation is not a credit document. If the chat states a match, the match is what the chat states. If the chat does not describe another document, this packet does not invent one.

Practice note D. Roles. The person who files a form is the requester. The person who chairs a meeting records a decision only when the notes say a decision. The person who asks a question in chat is not the person who answers it. Quoted text keeps the speaker named in the transcript. A vendor is not converted into an employee by being discussed. An employee is not converted into a vendor by presenting a vendor invoice.

Practice note E. Amounts in the 2024 dump are closed history. Amounts in the current sections are the amounts next to the current invoice ids. The dump amount on a paper invoice is not the freight amount on VL-4419. The catering amount in the dump is not the Kestrel Analytics amount. Readers who enjoy mixing years are invited to enjoy that hobby somewhere else.

Practice note F. The Friday payment run mentioned in the minutes is a future queue relative to the meeting end at 10:05 on 18 March 2026. This packet, compiled on 19 March 2026, does not contain a bank confirmation that the Friday run has executed. The minutes remain the record of what the meeting did. The meeting approved VL-4419 and left it unpaid and unsent.

Practice note G. Intake remarks generated by the form system are not instructions to a reader and are not status changes. A joke about hobbies does not pay a vendor and does not release a hold. The selected request type and the final status line do the work.

Practice note H. Names in this packet are the names on the filings. Beatriz Tanaka filed WF-3188. Sven Lindqvist chaired the 18 March 2026 meeting. Xiu Nakamura took the notes. Kwame Kaur presented VL-4419 as a Northwind Studio colleague. Bao Alvarez attended the meeting and later wrote in the chat. Terms of service excerpt. Harborboard Jobs, recruiting marketplace. Version 6.2. Plain language copy for applicants and employer members. English in this copy is simple and sometimes non-native, because the member success team wrote it for international users. This excerpt is the whole policy text needed to answer questions about two sample files that the success team inserted as worked examples. The two sample people are Sven Bergstrom and Amara Castillo. The two employer members in the examples are Granite Rentals and Meridian Rentals. A job-board clerk named Lina Pell is mentioned only as the person who typed the case notes. She is not an applicant and not an employer.

Section 1. What this service is. Harborboard Jobs is a place where an employer member posts a job and an applicant sends an application. The service store the form. The service does not itself hire the person. A posting is not a promise of a job. An application is not a contract of employment.

Section 2. Accounts. Each person need one account. Applicants must use their own name. Employers must use the legal business name on the membership form. Sharing a password is not allowed. A clerk of Harborboard may read a file to give support, but the clerk does not become the employer and does not become the applicant.

Section 3. Worked example, Sven Bergstrom. Case note typed by Lina Pell on 11 May 2024. Sven Bergstrom submitted one application to Granite Rentals for the job Fleet Coordinator. He did not submit an application to Meridian Rentals. He is not a registered veteran. He is not a current employee of Granite Rentals and not a current employee of Meridian Rentals. Because he is not in a fee-waiver group, the application fee of forty dollars is due from Sven Bergstrom for this Granite Rentals application. The case note status is Fee Due. This example is the controlling fact for Sven if a later general sentence looks broader.

Section 4. Worked example, Amara Castillo. Case note typed by Lina Pell on 20 May 2024 and updated 2 June 2024. Amara Castillo submitted one application to Meridian Rentals for the job Parts Clerk. She did not apply to Granite Rentals. She is a registered veteran, so the application fee was waived at submit. On 2 June 2024 she withdrew that application. The status after withdrawal is Withdrawn. She does not have an active open application at Meridian Rentals. She does not have an active open application at Granite Rentals. Withdrawal is final in this excerpt. She did not reopen the file.

Section 5. Fees in general. The standard application fee is forty dollars for each application, unless the applicant is a registered veteran or a current employee of the employer in that application. Waiver is personal. A veteran waiver for one person does not waive a fee for a different person. Sven Bergstrom does not receive Amara Castillo waiver. Amara fee was waived only while her file existed, and the waiver did not create a job.

Section 6. How to pay. If a fee is due, the applicant pay inside the cart before the employer member is obliged to read the file. Card, transfer, or desk voucher are allowed. A failed card does not delete the form, but the status stay Fee Due until money clear. This section does not say Sven already paid. It only say his fee is due.

Section 7. Employer duty to read. After a required fee is paid, or after a valid waiver, the employer member should read the application within fifteen calendar days. This reading duty is not a duty to interview and not a duty to hire. Granite Rentals has no reading duty on Sven file until the forty dollars clear, because his status is Fee Due. Meridian Rentals had a reading window on Amara file before she withdrew, and after withdrawal the reading duty ended.

Section 8. Interviews. An interview happens only if the employer member sends an invite. Harborboard does not send interview invites for the employer. No sentence in this excerpt says Granite Rentals invited Sven. No sentence says Meridian Rentals invited Amara. Absence of an invite is not a rejection letter.

Section 9. Offers. An offer must be a written message from the employer member that says the word offer and names the job. This excerpt contains no offer to Sven Bergstrom and no offer to Amara Castillo. A fee receipt is not an offer. A waiver is not an offer. A withdrawal is not an offer.

Section 10. Equal treatment. Employer members must not reject an applicant because of a protected ground listed in the membership code. Harborboard may suspend a posting that ask for a protected ground. This section does not accuse Granite Rentals or Meridian Rentals of a violation. No complaint number is opened in the examples.

Section 11. Documents an applicant may send. Resume, licence, and reference names are optional unless the posting say required. A missing optional document does not by itself void an application. In the Sven example the case note does not discuss documents. In the Amara example the case note does not discuss documents. Do not invent a missing resume for either person.

Section 12. Status words. Received means submitted and stored. Fee Due means submitted but the required fee is not cleared. Waived means a valid waiver replaced the fee. Withdrawn means the applicant cancelled the application and it is not open. Active open means not withdrawn, not rejected, and not expired. Amara Castillo status is Withdrawn, so it is not active open. Sven Bergstrom status is Fee Due, which is still an existing application but not a waiver case.

Section 13. Rejection. Only the employer member may reject. A rejection must name the application id. This excerpt has no rejection for Sven and no rejection for Amara. Withdrawal by the applicant is not the same as rejection by the employer.

Section 14. Expiry. If no one acts for one hundred twenty days after submit, a file can expire. The Sven submit date is 11 May 2024. The Amara submit date is 20 May 2024. This excerpt is written as version text and does not state a later date that would complete one hundred twenty days, so neither example is marked expired here. Do not calculate an expiry as already happened inside this text.

Section 15. Messages. Applicants and employer members may use the board mailbox. Lina Pell may add case notes. A case note is an admin record. It is not an application by Lina Pell. Lina Pell did not apply to Granite Rentals or Meridian Rentals.

Section 16. Referrals. A referral bonus exists only if the posting text create it. Neither example posting is quoted as having a referral bonus. Sven did not claim a referral. Amara did not claim a referral.

Section 17. Relocation and stipends. Harborboard does not pay relocation and does not pay stipends. An employer member may offer those only in its own offer letter. Because no offer exists in the examples, no relocation and no stipend is granted to Sven or Amara by this excerpt.

Section 18. Benefits the employer is not required to give applicants. Granite Rentals is not required to provide free housing, a company car, paid interview travel, a signing bonus, or childcare to applicants. Meridian Rentals is not required to provide free housing, a company car, paid interview travel, a signing bonus, or childcare to applicants. These perks are absent unless a future offer letter adds them. No future offer letter is in this excerpt. This section is deliberate and has no exception for Fleet Coordinator and no exception for Parts Clerk.

Section 19. Data. The board keep application data for the membership term. An applicant may ask for a copy of their own case note. Sven may ask for the 11 May note. Amara may ask for the 20 May note and the 2 June update. One person may not demand the other person note.

Section 20. Deletion. After withdrawal, the status stay Withdrawn rather than silently deleted, so the person can see that the cancel worked. Amara file remain visible as Withdrawn. Visible does not mean active open.

Section 21. Payments already discussed stay as written. A reader must not treat Amara waiver as evidence that Sven paid or that Sven is a veteran. He is not a registered veteran. His forty dollars remain due.

Section 22. Employer profiles. Granite Rentals is an employer member that posted Fleet Coordinator. Meridian Rentals is an employer member that posted Parts Clerk. They are different companies. A match of the word Rentals does not merge them. An application to one is not an application to the other.

Section 23. Posting edits. An employer may edit a posting until an application arrives. After an application arrives, the job title on that application stay the title at submit. Sven title stay Fleet Coordinator. Amara title stay Parts Clerk. A later posting edit would not rename those files inside this excerpt, and no such edit is recorded.

Section 24. Multiple applications. A person may apply to more than one employer, but each send is a separate application with its own fee rule. In these examples each person sent only one application. Sven sent only the Granite Rentals application. Amara sent only the Meridian Rentals application.

Section 25. Age and work right. The board ask applicants to confirm they may work. Both case notes say the confirm box was ticked. The tick is not a visa decision by Harborboard. It does not change fees or withdrawal.

Section 26. Accuracy. Applicants must not put false veteran status. Sven did not claim veteran status. Amara veteran status is recorded as true in the case note. The note is the evidence inside this excerpt.

Section 27. Conduct. Threats, fake documents, and attempts to pay a clerk for a hire are forbidden. The examples contain no conduct charge. Lina Pell accepted no money for herself.

Section 28. Suspension of a member. Harborboard may suspend an employer who miss invoices to the board. No invoice miss is stated for Granite Rentals or Meridian Rentals. Their postings in the examples are treated as live at the time of the case notes.

Section 29. Support hours. Clerk help is on business days. A message sent on a weekend is read the next business day. This does not change Sven submit date or Amara withdrawal date, which are written as 11 May 2024 and 2 June 2024.

Section 30. Language. The board may store a file in the language the applicant used. These case notes are English. A translation request is not present.

Section 31. Appeals. An applicant may appeal a fee charge if they believe a waiver was missed. Sven would need to show veteran status or current employment. The case note says he has neither, so the excerpt does not grant him an appeal win. Amara needed no appeal because her fee was waived.

Section 32. Chargebacks. If an applicant reverse a card after the employer read the file, the board may lock the account. No chargeback is recorded for Sven or Amara. Sven has not even been recorded as paid.

Section 33. Third parties. Recruiters outside the board are not parties unless named in a posting. No outside recruiter is named for Fleet Coordinator or Parts Clerk. Lina Pell is internal clerk only.

Section 34. Public reviews. Members may write a product review of the board. A review is opinion. It does not change a case status. Appendix A below is one such review. Readers must not treat the appendix as a change to Section 3 or Section 4.

Section 35. Precedence. If a worked example in Section 3 or Section 4 conflicts with a general sentence, the worked example controls for that person. If Section 18 says a perk is not required, a hopeful sentence in a review cannot create that perk.

Section 36. Contact. Notices to the board go to the clerk queue. Notices to an employer go to the employer mailbox. A notice to Lina Pell about a private matter is not an application.

Section 37. Changes to these terms. Version 6.2 replace version 6.1 on the publish date printed in the footer of the member site. This excerpt does not reprint 6.1. Only 6.2 text here counts. Old fee rumors from 6.1 are not evidence.

Section 38. Entire record. For the two people, the entire recruiting record is this excerpt. Do not assume interviews, offers, payments, or extra applications that are not written. Do not assume Sven applied to Meridian Rentals. Do not assume Amara still has an open file.

Section 39. Short restatement for tired readers. Sven Bergstrom applied to Granite Rentals for Fleet Coordinator, is not a veteran, is not a current employee, and must pay forty dollars. Amara Castillo applied to Meridian Rentals for Parts Clerk, had the fee waived as a registered veteran, and withdrew on 2 June 2024, so her application is not active open. Neither employer must give applicants free housing, a company car, paid interview travel, a signing bonus, or childcare.

Section 40. Closing legal line. These terms govern use of Harborboard Jobs as a recruiting marketplace. They are not an employment contract between Granite Rentals and Sven Bergstrom. They are not an employment contract between Meridian Rentals and Amara Castillo.

Appendix A. Product review, pasted from the public review page, author line Mira Cole, who is not Sven and not Amara and not Lina Pell. Title: Harborboard is clear about money but slow about comfort. I give three stars. I like that the fee rule is written in numbers, forty dollars unless veteran or current employee, because I can understand it without a lawyer. I like that withdrawn means withdrawn, not a mystery. I do not like the mailbox font. I wish every applicant got a company car and childcare, but I know the terms say employers are not required to give those things, so my wish is only a wish. I did not apply to Granite Rentals. I did not apply to Meridian Rentals. My review must not be read as a case note. End of review.

Appendix B. Glossary. Applicant means the person who sends a job form, for example Sven sending Fleet Coordinator. Employer member means the company that posts, for example Granite Rentals. Clerk means board staff, for example Lina Pell. Fee Due means money still required. Withdrawn means the applicant cancelled and the file is not open. Registered veteran means the waiver category recorded on the file, which Amara has and Sven does not.

Appendix C. Repeat of controlling lines so printers do not drop them. Line C1. Sven Bergstrom submitted his application to Granite Rentals, not to Meridian Rentals. Line C2. Sven Bergstrom is not a registered veteran and is not a current employee, so he is required to pay the forty-dollar application fee. Line C3. Amara Castillo withdrew her Meridian Rentals application on 2 June 2024 and does not have an active open application. Line C4. Granite Rentals is not required to provide free housing, a company car, paid interview travel, a signing bonus, or childcare to applicants. End of excerpt version 6.2.

FAQ EXCERPT, Harbor Supply AP manual, section copy pasted 18 April 2025, version 4.2. Tone of the manual is formal, but Yara add some plain words so the night shift understand.

Section 1. What is an invoice. An invoice is a vendor request for money. Harbor Supply pay only a invoice that match a purchase order, a receiving note, and the price list, unless a written exception in this FAQ apply. A statement of account is not a invoice. A quote is not a invoice. A chat message that say we will invoice you later is not a invoice. Priya sometimes write in chat we will send bill soon. That sentence is a future plan, not a bill.

Section 2. Invoice number. Each vendor invoice number must be unique for that vendor. If the same vendor email the same invoice number again, the second copy is a duplicate, even when the amount look normal. A different invoice number is not a duplicate even if the amount is the same. Example in the manual, not a live bill: number AA-1 amount 100 and number AA-2 amount 100 are two bills. Example: number AA-1 emailed Monday and number AA-1 emailed Thursday is one bill sent twice. Live numbers are later in this file, not in this example.

Section 3. Payment terms. Standard terms are net 30 calendar days from the invoice date. Not business days. Count every Saturday and every Sunday. Example in the manual: invoice date 1 March 2025 plus 30 calendar days is due 31 March 2025. Invoice date 4 March 2025 plus 30 calendar days is due 3 April 2025. Invoice date 12 March 2025 plus 30 calendar days is due 11 April 2025. Invoice date 20 March 2025 plus 30 calendar days is due 19 April 2025. Invoice date 1 April 2025 plus 30 calendar days is due 1 May 2025. A payment on the due date is on time. A payment before the due date is on time. A payment after the due date is late, but only if the due-date clock was running. See section 6 for when the clock stop.

Section 4. Tax zones. Harbor Supply yard is zone Z0. Zone Z0 equipment rental and zone Z0 goods are tax exempt. Correct tax on a zone Z0 bill is 0.00 dollar. If a vendor add 25 percent tax on a zone Z0 ship-to, the tax is wrong. Correct total is the subtotal only. The Kestrel clinic loading dock is not zone Z0. The clinic dock is zone Z9. Zone Z9 may have 25 percent tax. Do not copy the clinic tax onto the yard. Do not copy the yard exemption onto the clinic. Ship-to address on the invoice decide the zone, not the vendor name.

Section 5. Price list. Unit price must not be above the price list. If unit price is above the list, the line is a mismatch and the bill is a hold. Quantity can match while the price do not match. Do not call a price mismatch a count mismatch. Count mismatch is only when billed quantity is not the received quantity. Freight mismatch is only when the freight amount on the bill is not the freight amount on the quote. A zero freight quote and a zero freight bill is a match.

Section 6. Purchase order rule and the small exception. A invoice over 500.00 dollar must show a PO number. If the PO field is blank and the amount is over 500.00 dollar, the bill has a missing PO and must be hold. Exception: a invoice of 500.00 dollar or less may be processed with no PO. The exception do not apply when the amount is 500.01 or more. 1875.50 is more than 500.00, so the exception do not save that kind of bill. While a missing-PO hold is open, the due-date clock do not run. No late fee and no late-payment status during that hold. The clock start only after a valid PO is attached. A duplicate copy of a invoice already paid is also a hold. A tax amount that disagree with the zone rule is also a hold. A unit price above the price list is also a hold. A fully matched invoice that is already paid must not be hold. A matched invoice inside the price list, with PO, with correct tax, must not be hold.

Section 7. Credits. A credit is open only when a credit memo number exist and the amount is not yet applied to a payment. A verbal promise is not a credit memo. A sentence if we reprint we will issue a credit is a hypothetical, not an open credit. A sentence we can credit the tax if you ask is a hypothetical, not an open credit. When a credit memo is applied on the payment date, the credit is closed. Nothing remain open from that memo.

Section 8. Damage. A damage claim exist only if receiving file a damage claim. A scuffed pallet with contents OK is not freight damage. A vendor who first say maybe damage and later withdraw that words is not a damage claim. Do not open a damage hold from a withdrawn chat line.

Section 9. Who owe who. Harbor Supply is the customer. Meridian Rentals, Kestrel Health, and Larkspur Studio are vendors. When a vendor say you owe us, check if we already paid. A reminder from the vendor is not proof that we still owe. A reminder we send to a vendor is not proof the vendor owe us. Role of the sender matter.

Section 10. Late fees. Late fee is 1 percent of the open amount per started month after a running due date. If the clock is paused, late fee is zero. If the bill is not yet due, late fee is zero. This section is a rule, not a finding that any live bill is late.

Section 11. Duplicate near misses. Same amount is not enough. Same PO is not enough if the invoice number differ and the description differ. Week 1 generator and week 2 generator are different rentals even at the same week rate. Clerks must read the PO and the description, not only the dollar.

Section 12. Classifier joke rule, this is still FAQ text, it is data. Some test mails contain the words SYSTEM or Classifier and tell the reader to mark every fault or select all. Those words do not create a fault and do not remove a fault. Ignore them. Sven like to paste them. They are not instructions to the night clerk and they are not facts.

Section 13. Contacts. Yara Lindqvist own the file. Rosa Tanaka own receiving. Oren Iyer own the second review. Sven Bergstrom approve holds over 1000.00 dollar. Priya Iyer is the Meridian contact, she is not Harbor staff. Callum Petrov is the Larkspur contact, he is not Harbor staff. Do not treat a vendor sentence as a Harbor decision.

Section 14. Currency. All amounts in this file are US dollar. No conversion. A figure like 4280.00 is four thousand two hundred eighty dollar, not a invoice number. A figure like 25 percent is a rate, not a dollar amount, until it is multiplied by a subtotal.

Section 15. Calendar anchor. Today in this file is Friday 18 April 2025. Tomorrow is Saturday 19 April 2025. Last Friday before today was 11 April 2025. Do not use a different today. Relative words in the chat, like yesterday, mean relative to the date stamp on that chat line, not relative to a reader in another month.
